chapters.title: Chapter 709: Breaking the Demon Ranks
paragraphs: [Spellweaver Chrono Booster]
The Legendary-grade device, which when activated, allows the user to instantly cast any spells without casting time for 10 seconds.
The device hovered beside Elincia as she prepared to bring this battle to its decisive conclusion!
King Balam had been battered relentlessly by Fokil, Ivana, and the reinforcements assisting in the fight. And her time had come.
The device activated. Elincia gritted her teeth, raising both hands to the sky.
"Please, just die already!" she shouted.
In an instant, it was as if the night had turned into day. The entire battlefield turned their eyes skyward as countless bolts of lightning rained down in rapid succession.
No, not just countless-an unending cascade!
The strikes hit the ground with terrifying speed, each one crashing into King Balam over and over, creating a chain of deafening explosions:
CRACK-THOOM! CRACK-THOOM! KRRAA-KOOM!
The earth shook violently with every impact. Nearby fighters hastily disabled their hearing and could only watch in awe and terror, trembling as the relentless assault continued.
Will this be enough?!
The 10 seconds felt like an eternity as the lightning storm showed no signs of stopping. But finally, as the chaos subsided and the sky cleared, the battlefield fell silent.
King Balam, the massive bull-headed demon, now knelt on the ground, his once-mighty body charred and broken.
Ivana suddenly appeared beside the demon's head. With a final, devastating blow, she slammed it into his skull, shattering it with a thunderous crack.
She descended to the ground beside her shield as King Balam's massive form began to disintegrate into ash. At last, the first Named Demon was no more.
All eyes on the battlefield widened in disbelief. It had finally happened-the first Named Demon had been defeated!

King Balam's fall was a monumental victory, a turning point in the war. Cheers of triumph erupted across the battlefield as the forces, reinvigorated by their success, scattered and surged toward the remaining Named Demons.
Victory chants echoed through the air as the warriors regained their morale. "We can win this!"
Elincia, still riding the high of her success, quickly moved toward Duke Alloces, while Ivana and Fokil rushed toward Countess Murmur.

By the time Elincia joined the battle against Duke Alloces, it was clear that the demon was already in dire straits. Goldrich had inflicted massive damage, leaving the demon vulnerable. When Elincia joined forces with additional mages, they unleashed a relentless torrent of magical attack upon the Duke.
Duke Alloces staggered, unable to maneuver or counterattack as Optimus and Skywarden hammered him with relentless strikes, forcing him into submission.
"Keep up the pressure! Focus! Hit him with everything we've got!" came the rallying cries as the assault intensified.
Goldrich and Elincia closed in, their magic becoming fiercer and more devastating with each strike.
The once-mighty Duke Alloces, his dual swords gleaming in the dim light, now stood frozen, unable to withstand the unyielding barrage.
And then, it was over. The battlefield erupted in a blinding flash as Alloces's form collapsed to the ground. His body shimmered briefly before crumbling to ash, carried away by the wind.
Another Named Demon had fallen!
"We've done it! We've defeated the named demon!"
This wasn't just another battle-it was a surge of hope, a sign that the tide of war was shifting in their favor. Two down, and the remaining demons were now within reach of the same fate.

On the other side of the battlefield, Countess Murmur was also under relentless assault. Fokil's flying hammer and Ivana's shield strikes continued to pound her in midair, each blow disrupting her movements and leaving her increasingly vulnerable.
Booba maintained his hit-and-run tactics, striking swiftly from the back of his wyvern before retreating, while Paul and Marlene worked together to keep the Countess completely restrained.
Their coordination ensured that the demoness had little opportunity to retaliate or escape.
The fight on this front was quickly becoming more controlled, the chaos giving way to precision as the team tightened their grip.

A well-aimed hammer strike from Fokil sent Countess Murmur spiraling out of the sky, her wings too damaged to sustain her flight. Booba delivered a crushing blow that sent her plummeting to the ground.

As soon as she hit the earth, the demoness was overwhelmed. A barrage of attacks from every direction rained down on her, leaving her no room to defend herself. Blow after blow landed with brutal precision, breaking her defenses entirely.
The fight ended swiftly.
Another victory!
Cheers erupted once more, echoing across the battlefield as the forces celebrated the defeat of yet another Named Demon.

"Tora!" Max exclaimed, her face lighting up with excitement as she watched from a distance. The victories against the three Named Demons had reinvigorated her enthusiasm. "Tora, this is incredible progress-three Named Demons have been defeated!"
"Yes, Max," Tora replied, nodding with a faint smile. "Now, we're just waiting for SpeedGang's domain to dissipate and see the outcome of their fight."
All eyes turned to the same point on the battlefield as SpeedGang's domain began to fade, bursting like a soap bubble.
There they stood-SpeedGang, Charmelyn, and Kingsley-victorious against Marquis Orias! Their triumph was unmistakable, and cheers erupted from the surrounding forces.
This moment was nothing short of extraordinary!
The battlefield shifted decisively in their favor as the morale surged. With four Named Demons down, everyone rallied, scattering across the field to clean up the remaining demons.
Meanwhile, the top players quickly gathered their resources, regrouped, and sprinted toward the same destination-the heart of the main battle.

There, the ultimate villain, Duke Focalor, was under siege. Hundreds of skeleton warriors swarmed him, while massive chunks of ice and razor-sharp arrows hurtled through the air, pelting the demon with unrelenting precision.
Broken moved with incredible speed, landing blow after blow on Focalor, trying to force him
into a corner.
The time had come to combine their strength, to unleash their most devastating attacks.
They needed to end this battle swiftly and decisively-this was their moment to bring the war to its climactic conclusion!

chapters.title: Chapter 710: Radiant Swordmaster
paragraphs: Broken, Frostedge, Galactron and Zeno continued their relentless attacks in the same consistent pattern. The damage they dealt wasn't overwhelming enough to push Focalor into a dire situation, but it was steady, proving their strategy was working.

As more reinforcements arrived-particularly high-level players and NPCs fresh from defeating the other four Named Demons-their combined efforts began to significantly amplify the damage output against Focalor.

Even so, only ranged attackers dared to engage directly, maintaining their distance as they unleashed barrages of arrows, spells, and projectiles. Meanwhile, close-range fighters focused on clearing the battlefield of lingering demons to ensure Focalor remained isolated.

Broken was careful to ensure that both Alora and Ivana stayed out of close combat against Focalor. The demon's level and raw power were simply too high. Even Broken himself, bolstered by Gaia's healing skills and defensive support, found it incredibly difficult to hold his ground.
Now, a pressing question loomed: Is this the right time to summon the Golden Paragon?

Just as he managed to parry another one of Focalor's devastating attacks, two figures approached rapidly from opposite directions. In unison, they struck the demon with a spear and a greatsword, their combined force sending Focalor hurtling to the side.
The sheer impact of the clash also caused Broken to skid backward, struggling to maintain his footing after the forceful parry.
"Thanks, Broken, for holding him off this long!" one of the figures said.
The voice belonged to an elf woman with short white hair, clad in heavy armor with a base of white and dark silver. It was Iveth, the forest elf who had previously visited Broken in Slumdon Town.
Her companion, another elf wielding a greatsword, was a man equally clad in tank-like armor. The two exuded an aura of experience and strength, clearly prepared for this level of combat.
They moved seamlessly, engaging Focalor head-on, their builds and expertise allowing them to shoulder the burden Broken had carried so far.
This was it a crucial moment in the battle!
They needed to capitalize on this moment-to deal as much damage as possible and create an opening to bring Focalor down. There would be no greater opportunity than now.

Broken clenched his jaw. He could only sustain this skill for a maximum of five minutes, but with the growing number of high-level players converging on the area, their combined efforts and also the skill from the summon would amplify the damage output significantly. [Summon Golden Paragon (Conditional Active Skill) activated]
As the skill took effect, Focalor's attention snapped toward Broken. A mix of golden and dark auras swirled around him, wrapping his body in a chaotic, menacing energy.

"You piece of trash!" Focalor snarled, his teeth grinding as he deftly evaded attacks from Iveth and her companion. With a burst of speed, he hurtled straight toward Broken, an enormous energy ball spinning violently in his grasp.
The air crackled with power as Focalor's form closed the distance in an instant, aiming the devastating energy ball directly at Broken.

Broken raised his Gravestone Greatsword into a parry stance, his grip tightening. He knew the impact would be immense, and there was no guarantee he could withstand it. Yet, he stood firm, prepared to face it head-on.
The energy ball collided with his greatsword.
BOOOOOOOM!

An explosion tore through the battlefield, a massive shockwave rippling outward as debris scattered in all directions. But instead of shattering the target, the energy was reflected backward, its explosive force chasing after Focalor in a chain of detonations.
Everyone watching froze, stunned into silence. Broken had held his ground, withstanding Focalor's attack with the Gravestone Greatsword.
But that wasn't the most shocking part!
Emerging behind Broken, floating, was a figure that seemed to embody divinity itself.
It was enormous, nearly twice the size of a normal human. The figure's form was clad in jet- black heavy armor adorned with glowing golden accents that shimmered like divine light.

Its helmet completely obscured its face, but glowing blue energy emanated from within, pulsing through intricate golden carvings. A massive greatsword, blazing with golden brilliance, rested in its hands, and a pair of majestic, radiant wings stretched out from its back.
Everyone watching was struck with awe and disbelief. The battlefield seemed to pause as they took in the sight.
It was Broken's Golden Paragon.
The majestic figure floated effortlessly, its back to Gaia, facing the battlefield ahead with an imposing presence.
As Broken activated the Golden Paragon, a series of notifications appeared before him.
[You have activated the skill to summon the Golden Paragon.]
[You have received Stat Amplification bonus: Strength, Constitution, and Agility increased by 150% and Intelligence increased by 75%.]
[You have activated Divine Aura: Allies within a 20-meter radius gain 20% increased attack power and 15% increased movement speed.]
[The Golden Paragon has unlocked some unique skills to match your traits as the summoner.]
[You have access to a new skill Radiant Swordmaster (Offensive Active Skill)] [Executes a sweeping slash, releasing waves of radiant energy that devastate enemies.]
[Effect:]
[-600% Attack Power as Divine Light Damage in a cone AoE (35 meters long, 15 meters wide).
[- Inflicts Radiant Wound: Healing effects on enemies reduced by 50% for 10 seconds.]
[Cooldown: 10 seconds.]
[You have access to a new skill Celestial Bulwark (Defensive Active Skill)]
[Creates a radiant shield to protect allies, reducing damage and bolstering defenses.]
[Effect:]
[- Absorbs 40% incoming damage for 7 seconds.]
[- Allies gain 15% bonus Defense and Magic Resistance for 10 seconds.]
[Cooldown: 20 seconds.]
[You have access to a new skill Heaven's Judgment (Ultimate Active Skill)]
[Channels divine energy into a devastating explosion, obliterating enemies in range.]
[Effect:]
[-1000% Attack Power as Divine Light Damage in a 75-meter radius.]
[- Stuns enemies for 5 seconds.]
[- Removes all buffs from enemies.]
[Cooldown: Once per Summon.]
[You have access to a new skill Infernal Blade Mastery (Passive Skill)]
[Adds Divine Flames to attacks, causing continuous damage over time.]
[Effect:]
[- 75% additional Divine Light Damage over 5 seconds.]
[-Stacks up to 3 times.]

Broken immediately unlocked four new skills. He skimmed through their descriptions, appreciating their straightforward mechanics and practicality. The set included three active skills and one passive ability.
There was no hesitation on his part-he was more than capable of juggling multiple skills in
the heat of battle.

One skill was offensive, designed for dealing damage. Another was defensive, meant to shield allies. The passive skill enhanced close-range attacks, and the ultimate ability was a game- changer: an area-of-effect attack with powerful crowd control capabilities. Truly exceptional. His stats had been massively boosted. This sudden upgrade had transformed him in mere moments, and he knew he had to keep attacking relentlessly to make the most of the Golden Paragon's summon duration.

The Golden Paragon moved in perfect harmony with Broken, mirroring his parrying stance. The sight was nothing short of awe-inspiring. It left not only the defenders on the battlefield speechless but also caused the Named Demon before him to falter.
"You're nothing but trash that needs to be destroyed!" Focalor snarled.
"You've said that a dozen times now," Broken replied.
His grip on the greatsword tightened as he prepared for his next move.
[Radiant Swordmaster (Offensive Active Skill) activated.]
Broken unleashed his new power. The air around him seemed to hum and crackle as radiant
energy surged outward. Waves of brilliant light cleaved through the battlefield in a sweeping arc, hurtling straight toward Focalor with devastating precision.

The air crackled with power as Focalor's form closed the distance in an instant, aiming the devastating energy ball directly at Broken.
Broken raised his Gravestone Greatsword into a parry stance, his grip tightening.
He knew the impact would be immense, and there was no guarantee he could withstand it.
Yet, he stood firm, prepared to face it head-on.
The energy ball collided with his greatsword.
BOOOOOOOM!
An explosion tore through the battlefield, a massive shockwave rippling outward as debris scattered in all directions.
But instead of shattering the target, the energy was reflected backward, its explosive force chasing after Focalor in a chain of detonations.
Everyone watching froze, stunned into silence.
Broken had held his ground, withstanding Focalor's attack with the Gravestone Greatsword.
But that wasn't the most shocking part!
Emerging behind Broken, floating, was a figure that seemed to embody divinity itself.
It was enormous, nearly twice the size of a normal human.
The figure's form was clad in jet- black heavy armor adorned with glowing golden accents that shimmered like divine light.
Its helmet completely obscured its face, but glowing blue energy emanated from within, pulsing through intricate golden carvings.
A massive greatsword, blazing with golden brilliance, rested in its hands, and a pair of majestic, radiant wings stretched out from its back.
Everyone watching was struck with awe and disbelief.
The battlefield seemed to pause as they took in the sight.
It was Broken's Golden Paragon.
The majestic figure floated effortlessly, its back to Gaia, facing the battlefield ahead with an imposing presence.
As Broken activated the Golden Paragon, a series of notifications appeared before him.
[You have activated the skill to summon the Golden Paragon.]
[You have received Stat Amplification bonus: Strength, Constitution, and Agility increased by 150% and Intelligence increased by 75%.]
[You have activated Divine Aura: Allies within a 20-meter radius gain 20% increased attack power and 15% increased movement speed.]
[The Golden Paragon has unlocked some unique skills to match your traits as the summoner.]
[You have access to a new skill Radiant Swordmaster (Offensive Active Skill)] [Executes a sweeping slash, releasing waves of radiant energy that devastate enemies.]
[Effect:]
[-600% Attack Power as Divine Light Damage in a cone AoE (35 meters long, 15 meters wide).
[- Inflicts Radiant Wound: Healing effects on enemies reduced by 50% for 10 seconds.]
[Cooldown: 10 seconds.]
[You have access to a new skill Celestial Bulwark (Defensive Active Skill)]
[Creates a radiant shield to protect allies, reducing damage and bolstering defenses.]
[Effect:]
[- Absorbs 40% incoming damage for 7 seconds.]
[- Allies gain 15% bonus Defense and Magic Resistance for 10 seconds.]
[Cooldown: 20 seconds.]
[You have access to a new skill Heaven's Judgment (Ultimate Active Skill)]
[Channels divine energy into a devastating explosion, obliterating enemies in range.]
[Effect:]
[-1000% Attack Power as Divine Light Damage in a 75-meter radius.]
[- Stuns enemies for 5 seconds.]
[- Removes all buffs from enemies.]
[Cooldown: Once per Summon.]
[You have access to a new skill Infernal Blade Mastery (Passive Skill)]
[Adds Divine Flames to attacks, causing continuous damage over time.]
[Effect:]
[- 75% additional Divine Light Damage over 5 seconds.]
[-Stacks up to 3 times.]
Broken immediately unlocked four new skills.
He skimmed through their descriptions, appreciating their straightforward mechanics and practicality.
The set included three active skills and one passive ability.
There was no hesitation on his part-he was more than capable of juggling multiple skills in
the heat of battle.
One skill was offensive, designed for dealing damage.
Another was defensive, meant to shield allies.
The passive skill enhanced close-range attacks, and the ultimate ability was a game- changer: an area-of-effect attack with powerful crowd control capabilities.
Truly exceptional.
His stats had been massively boosted.
This sudden upgrade had transformed him in mere moments, and he knew he had to keep attacking relentlessly to make the most of the Golden Paragon's summon duration.
The Golden Paragon moved in perfect harmony with Broken, mirroring his parrying stance.
The sight was nothing short of awe-inspiring.
It left not only the defenders on the battlefield speechless but also caused the Named Demon before him to falter.
"You're nothing but trash that needs to be destroyed!" Focalor snarled.
"You've said that a dozen times now," Broken replied.
His grip on the greatsword tightened as he prepared for his next move.
[Radiant Swordmaster (Offensive Active Skill) activated.]
Broken unleashed his new power.
The air around him seemed to hum and crackle as radiant
energy surged outward.
Waves of brilliant light cleaved through the battlefield in a sweeping arc, hurtling straight toward Focalor with devastating precision.

chapters.title: Chapter 711: Celestial Bulwark
paragraphs: The Golden Paragon was truly extraordinary!

Broken quickly amplified not only his own attacks but also boosted the impact of every ally around him, making their strikes land with devastating force. His confidence surged as he advanced toward Focalor. This time, he wielded his Wavebreaker Spear, activating his Water Domain to gain even more control over the battlefield.

With the ability to stay airborne, Broken executed a relentless flurry of spinning strikes and sweeping attacks, parrying every attempt the demon made to retaliate. The Golden Paragon's buffs elevated the attack power of everyone in his vicinity, creating a surge of momentum that was impossible to ignore.
The spectacle turned heads across the battlefield. Whispers spread rapidly as onlookers tried to make sense of what they were witnessing.
"Is that... a skill similar to the one King Alorik used?"
"Yes! That's the Golden Paragon-I'm certain of it!"
"What even is that?"
"It's a legendary skill, exclusive to the heir of the Dissidia Kingdom."
"No way! Does that mean Broken is the heir to Dissidia? How is that possible? I thought the Crown Princess was Alora!"
"But it's clear this skill's full potential only shines when used alongside a strong team, right?"
"Still, why did King Alorik lose despite wielding the same power?"
"No one said Broken is guaranteed to win either. I just hope this fight ends soon-I can't take the suspense!"
[Celestial Bulwark (Defensive Active Skill) activated.]

With the activation of this defensive skill, Iveth and the forest elves finally gained the stability they needed to withstand Focalor's relentless attacks. The shield provided just enough protection for close-range players to strike while allowing others to retreat and regroup when necessary.
"You worthless scum!" Focalor snarled, frustration mounting as he found himself besieged by attacks from every direction.
Pinned to one spot, he had no room to maneuver.
Broken capitalized on the chaos, pressing his assault. Thanks to two close-range fighters stepping in to cover his role as a tank, he now had more freedom to focus entirely on his offensive strikes.
One minute. Even a single minute felt like an eternity as they continued their brutal, unrelenting barrage.
"Keep attacking! We can defeat the Named Demon!"
Shouts of encouragement echoed across the battlefield, fueling the growing optimism. The tide of the battle was shifting, and victory felt within reach.

As time passed, more close-range fighters closed in, adding to the intensity. Optimus darted forward, striking Focalor from the side with a series of sharp kicks and punches before retreating just as quickly. Charmelyn multiplied herself into countless clones, each delivering an attack in rapid succession.

Focalor was overwhelmed. The barrage was too much, and he could no longer fend off the relentless waves of assaults. The buffs from Golden Paragon were proving invaluable, shielding the team and empowering their strikes.

Then, the battlefield shifted again. Alora and Ivana joined the fray. Spotting Ivana, Focalor unleashed a massive energy ball aimed directly at her. The attack sent her hurtling backward, but she recovered swiftly.
At that moment, Kingsley's bear-form charged into the fray, trampling the demon under its enormous weight. The momentum was undeniable. Focalor was faltering.
[Heaven's Judgment (Ultimate Active Skill) activated.]

Broken unleashed the Golden Paragon's ultimate skill, a move that was vital to stun the demon and focus all their damage on a single target. The Golden Paragon avatar raised its greatsword high into the air, and a brilliant golden light erupted from the blade. It grew rapidly, transforming into a massive weapon.

With one colossal swing, the greatsword came crashing down, creating a devastating explosion that shattered everything in its path. Focalor was thrown to the ground, reeling under the relentless onslaught.
This was the moment.
Broken swiftly switched weapons, summoning his Wavebreaker Spear and the Golden Bow of Artemis.
[Sniper's Focus (Active Skill) Lv. 5 activated.]
The sky seemed to split open, and from its depths descended a duplicate of the Wavebreaker Spear, encased in a blinding golden glow. The spectacle was a dazzling display of raw power.
Two seconds.
And the spear shot downward like a blazing comet, targeting Focalor, who was already besieged by countless attacks. Broken prepared to summon his Bedrock Breaker for the next strike.
But then...
Something no one anticipated happened.
Focalor caught the original spear!
It was so swift, so unexpected, that it left the battlefield in stunned silence. In a single motion, the demon redirected the spear with terrifying precision. And then...

The spear pierced Iveth's chest. The elf woman staggered, her expression frozen in shock, as the massive spear fell from the sky, striking with earth-shattering force. Explosive waves of waters and countless water spears rained down mercilessly upon the battlefield, carving destruction into the earth.
Yet in that fleeting, heart-stopping moment, there was one truth-only Broken could see.
[You have killed Iveth Lv. 247.]
Broken froze, his mind reeling as the message appeared before him.
No way. This can't be happening!
He had explicitly set his target to Focalor. There was no room for error-only demons were supposed to be affected by his attacks.
That was a fundamental rule in Immortal Legacy, a safeguard hardwired into the system. Yet, here it was, glaring at him as if mocking his disbelief.
Frantically, he checked his settings again. Everything was correct. The target lock, the exclusion of allies-everything was as it should have been. But none of that changed what had just happened.

Before his eyes, Iveth's body lay pinned to the ground by the spear. As her form shattered into glimmering fragments, breaking apart with an eerie finality, the weight of what had happened settled over him.
"Iveth!"

A cry broke through the battlefield. Her companion, a forest elf, threw his spear aside and rushed toward her, desperation etched on his face. But he was too late. She was gone. "Focus on the battle, Elrin!" Zeno's voice rang out, but the elf man's grief left him utterly vulnerable.
In that instant, Focalor surged forward, slipping free from Optimus and Ivana's combined assault. He closed the distance to Elrin in a heartbeat, pressing a clawed hand to the elf's back.
Crimson energy pulsed from Focalor's palm, spreading like a tide across Elrin's body. The elf barely had time to scream before he erupted in a violent explosion.
"No!" Broken's voice tore from his throat.
"Regroup! Hold your positions!" Zeno's voice barked out again.
But the damage was done. The loss of two forest elves caused the frontline defense to collapse, their formation crumbling under the pressure.
Ivana was now in danger.
And he had to act fast.

chapters.title: Chapter 712: The Clock Strikes Zero
paragraphs: Ivana!

Broken dashed forward with everything he had. Focalor had just slaughtered two forest elves and now surged through the air, evading strikes from skeletal warriors. His hands glowed with twin orbs of crackling energy, each aimed directly at Ivana.
Ivana was in danger.
Focalor moved with terrifying speed, bearing down on her. But then, out of nowhere, a figure clad in heavy crimson armor appeared near them.

In an instant, a domain expanded outward from the armored figure, encapsulating everyone within its shimmering boundary-Broken, Ivana, Alora, and Frostedge were all caught inside. The figure, SpeedGang, struck his shield against the ground with a resonating clang, pointing at Focalor, who hovered above them.
"No one can use magic in this domain!" SpeedGang declared.
No magic? That would be disastrous. Focalor thrived on raw power based on his stats alone, making him even deadlier without magic to counter him.
Is this guy out of his mind? Broken cursed inwardly.
"Hah! It seems you've learned nothing," Focalor sneered.
Unfazed by SpeedGang's declaration, the Named Demon ascended higher into the air. With terrifying precision and raw, overwhelming power, he slammed into the domain's barrier.
In mere moments, the barrier shattered into countless fragments, breaking apart with a deafening crash.
SpeedGang froze in place, his figure flickering briefly before dissolving into pixels and vanishing into thin air. The domain that was supposed to turn the tide had been obliterated effortlessly.
Focalor's raw strength had rendered the strategy futile, leaving the battlefield exposed and vulnerable once more.
Damn it!
There was no one left to take the full tanker role, and Broken couldn't allow Ivana to step into such a vulnerable position.
"Ivana, retreat!" he shouted.

As Focalor's strike neared Ivana, Broken surged forward, intercepting it just in time. Massive ice swords materialized in the air, slamming repeatedly into Focalor, but the demon's magic shield absorbed the relentless onslaught.
Broken didn't let up. He launched a flurry of attacks, spinning his spear with precision and thrusting it forward in rapid strikes aimed at breaking through Focalor's defenses.
Suddenly, a colossal ice wall appeared behind Focalor, trapping the demon in a confined space. This was the opportunity Broken needed for a decisive blow. He moved in for a fatal strike.

But Focalor was faster. The demon slammed his hand forward, unleashing a powerful wave of energy that blasted out in all directions. The sheer force hurled Broken and everything near the demon backward, scattering debris and allies alike.
Broken gritted his teeth as he regained his footing.
Even with the buffs from the Golden Paragon, this demon was proving to be nearly impossible to defeat.
Broken summoned the Legendary Golem Blackthorn to the battlefield.
With a thunderous crash, the colossal golem materialized. Wielding an enormous greatsword, Blackthorn wasted no time and charged directly at Focalor, its heavy footfalls shaking the ground.

At the very least, Blackthorn's presence relieved some of the pressure from Broken, taking on the critical role of tanking the heavy damage. This gave him a brief window to recalibrate his strategy while continuing to coordinate his team.

The battle raged on for another grueling three minutes, and the tension only grew heavier. This fight was exhausting, both physically and mentally, as Focalor remained virtually unscathed despite their desperate efforts.
Everyone attacked with increasing desperation, aware of the stakes. Broken, too, pushed himself to the limit, knowing full well that the duration of Golden Paragon was ticking down.
He unleashed every skill at his disposal, aiming to deal as much damage as possible before his time ran out.
But it was becoming painfully clear-this Named Demon, levels over 400, was far tougher than any of them had anticipated.

Frostedge, Galactron, and Zeno didn't falter for a moment, their relentless barrage of attacks showing no signs of slowing. Yet, the battlefield's grim reality was undeniable. Despite their best efforts, they had yet to inflict any significant damage on the demon.

Broken pressed forward, his Golden Paragon Avatar mirroring his every move, amplifying his speed and power. His strikes were faster, stronger, and more precise than ever before. But even now, Focalor seemed untouched by fatigue, his movements swift and calculated as he countered and evaded with ease.

Hovering in the air, Focalor smirked, effortlessly dodging and deflecting the barrage of attacks from every direction. With a casual, almost mocking glance, he retaliated repeatedly, sending waves of destruction back at his opponents.
"The duration is almost up, isn't it?" Focalor's voice was laced with disdain. "Ha! Amateurs. You've wasted the Golden Paragon. What a pathetic waste!"
With that, he darted through the air at incredible speed, his trajectory aimed directly at Broken.
"Once this ends, so will all of you. There will be no second chance, no last stand. This fight is over!" Focalor roared.
3 minutes, 48 seconds.

The duration of the Golden Paragon was down to just over a minute. Broken pushed himself to the edge, pouring every ounce of mana and resources he had left into a relentless flurry of attacks. If his time in this battle was coming to an end, he was determined to leave behind as much damage as possible to ease the burden on his allies.
3 minutes, 59 seconds.
His eyes darted across the battlefield, searching desperately for any signs of a breakthrough, any glimmer of hope. But no answer came to him.
4 minutes, 19 seconds.
In a critical moment, Ivana stepped in to shield Broken, blocking Focalor's attacks. Her actions gave him just enough time to recover and prepare for a counterattack.
"Ivana, you need to leave!" Broken shouted firmly.
Ivana didn't respond, her focus locked entirely on the fight. Meanwhile, Alora continued to exploit the chaos, slipping in and out of Focalor's blind spots to strike from unexpected angles.
The team's attacks came in waves, one after another, but it was becoming painfully evident that even their best efforts couldn't make a dent in the Named Demon.
4 minutes, 34 seconds.
Is this it? Is there really no way out of this? Does it all end here?
Focalor unleashed another devastating energy explosion, scattering the frontline once more.
Chaos spread as their formation disintegrated.
The Named Demon remained untouchable, undeterred, and impossibly powerful.
4 minutes, 52 seconds.
And then it happened.

With a blinding burst of speed, Focalor shot toward Broken, timing his attack perfectly as the duration of the Golden Paragon expired. The radiant avatar dissolved into nothingness, fading from sight as if it had never been there at all.
Before anyone could react, Focalor closed the distance. His clawed hand extended and about to reach Broken.
"Enough with the games, kiddo," Focalor snarled.
[The duration of the Golden Paragon summon has ended.]
No way!
Broken felt the crushing weight of reality as his stats plummeted, leaving him drastically weakened.
The penalty for using the Avatar struck hard, locking him out of all his skills.
The final blow came swift and brutal. His health dropped to zero.
[You have triggered the Ethereal Form.]
A brilliant light enveloped his body, wrapping him in an ethereal glow. In this state, he was immune to physical attacks-but still vulnerable to magic.
"Such an adorable way to try and cling to life," Focalor mocked.
Broken clenched his fists tightly. He could still survive this. If he used the Mask of Scorched
Fury, it would trigger the Fiery Rebirth skill, allowing him to resurrect and launch a counterattack, no matter the cost.
Focalor, wearing a cold, thin smile, prepared his follow-up strike. Dozens of glowing magic circles appeared behind the Named Demon, ready to unleash a relentless barrage of attacks.
Suddenly, an explosion erupted around Broken, engulfing his vision in blinding light.
What just happened?
Before he could make sense of it, someone grabbed him from the side. The grip was firm, and the next thing he knew, he was slung over a shoulder and whisked away at incredible speed.

"You're such a troublesome Guild Master! Can't any of you hold your ground without me around?" the figure said as they ran, carrying Broken on their shoulder, away from the clutches of the Named Demon.
Broken, still dazed from the sudden explosion and his health depletion, could barely process what was happening.
At the same time, a ripple of shock spread through every member of Vensalor Guild, as a notification lit up the guild chat.
[Maylock has logged into the game.]

3 minutes, 59 seconds.
His eyes darted across the battlefield, searching desperately for any signs of a breakthrough, any glimmer of hope.
But no answer came to him.
4 minutes, 19 seconds.
In a critical moment, Ivana stepped in to shield Broken, blocking Focalor's attacks.
Her actions gave him just enough time to recover and prepare for a counterattack.
"Ivana, you need to leave!" Broken shouted firmly.
Ivana didn't respond, her focus locked entirely on the fight.
Meanwhile, Alora continued to exploit the chaos, slipping in and out of Focalor's blind spots to strike from unexpected angles.
The team's attacks came in waves, one after another, but it was becoming painfully evident that even their best efforts couldn't make a dent in the Named Demon.
4 minutes, 34 seconds.
Is this it?
Is there really no way out of this?
Does it all end here?
Focalor unleashed another devastating energy explosion, scattering the frontline once more.
Chaos spread as their formation disintegrated.
The Named Demon remained untouchable, undeterred, and impossibly powerful.
4 minutes, 52 seconds.
And then it happened.
With a blinding burst of speed, Focalor shot toward Broken, timing his attack perfectly as the duration of the Golden Paragon expired.
The radiant avatar dissolved into nothingness, fading from sight as if it had never been there at all.
Before anyone could react, Focalor closed the distance.
His clawed hand extended and about to reach Broken.
"Enough with the games, kiddo," Focalor snarled.
[The duration of the Golden Paragon summon has ended.]
No way!
Broken felt the crushing weight of reality as his stats plummeted, leaving him drastically weakened.
The penalty for using the Avatar struck hard, locking him out of all his skills.
The final blow came swift and brutal.
His health dropped to zero.
[You have triggered the Ethereal Form.]
A brilliant light enveloped his body, wrapping him in an ethereal glow.
In this state, he was immune to physical attacks-but still vulnerable to magic.
"Such an adorable way to try and cling to life," Focalor mocked.
Broken clenched his fists tightly.
He could still survive this.
If he used the Mask of Scorched
Fury, it would trigger the Fiery Rebirth skill, allowing him to resurrect and launch a counterattack, no matter the cost.
Focalor, wearing a cold, thin smile, prepared his follow-up strike.
Dozens of glowing magic circles appeared behind the Named Demon, ready to unleash a relentless barrage of attacks.
Suddenly, an explosion erupted around Broken, engulfing his vision in blinding light.
What just happened?
Before he could make sense of it, someone grabbed him from the side.
The grip was firm, and the next thing he knew, he was slung over a shoulder and whisked away at incredible speed.
"You're such a troublesome Guild Master!
Can't any of you hold your ground without me around?" the figure said as they ran, carrying Broken on their shoulder, away from the clutches of the Named Demon.
Broken, still dazed from the sudden explosion and his health depletion, could barely process what was happening.
At the same time, a ripple of shock spread through every member of Vensalor Guild, as a notification lit up the guild chat.
[Maylock has logged into the game.]

chapters.title: Chapter 713: The Queen of Pride Watches
paragraphs: If one were to ask where in Yunatea technology advanced the most rapidly, where immense power converged, and where the ruler's authority was unrivaled and justice was enforced with unyielding precision, the answer would be clear:
The Central Continent, specifically the Kingdom of Calenvalis.

The throne room of the kingdom was a masterpiece of grandeur. Its polished white stone floor gleamed with intricate patterns, while towering pillars and walls shimmered with white and gold. Every detail radiated regal authority and unmatched luxury.

At the far end of the hall, seated upon the throne, was a woman of commanding presence. She wore a flowing gown of white silk, accented with simple yet elegant light gold armor that symbolized both grace and strength. Her long, silver hair cascaded down her back, complementing her sharp, regal features.
This was no ordinary ruler. Her pointed ears marked her as an elf, but not just any elf. She was a High Elf, the mightiest among her kind-not only of High Elves but also of all elven races.
She was the Queen of Calenvalis, a figure renowned for her unmatched power, influence, and command.
She was a symbol of both fear and reverence, a paragon of authority whose reach extended far beyond the borders of her kingdom.
But her identity carried even more weight. She was the Ancestral Wielder of the Pride Champion, a title and legacy that marked her as the pinnacle of elven power and dominion.
"Your Majesty," a player clad in gleaming gold heavy armor knelt before the throne, his voice steady but reverent.
Two others followed his example, lowering themselves in deference.
The High Elf Queen tilted her chin slightly, her silver hair catching the ambient light, but offered no response.
"A great war is unfolding in the Dissidia Kingdom," the armored man continued, his gaze fixed on the floor. "Reports of the potential arrival of Named Demons have been confirmed."
Still, the queen remained silent, her expression serene yet unreadable.
"At first, there were four Named Demons, all ranked in the 50s," the man pressed on. "Then, a higher-ranked Named Demon appeared-ranking 36. The King of Dissidia fought this Named Demon."

Her silence persisted, and the player continued. "In short, the king's younger brother seems to be orchestrating yet another rebellion, this time with a far more brutal agenda. His plan appears to involve the Demon Bael."
The mention of the name broke the queen's stillness. Her lips parted slightly as she spoke in a calm tone, "Bael?"
"The defeated Bael dares to set his sights on Yunatea?" she murmured.
"Your Majesty..." the man continued, his tone quieter, almost hesitant. "It appears that the ritual failed. It also failed to summon Demon Bael to Yunatea."
"Bael will not come to Yunatea so easily," the queen replied.
The player fell silent, his gaze still cast downward.
"And... what, exactly, makes this news worth my interest?"
The player hesitated, his voice trembling slightly as he finally spoke. "This is... about the current wielder of the Greed Blessing..."
At those words, the queen's expression shifted.
"You've found that child?" she asked.
Broken, in his weakened state had been saved by an unexpected figure-Maylock.

The archer had swooped in at the last possible moment, snatching Broken away just before Focalor could deliver a fatal blow. Now, the two of them retreated from the battlefield, Maylock running at full speed while Broken hung, too drained to argue. In his current state, staying in the fight wasn't just dangerous-it was impossible.
But the battle raged on.

Without Broken, the team's overall damage output plummeted. The remaining fighters, desperate to fill the void, pushed themselves to the brink. Close-range fighters and tanks stepped forward, forcing themselves into the frontline to hold the Named Demon back. Yet, the grim reality was clear: this strategy was unsustainable.

Among those who surged to the front was Booba, wielding his sword with ferocity. He attacked relentlessly, but even his might paled before Focalor's overwhelming power. With a swift, effortless slash of Focalor's hand, Booba's form disintegrated.
Everyone swallowed hard, dread creeping into their hearts.

Focalor wasted no time, darting toward other frontliners. Skywarden barely had a chance to react before Focalor's clawed hand pierced his chest clean through. Moments later, the demon surged forward again, his next strike cleanly severing Optimus's head.
Both tanks disappeared from the battlefield, their absence a devastating blow.

Kingsley, in his massive bear form, roared and charged, his enormous paws slamming into the ground in a desperate attempt to corner Focalor. But before he could land a meaningful hit, a barrage of supermassive magical attacks rained down from above, smashing into the armored bear repeatedly. With a final, echoing roar, Kingsley, too, vanished.
One by one, the tanks were being eradicated. The frontline was crumbling fast.
This was no longer a fight for victory-it was becoming a fight for survival.
"Broken, I need to tell you something important.
Broken struggled against Maylock's grip as they reached a relatively safe area.
"Broken! Listen to me!" Maylock snapped, his voice firm as he clamped both hands onto Broken's shoulders
"We need to do something!" Broken said. "Alora, Ivana, and the others—"
"Broken, listen to me!" Maylock interrupted.
"I still have one item I can use," Broken said back.
"I know, I know!" Maylock replied quickly, tightening his hold. "But there's something important you need to hear first. Just listen!"
"What's that?"
"Look, we all know we have to win this war. You know it, I know it-everyone knows it. And I'm taking the responsibility to say what needs to be said right now," Maylock stated firmly.
"Maylock, what are you saying?"
"Broken!" Maylock's sharp voice cut through. "This is about the quest you received a long time ago."
"...The quest?"
"Yes," Maylock continued. "The quest you got after clearing the Trial Domain in Wildwood Forest. The one given to you by King Elandorr-the first Ancestral Wielder of the Sloth
Champion."

Broken fixed his gaze on Maylock, his expression tense. He had already explained many details to Elincia and Goldrich in the past, and the information had been passed along to Maylock as well. However, Broken hadn't delved deeply into the topic again-especially since Maylock hadn't logged in since the war at Deadbay City.
But the quest?
"This quest might be the key to changing the outcome of this war," Maylock said.
With trembling hands, Broken opened his list of ongoing quests and his eyes landed on one in particular.
[Deity Bane Quest II - The Dragon Princess' Call]

chapters.title: Chapter 714: The Ancestral Greed Champion
paragraphs: 449 Days Earlier.
"A special NPC?" Maylock repeated.

"Khi khi khi, yes... the boy was sought out by a Special NPC who waited for him all morning near the central plaza-a stunning woman so beautiful that every man passing by couldn't help but gawk, their mouths hanging open," Goldrich chuckled.
Maylock, seated in the room alongside Goldrich and Elincia, rubbed his chin thoughtfully.
"Broken certainly has a knack for attracting the attention of Special NPCs, doesn't he?" Elincia said with a soft laugh. "First Princess Alora, and now this new woman."
"And who exactly is this woman? Someone important?"
"I'm not entirely sure," Goldrich admitted, still smiling. "Why don't we ask Broken directly?" 394 Days Earlier.
"That's certainly an extraordinary taunt skill," Maylock said as he watched a video clip circulating online.

"She definitely has an impressive set of skills, doesn't she?" Elincia replied. "They went to the desert area earlier today-looks like Broken wanted to test his new Legendary-grade spear, and... well, that happened."
"She used a taunt skill that drew in so many monsters at once? That's definitely a high-grade skill. Is this the first time she's shown it?"
"We've never been on the same battlefield as her before," Elincia admitted. "But she does seem worthy of the title Special NPC."
Maylock was quiet for a moment before speaking again. "It's strange. Just a few months ago, people in Deadbay only knew her as a chef with no combat potential. And now, she's a powerful Special NPC."
"Do you know what triggered it?" Elincia asked.
"From what I've heard, it happened after she lost her mother," Maylock replied thoughtfully.
"That's certainly a unique way to gain Special NPC status," Elincia mused.
Maylock nodded slowly. "I'm convinced that this woman-her mother, I mean-held something important tied to Yunatea's greater lore," he said with a sigh.
"You're not speculating further?"
"Not yet, not now."
"I know you're already holding onto something you're thinking about!"
250 Days Earlier.

Maylock, Elincia, and Goldrich sat in the same room, the air heavy with tension after witnessing the intense battle Broken and the others had fought against a Named Demon in Hell. Fortunately, they had emerged victorious, though many factors had played a crucial role in that hard-fought battle.
"Do you understand the blessing possessed by the first Ancestral of the Greed Champion?" Maylock began, breaking the silence.
"It was the power to control Mana and Elements," Goldrich replied, his tone steady.
"Yes, but it goes beyond that," Maylock said, leaning forward slightly. "They had the ability to craft their own skills."
Goldrich tilted his head, a hint of curiosity in his expression. "Are you suggesting that she's the Greed Champion?"
"It's too early to draw conclusions," Maylock said, standing and preparing to leave the room.
Goldrich's eyes narrowed slightly as he spoke again. "Are you worried about something, Maylock?"
Maylock paused for a brief moment before responding. "No. I'm not worried about anything -or anyone."
With that, he left the room.
217 Days Earlier.
"That's so depressing," Maylock muttered as they made their way through the dense Wildwood Forest.
"Monsters that many, and all we could do was hide in a cave, holding out and hoping for help. That's so depressing," he continued, shaking his head.
Walking beside him, Elincia replied with a slight smile. "Luckily, we had a powerful tanker on our side."
"Not just powerful," Maylock corrected. "We'd all have died a pointless death against that many monsters if not for her. She held off their attacks all on her own. Not even ten
Skywardens could've managed that."
Elincia chuckled softly. "Are you favoring her now, the way you idolize Broken?"
"I always admire someone with overpowered abilities."
"Is that why you agreed when Broken suggested taking her to meet the fae?"
"Not really... there just wasn't any other viable option given the situation," Maylock replied.
205 Days Earlier.

"Once again, we've been saved by an insanely powerful and overpowered Special NPC," Maylock remarked, brushing off the tension as they regrouped after defending Deadbay City from a massive assault that had nearly brought the city to its knees.
"Khi khi khi, I can see how the Golden Age Company rushed their decisions to handle this event," Goldrich chimed in. "It seems they didn't anticipate things escalating to this level."
Elincia let out a weary sigh. "It's clear they don't have much control over what's happening, especially with the fae launching their attacks on Deadbay City."
Maylock glanced at her thoughtfully. "My contact from the Central Continent mentioned something interesting-the Queen was paying attention to this battle."
"The Queen? The High Elf Queen?"
"Yes," Maylock confirmed. "If the strongest being in Yunatea is taking an interest in what just happened, there's likely something bigger at play-something we're not aware of yet."
"And what might that be?" Elincia pressed.
"Perhaps something tied to the ancient war," Maylock speculated. "I don't know for sure, but I'll let you know if I learn more. Unfortunately, I won't be able to log in as often after this."
157 Days Earlier.
"Congrats on the guild's inauguration, I'm so happy for everyone," Maylock said.
Four floating avatars were visible in the virtual space-Maylock, Elincia, Goldrich, and another figure in the room.
"You should've been there," Elincia said. "He was really looking forward to seeing you."
"I can't," Maylock replied flatly. "I can't show up when I know I won't be able to contribute anything meaningful to the guild."
"Take your time, Maylock," Goldrich said. "Come back when you're ready."
"Thanks..." Maylock replied softly.
Elincia's expression shifted slightly as she broke the silence. "So, why did you call this meeting? And why did you invite Freya this time?"
Maylock turned to look at Freya's avatar. "Well, I've been studying some important information that Broken shared, and there's a question I've been wanting to ask you."
"Just get to the point," Freya said.
"Why did you hide the truth from Broken?"
"What truth?" Elincia interjected.
Freya sighed, her demeanor calm but resigned. "That's a question I'm sure you already know the answer to."
"Wait..." Elincia pressed. "Maylock, is your suspicion correct?"
"One hundred percent," Maylock said firmly.
"That's some absolute certainty," Elincia remarked.
[She was the hope. The chosen one.]
"This relates to the current Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion," Maylock said.
[She survived. While the others perished.]
"According to lore from numerous sources, the last Dragon Kingdom hid their heir-a dragon egg-in a secret location," he explained.
[She lived with those lower than her. She was saved by the humble one.]
"Yes," Maylock added, "the egg was rescued by the Dragonkin in the West Continent."
[But, another disaster struck. A calamity seemed to follow her.]
"However, the Dragonkin tribe was raided by an unknown force-most likely sent by the High
Elf Queen," he said grimly.
[Everything perished. Except her.]
"Every dragonkin in that area was wiped out, but this important figure should still have survived," he said.
[She was so isolated. She felt forgotten and forlorn.]
[The voice told her of her destiny. To fulfill a heavy duty of her people.]
[The girl had a choice to make. To accept her fate or run away.]
[She thought of the people she used to know. But they were gone, so she chose to stay.]
[The Dragon Princess lost her wings. But she was ready to take on her destiny.] "The dragon princess survived, but she lost her wings and was hidden by someone-or
something. The only one who might know the truth is the first Ancestral Wielder of the Sloth Champion: King Elandorr, who met Broken during the Trial Domain."
Maylock turned to Freya. "The mountain depicted on her bracelet-is the location where the
Dragonkin lived. That's correct, isn't it?"
"Yes," Freya replied simply.
The space fell silent for a moment before Freya spoke again. "It would be better if Broken never completes the quest."
Maylock nodded slowly. "I understand."

"But..." Freya continued, her tone softening slightly. "I won't make the decision for the entire scenario. I know you all care for him too. So, if you believe the time has come, make the call. But I'll stand by my conviction."
Elincia and Goldrich remained quiet, their expressions heavy with thought after hearing her words.

"When the time comes, let me take the blame," Maylock said at last, breaking the silence. "I'm used to being cast aside for my boldness. Thanks for the meeting." With that, his avatar disappeared, leaving the room.
Elincia, still present, turned to Freya and shook her head. "It should have been us protecting her."
Freya nodded slowly but said nothing.
The Current Time

"The person you've been searching for is here, right by your side. The Dragon Princess... Ivana is the one you've been looking for. The current Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion. The one who can craft any skill needed when it's for someone she truly cares about. She's the only hope we have right now." Broken shook his head in disbelief as Maylock's words sank in.

"I can't show up when I know I won't be able to contribute anything meaningful to the guild."
"Take your time, Maylock," Goldrich said.
"Come back when you're ready."
"Thanks..." Maylock replied softly.
Elincia's expression shifted slightly as she broke the silence.
"So, why did you call this meeting?
And why did you invite Freya this time?"
Maylock turned to look at Freya's avatar.
"Well, I've been studying some important information that Broken shared, and there's a question I've been wanting to ask you."
"Just get to the point," Freya said.
"Why did you hide the truth from Broken?"
"What truth?" Elincia interjected.
Freya sighed, her demeanor calm but resigned.
"That's a question I'm sure you already know the answer to."
"Wait..." Elincia pressed.
"Maylock, is your suspicion correct?"
"One hundred percent," Maylock said firmly.
"That's some absolute certainty," Elincia remarked.
[She was the hope.
The chosen one.]
"This relates to the current Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion," Maylock said.
[She survived.
While the others perished.]
"According to lore from numerous sources, the last Dragon Kingdom hid their heir-a dragon egg-in a secret location," he explained.
[She lived with those lower than her.
She was saved by the humble one.]
"Yes," Maylock added, "the egg was rescued by the Dragonkin in the West Continent."
[But, another disaster struck.
A calamity seemed to follow her.]
"However, the Dragonkin tribe was raided by an unknown force-most likely sent by the High
Elf Queen," he said grimly.
[Everything perished.
Except her.]
"Every dragonkin in that area was wiped out, but this important figure should still have survived," he said.
[She was so isolated.
She felt forgotten and forlorn.]
[The voice told her of her destiny.
To fulfill a heavy duty of her people.]
[The girl had a choice to make.
To accept her fate or run away.]
[She thought of the people she used to know.
But they were gone, so she chose to stay.]
[The Dragon Princess lost her wings.
But she was ready to take on her destiny.] "The dragon princess survived, but she lost her wings and was hidden by someone-or
something.
The only one who might know the truth is the first Ancestral Wielder of the Sloth Champion: King Elandorr, who met Broken during the Trial Domain."
Maylock turned to Freya.
"The mountain depicted on her bracelet-is the location where the
Dragonkin lived.
That's correct, isn't it?"
"Yes," Freya replied simply.
The space fell silent for a moment before Freya spoke again.
"It would be better if Broken never completes the quest."
Maylock nodded slowly.
"I understand."
"But..." Freya continued, her tone softening slightly.
"I won't make the decision for the entire scenario.
I know you all care for him too.
So, if you believe the time has come, make the call.
But I'll stand by my conviction."
Elincia and Goldrich remained quiet, their expressions heavy with thought after hearing her words.
"When the time comes, let me take the blame," Maylock said at last, breaking the silence.
"I'm used to being cast aside for my boldness.
Thanks for the meeting." With that, his avatar disappeared, leaving the room.
Elincia, still present, turned to Freya and shook her head.
"It should have been us protecting her."
Freya nodded slowly but said nothing.
The Current Time
"The person you've been searching for is here, right by your side.
The Dragon Princess...
Ivana is the one you've been looking for.
The current Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion.
The one who can craft any skill needed when it's for someone she truly cares about.
She's the only hope we have right now." Broken shook his head in disbelief as Maylock's words sank in.

chapters.title: Chapter 715: Lunar Tear Crystal
paragraphs: The Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion was once the ruler of the Dragon race, the mightiest being in Yunatea's history. However, their reign was ultimately brought to ruin by the Pride Champion, the High Elf Queen-who now rules the Central Continent, specifically the Kingdom of Calenvalis.

The High Elf Queen formed an unholy alliance with King Bael, the ruler of Hell. Together, their pact led to the annihilation of the dragon race. Dragons were hunted and slaughtered, their once-mighty kingdom crushed. Even the Dragon King, the First Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion, was ultimately defeated, their power extinguished.

But the war didn't truly end there. It was foretold that the dragon lineage would endure, as a successor had been born-a hidden heir, prophesied to rise as the Dragon Princess, the next Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion.

The tale of the Dragon Princess faded into obscurity, buried by the passage of time. That is, until years before the Players' arrival in Yunatea, when whispers emerged of a devastating raid that annihilated the Dragonkin tribe in the West Continent.
This raid was said to have been orchestrated by emissaries of the High Elf Queen, determined to hunt down the elusive Dragon Princess.

The story of her escape and disappearance remains cloaked in mystery. However, rumors suggest her survival was made possible by the intervention of a revered figure in Yunatea- particularly celebrated in the East Continent-the Moon Goddess.
The Moon Goddess was long rumored to be intertwined with Yunatea's most pivotal events and was said to share a deep bond with the First Ancestral Wielder of the Sloth Champion, King Elandorr.
Though King Elandorr was believed to have perished ages ago, his name resurfaced when Broken successfully completed the Trial Domain and encountered a fragment of Elandorr's soul.

Back in the present, during earlier encounters, Ivana had been nothing more than an ordinary NPC living in a quiet coastal area of the Dissidia Kingdom. Raised by a humble mining family, her life was simple and uneventful-until a sudden, life-altering moment. When the person who had adopted her passed away, everything changed. In that instant, Ivana ascended to the status of a Special NPC.

As a shielder, Ivana gained a reputation for possessing an arsenal of overpowered skills. Strangely, these abilities only emerged under certain conditions-primarily when they involved protecting the people or things she cared for the most. This became evident during critical moments, such as defending Deadbay City or aiding... Broken.

No special NPC could manifest such extraordinary skills spontaneously, unless they bore a Sin Blessing-specifically, that of the Greed Champion, who possessed the unique ability to craft any skill they desired. This power marked her as the rightful heir to the Dragonblood Throne and the legacy of the Greed Champion.

"Yes, Ivana is the Dragon Princess," Maylock said. "The quest is S-rated. I'm certain the reward will give us a chance to win this war. More importantly, if we can break the seal that locks away her true power, it will be our turning point-the greatest opportunity we have to end this war. It's the only way."
Broken reached into his inventory and retrieved something from it.
[Unique-grade All You Need Ticket]

It was a reward he had earned after completing the quest 'Uncovering the Hero of Destiny,' a mission tied to King Elandorr's legacy, granted to him through the heirloom ring he'd won during the competition in the Dissidia Kingdom.
"Activate the ticket," Maylock said.
Broken hesitated, his grip tightening on the item. "What will happen to Ivana?"

Meanwhile, on the battlefield, the situation was growing increasingly dire. One by one, important figures fell. After the frontline defenders like Optimus, Skywarden, and Kingsley were killed, even Goldrich and Elincia succumbed to Focalor's relentless onslaught.

With fewer damage dealers and close-range defenders remaining, the battlefield's momentum tilted dangerously in Focalor's favor. The absence of Broken had left a massive void, allowing the Named Demon to target high-priority damage dealers with ease, his attacks almost unchallenged.

Focalor soared swiftly through the chaos, his eyes locking onto Ivana. The girl raised her shield, bracing herself for his assault. But before the demon could reach her, a massive hammer came hurtling toward him. With a cold, thin smile, Focalor caught the hammer mid- air effortlessly, then flung it back with incredible force.
The hammer crashed into Fokil, sending him flying across the battlefield with a devastating impact.

Alora seized the opening, darting in with her blade. However, Focalor moved with lightning speed, grabbing her by the throat. Alora dropped her sword, her hands clawing at his grip in a desperate attempt to break free.

With a single powerful kick, Focalor struck Ivana's shield, sending her sprawling to the ground. He landed over her, pinning her face into the dirt with his foot. Shadowy tendrils emerged from the ground, binding her in place and rendering her unable to fight back.
Frostedge rushed in, closing the distance to launch a melee assault. However, it was clear he was struggling to maintain his offense while defending himself against the demon's overwhelming power.

With a sinister gleam in his eye, Focalor formed a massive shadow tendril resembling a spear. The dark weapon surged forward, piercing Frostedge's chest with brutal force, lifting him off the ground and hurling him far beyond the battlefield.
The situation was grim. Victory was slipping further from their grasp with each passing moment.
No matter what happens, there was no better choice left for them to make.
Broken had made his decision-this was their only hope, their one chance to turn the tide.
[Unique-grade All You Need Ticket activated.]
The ticket in his hand ignited, engulfed by a radiant light before disintegrating into nothingness. Notifications flooded his vision.
[Analyzing the most suitable item required by the activator in the current situation.]
[Analyzing all scenarios.]
[The blessing from the Moon Goddess interferes with the ticket.]
The Moon Goddess? Again?
Why was her influence always intertwined with these pivotal moments?
[Her blessing has been infused into the item and successfully triggered the most desired
outcome from the ticket.]
[You have gained her recognition and appreciation.]
[The item has been decided: you have received Mythic-grade Lunar Tear Crystal.]
The notifications faded, leaving Broken holding the shimmering crystal, its glow pulsating
faintly with ethereal energy.

[A radiant crystal imbued with the essence of the Moon Goddess, crafted to suppress or restore hidden powers and memories. It holds the ability to break seals created with divine energy, revealing the true identity and potential of its bearer.]
[Effect:]
[- Dispels divine seals that hide powers, identities, or memories.]
[- Unlocks the full potential of the affected individual.]

[The Lunar Tear Crystal was forged in ancient times by the Moon Goddess herself, meant to safeguard those burdened with dangerous legacies or overwhelming destinies. It can only be activated in the presence of someone whose sealed potential aligns with their destined path.]
"Ivana..." Broken whispered, his voice barely audible as he clenched his fist tightly. This was their only chance, the only option left.
Without hesitation, he activated the Lunar Tear Crystal. A brilliant light erupted from his hand, radiating with an almost divine glow.

At the same moment, far across the battlefield where Ivana lay pinned under Duke Focalor's grasp, a similar light began to shine, emanating from her. The sudden burst of energy caught everyone's attention, piercing through the chaos.
[Congratulations, you've successfully completed the quest.]
The notification flashed before Broken's eyes, a sign that their decision had finally paid off.

chapters.title: Chapter 716: Stay With Me
paragraphs: All eyes were locked on Duke Focalor, their primary adversary that night. However, two figures remained caught in the demon's grip-Princess Alora, struggling as his right hand tightened around her neck, and Ivana, pinned beneath his foot, her head crushed harshly into the dirt.

Desperation filled the air as players and NPCs launched attack after attack, trying to free the two women. But Focalor proved too strong. Without moving from his spot, he summoned several magic circles around him, effortlessly repelling every assault. Each blast sent attackers flying backward, their efforts reduced to nothing.
Then, suddenly—something changed.
Ivana's body, pinned beneath Focalor's foot, began to glow with a brilliant white energy. The light pulsed, burning away the shadow tendrils binding her to the ground.
Focalor immediately glanced down, his expression shifting from smug confidence to shock.
What happened?!
The tense question echoed through the battlefield, whispered by everyone who witnessed the sudden change.

With a snarl, Focalor flung Alora aside, throwing her body toward the ranks of the knights. Her limp form flew through the air before crashing into the defensive line, where Lionell caught her, pulling her to safety.
Focalor, now enraged, conjured a massive energy ball in his right hand. His teeth clenched as he channeled all his fury into it, slamming the attack toward Ivana.
"Ivana! No!"
Broken sprinted toward them, panic seizing his chest. But before he could reach her-
Everything stopped!
For a brief moment, the world seemed to freeze. Sounds were sucked into silence. Time itself appeared to halt. But it wasn't truly time that stopped-
It was gravity.
All at once, the battlefield felt as though it was being pulled toward a single point. The force wasn't coming from Focalor-it was coming from Ivana, still lying beneath him.
Then, without warning, it happened.
A massive, supermassive explosion erupted from their position.
B-BOOOOOOM!!!

The deafening blast of pure energy ripped through the battlefield with a WHOOOMPH of unstoppable force, sending shockwaves that crashed into everything in its path, scattering debris and bodies alike.
KRAK-KOOOOM!!!
The ground shattered with a violent crack, debris whooshed through the air, and a storm of dust and rubble WHOMPED outward, engulfing the battlefield in chaos.
THUUUUMMM!!!

Broken barely registered what was happening as he was hurled backward. The shockwave tore through knights, players, demons-no one could withstand its sheer force. Those who tried to brace themselves were immediately overwhelmed, the damage from the explosion ripping through the area mercilessly.
Debris and dust swirled violently into the air, rising like a towering storm. The battlefield became a chaotic blur of flying rubble and shattered earth.
Polly emerged. Broken leapt onto her back, and with a powerful beat of her wings, she lifted him into the air, carrying him away from the epicenter of the blast.
Below, Maylock was already retreating, sprinting across the battlefield with swift movements to evade the destruction tearing through everything in its path.
"Alora?!" Broken frantically scanned the battlefield. Through the debris, he spotted Lionell, cradling Alora in his arms as he quickly retreated, carrying her to safety.
But Ivana?!
Panic clawed at his chest.
"What happened to Ivana?!"
Broken quickly checked his Affinity Status with Ivana, and her name was still there. Relief washed over him briefly-she was alive.
But... that explosion.
It was undoubtedly caused by Ivana, likely as part of the process of unlocking her seal or something deeper. Yet, why had the blast affected everyone on the battlefield?
That could only mean one thing-Ivana had no control over the explosion. Or worse, the detonation hadn't been something she triggered intentionally.

Broken's gaze shifted to the Guild Status panel. His heart sank as he saw more guild members marked as deceased. Only Charmelyn, Tora and Maylock remained alive, while Frostedge's buff was still active on him, indicating that Frostedge had survived somewhere. He also spotted Galactron, hovering in the air on the head of his skeletal dragon, scanning the battlefield.
SexyGrill and SexyBloom still survived too.
As soon as the shockwave settled, Broken leaned forward. "Polly, back to the center of the explosion!" he ordered.
Polly immediately shifted her flight path, wings beating hard as they rushed back toward the epicenter of destruction.
His vision filled with a flurry of notifications, but he skipped through them all without hesitation.
None of it mattered right now.
He needed to know.
He needed to know what happened to Ivana.
As they approached the center of the explosion, the devastation became clear. Nothing remained near the blast zone-just scorched earth and scattered debris.

Polly swooped low, Broken leapt off her back, landing firmly on the ground. He pushed forward, stepping through the swirling dust and smoke, his heart pounding in his chest. His eyes locked onto the spot where Ivana had been moments ago.
And there, standing amidst the wreckage...

Broken froze. His body tensed, his hands trembling before clenching into fists. His jaw tightened as he struggled to process what he was seeing, a swirl of emotions crashing over him-confusion, awe, and dread, all at once.
Because the figure before him wasn't the Ivana he knew.

There she stood, her familiar blonde hair flowing past her shoulders. She was clad in heavy armor, cracked and glowing with faint traces of energy. From the cracks in her back, a pair of dragon wings slowly unfurled, stretching and flexing with a quiet, ominous grace.
Two sharp horns curved from the sides of her head, and as the dust cleared further, Broken's gaze dropped lower-
A tail swayed behind her, slow and deliberate. A dragon's tail.
This wasn't just Ivana.
This was something more.
His gaze drifted beyond her, toward the distant figure that had haunted them throughout the battle.
Duke Focalor.
The Named Demon stood motionless, watching Ivana with a cold, calculating stare. His body remained intact, untouched by the blast, his presence still radiating dread. Yet, for now, he did nothing.
"Ivana..." Broken whispered, his mind racing.
The quest mentioned that she lost her memories.
Did unlocking the seal cause her to forget everything? Did she lose who she was? Did she forget... me?

Without hesitation, Broken began to walk toward her. Slowly, carefully, he approached the dragon-like figure standing before him. He didn't care about Focalor. He didn't care about anything else at that moment.
He just needed to know that she was still Ivana.
Finally, Broken stopped, standing directly behind her. The faint glow of her dragon wings shimmered in the dim light.
"Ivana..." he murmured, his voice soft and uncertain.
At the sound of his voice, the girl stirred. Her head turned slowly, her golden hair falling across her face as she looked back at him.
Their eyes met. Broken's breath caught. For a fleeting second, fear clawed at his chest-fear that she wouldn't recognize him, that she would be someone else entirely. But then he saw it.
The same eyes.
The same gaze he had come to know, filled with emotion and warmth.

Without a second thought, Broken stepped closer and wrapped his arms around her, pulling her into a firm embrace. There was no hesitation. No doubt. He held her tightly, as if anchoring her to the world.
She didn't pull away.
"You are still the Ivana I know," Broken whispered. "You haven't lost anything."
Moments passed in silence before a soft voice broke through.
"Broken..." she finally said.
"I'm with you," he whispered back, holding her closer. "I won't leave you. No matter what happens, I'm here."
Ivana's body trembled slightly in his arms. "What should I do?"
"End our enemy. And everything will go back to how it was." "But... I... I'm not the same Ivana anymore..." she said softly, her voice wavering.
Broken pulled back just enough to look at her, his hands cupping her face. "You are the same
Ivana. You've never changed. You're still the kind, caring Ivana I've always known."
There was a pause, the weight of his words settling over her. Slowly, she nodded. "I'm scared..." she admitted, her voice barely above a whisper.
"You don't have to be afraid," Broken reassured her. "We'll get through this together."
For a moment, silence stretched between them, broken only by the distant sounds of the battlefield. Then, Ivana's quiet voice reached his ears once more.
"Stay with me."
"I will," Broken said. "Always."
"What a touching moment," came a cold voice from the other side. "Has the little romance scene ended? Because I'm getting a bit sick of watching this."
The demon spread his arms wide.
"What a jackpot this is, actually," he continued. "I couldn't have asked for more. I'll absorb all of your power... and no one will be able to stop me."
