He needed to know what happened to Ivana.
As they approached the center of the explosion, the devastation became clear.
Nothing remained near the blast zone-just scorched earth and scattered debris.
Polly swooped low, Broken leapt off her back, landing firmly on the ground.
He pushed forward, stepping through the swirling dust and smoke, his heart pounding in his chest.
His eyes locked onto the spot where Ivana had been moments ago.
And there, standing amidst the wreckage...
Broken froze.
His body tensed, his hands trembling before clenching into fists.
His jaw tightened as he struggled to process what he was seeing, a swirl of emotions crashing over him-confusion, awe, and dread, all at once.
Because the figure before him wasn't the Ivana he knew.
There she stood, her familiar blonde hair flowing past her shoulders.
She was clad in heavy armor, cracked and glowing with faint traces of energy.
From the cracks in her back, a pair of dragon wings slowly unfurled, stretching and flexing with a quiet, ominous grace.
Two sharp horns curved from the sides of her head, and as the dust cleared further, Broken's gaze dropped lower-
A tail swayed behind her, slow and deliberate.
A dragon's tail.
This wasn't just Ivana.
This was something more.
His gaze drifted beyond her, toward the distant figure that had haunted them throughout the battle.
Duke Focalor.
The Named Demon stood motionless, watching Ivana with a cold, calculating stare.
His body remained intact, untouched by the blast, his presence still radiating dread.
Yet, for now, he did nothing.
"Ivana..." Broken whispered, his mind racing.
The quest mentioned that she lost her memories.
Did unlocking the seal cause her to forget everything?
Did she lose who she was?
Did she forget... me?
Without hesitation, Broken began to walk toward her.
Slowly, carefully, he approached the dragon-like figure standing before him.
He didn't care about Focalor.
He didn't care about anything else at that moment.
He just needed to know that she was still Ivana.
Finally, Broken stopped, standing directly behind her.
The faint glow of her dragon wings shimmered in the dim light.
"Ivana..." he murmured, his voice soft and uncertain.
At the sound of his voice, the girl stirred.
Her head turned slowly, her golden hair falling across her face as she looked back at him.
Their eyes met.
Broken's breath caught.
For a fleeting second, fear clawed at his chest-fear that she wouldn't recognize him, that she would be someone else entirely.
But then he saw it.
The same eyes.
The same gaze he had come to know, filled with emotion and warmth.
Without a second thought, Broken stepped closer and wrapped his arms around her, pulling her into a firm embrace.
There was no hesitation.
No doubt.
He held her tightly, as if anchoring her to the world.
She didn't pull away.
"You are still the Ivana I know," Broken whispered.
"You haven't lost anything."
Moments passed in silence before a soft voice broke through.
"Broken..." she finally said.
"I'm with you," he whispered back, holding her closer.
"I won't leave you.
No matter what happens, I'm here."
Ivana's body trembled slightly in his arms.
"What should I do?"
"End our enemy.
And everything will go back to how it was." "But...
I'm not the same Ivana anymore..." she said softly, her voice wavering.
Broken pulled back just enough to look at her, his hands cupping her face.
"You are the same
Ivana.
You've never changed.
You're still the kind, caring Ivana I've always known."
There was a pause, the weight of his words settling over her.
Slowly, she nodded.
"I'm scared..." she admitted, her voice barely above a whisper.
"You don't have to be afraid," Broken reassured her.
"We'll get through this together."
For a moment, silence stretched between them, broken only by the distant sounds of the battlefield.
Then, Ivana's quiet voice reached his ears once more.
"Stay with me."
"I will," Broken said.
"Always."
"What a touching moment," came a cold voice from the other side.
"Has the little romance scene ended?
Because I'm getting a bit sick of watching this."
The demon spread his arms wide.
"What a jackpot this is, actually," he continued.
"I couldn't have asked for more.
I'll absorb all of your power... and no one will be able to stop me."

chapters.title: Chapter 717: Mythic Forge Crystal (Info Dump Alert!)
paragraphs: Broken gently released Ivana from his embrace, but his hands lingered, cupping her face. His thumbs brushed against her cheeks as he looked into her eyes.
And there it was-the same warmth, the same kindness, the same Ivana he had always known.
But she was no longer the simple chef girl from the coastal village.
She was the Dragon Princess.
She was the Ancestral Wielder of the Greed Champion.
Ivana was the Greed Champion.
His heart pounded, but he smiled softly at her.
Then, without a word, he turned toward Duke Focalor, his gaze locking on the demon who stood across the battlefield. Ivana moved to his side, standing just to his left.
As the dust settled around them, Broken glanced at the notifications from his quest completion, reading through the details he had ignored in the chaos.
[Deity Bane Quest II - The Dragon Princess' Call Completed]
[You have successfully located the Dragon Princess and assisted her in unlocking her true power.]
[The Princess's fate is no longer her own. She is free to walk her path, thanks to you.]
[Performance Evaluation]
["Fate bends for those bold enough to defy its flow. I once gave you a tool to reshape destiny, and now, I offer you another-though it comes with greater risks this time."]
[You not only unlocked the Dragon Princess's potential but also forged unbreakable bonds with allies willing to defend her cause.]
[Reward Unlocked: Reset & Recharge Ticket]

[Hit the ultimate do-over button! With this ticket, you get a total reset and a fresh recharge. Everything back to full, like you never even ran out. Perfect for when you need a second wind (or third... we won't judge)!]
[Reward Unlocked: Mythic Forge Crystal]
[A rare and volatile crystal capable of upgrading any Legendary weapon to Mythic grade. The crystal's power is unpredictable, but with it, the potential to forge legendary tales is in your hands.]
["Every blade has a destiny. Will you gamble yours?"]

["The road ahead is uncertain, Broken. There will be more enemies to face, more truths to uncover, and more choices to make. But know this: no fate is sealed until you decide it is."] [Your Fate is Now in Your Hands.]
[Will you wield the power to rewrite destiny-or will you succumb to its flow?]
[The choice is yours.]
Broken couldn't help but smile faintly as he skimmed through the quest rewards.
The exact same ticket he got from Goddess Akidia. Reset & Recharge Ticket.
That alone was valuable beyond measure. But his eyes widened slightly as he saw the next reward—a reward that left him momentarily speechless.
An item to upgrade a Legendary-grade weapon into Mythic-grade!
Broken blinked, unsure whether to laugh or shake his head in disbelief. The sheer rarity of such an item was unheard of. He knew what it meant-this wasn't just a reward; it was a game-changer.
"...A Mythic upgrade item?" he muttered to himself.
Even he wasn't sure what to say.
Without hesitation, he tore the ticket in his hand.
[You have activated the Reset & Recharge Ticket!]
[Your overall condition has been reset.]
[Mana replenished, Health fully restored, Stamina at peak levels.]
[Additionally, Soul Points have been completely filled.]
Without hesitation, he applied the second reward to his Wavebreaker Spear.
If there was one weapon he mastered above all others, it was the spear. The synergy between his Legendary-grade cape and Water Domain made this upgrade the perfect choice.
As he confirmed the enhancement, a series of notifications appeared in front of him:
[Mythic Upgrade Process Initiated...]
[Wavebreaker Spear is undergoing transformation...]
[Upgrade Successful!]
[You have upgraded +18 Wavebreaker Spear (Legendary) to +18 Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear (Mythic)].
Surprisingly, the +18 enhancement was still intact even after the upgrade process.
Without hesitation, Broken opened the detailed description of his newly upgraded weapon- Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear.
[+18 Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear]
[Grade: Mythic]
[Attack Power: 2314~2559
Stamina +244
Constitution +358
Strength +260]
[Durability: 100/100]
[Weight: 1600]

[Forged in the deepest ocean trenches, this spear now carries the blessing of an ancient abyssal deity. Its waters bring chaos to the battlefield, crashing down like tidal waves, while the mighty spirit of the Abyssal Tideboar hunts down enemies with unrelenting fury. Whether striking a single foe or devastating an entire army, the spear ensures no one escapes the
ocean's wrath.]
[Skills:]
Mythic Grade!
The glowing label was unmistakable. The sheer power radiating from the spear was overwhelming, and as he read through the weapon's stats and abilities, he couldn't help but tremble with excitement.

[ Abyssal Cascade - Torrent of Destruction (Mythic AoE Active Skill): Unleash the Abyssal Cascade, a colossal torrent of water that crashes down on enemies, overwhelming them with sheer force and leaving them drenched and vulnerable.
Effect:
A massive tidal wave crashes down in a large AoE, dealing 700% physical damage and 700%
water elemental damage to all enemies hit.
Enemies hit are knocked back and receive 2 stacks of Drench.
Crushing Depths: Enemies under the Drenched effect take an additional 30% water damage for 10 seconds.
Bonus Effect Tsunami Impact:
If five or more enemies are hit by Abyssal Cascade, it triggers a Tsunami Impact, dealing 400% water damage to all enemies in a secondary wave.
Boss Effect:
If the target is a boss or elite, Abyssal Cascade applies Armor Fracture, reducing their defense by 30% for 10 seconds.
Mana Cost: 1400
Cooldown: 50 Seconds]
First Skill: Abyssal Cascade.

Broken immediately noticed that this was a combination of his two previous AoE skills. The new skill created a powerful cascade of water and abyssal energy, devastating all enemies within a wide radius.

[ Abyssal Tideboar - Herald of the Storm (Active Evolved Boar Spirit): Summon the Abyssal Tideboar, a mythical beast that charges across the battlefield with the force of a tsunami. This mighty boar now embodies the spirit of the storm, devastating both
groups of enemies and bosses alike.
Effect:
The Abyssal Tideboar charges forward in a torrent of water, dealing 1,200% physical damage and 600% water elemental damage to all enemies in its path.
Boss Focus: Upon hitting a boss or elite enemy, the Tideboar performs a Crashing Headbutt, dealing 2,000% damage and applying Armor Fracture, reducing the target's defense by 40%
for 10 seconds.
Storm Aura:
The Tideboar emits a storm aura, dealing 400% water damage per second to nearby enemies and knocking back smaller foes.
Mana Cost: 1000
Cooldown: 40 Seconds
Duration: 25 Seconds]
Next Skill: Abyssal Tideboar. His old Water Boar skill had evolved into a more aggressive form. The Abyssal Tideboar summoned a massive water beast, charging through enemies with relentless force.
[I Oceanic Blessing - Gift of the Abyss (Enhanced Passive):
Wrap yourself in the ocean's protection, granting:
50% Defense Ignore
40% Fire Resistance
Immunity to Water Damage
Bonus Effect:
Tidal Surge: Every 3rd basic attack summons two water spears, each dealing 250% water damage and slowing the target.
Blessing of the Abyss: Each attack has a 20% chance to summon a second spear, dealing double damage.]

Next Passive: Oceanic Blessing. It was still the same passive skill from the previous version, but now its single-target damage output was significantly boosted. His single-target attacks would deal massive damage, making him far more lethal against powerful bosses and elite monsters.
[X Abyssal Spear - Piercing Spear of the Abyss (Active Single-Target Finisher Skill):
Focus the spear's chaotic water energy into a devastating single-target thrust, piercing through armor and trapping the target in a Water Prison.
Effect:
Deals 800% physical damage and 500% water elemental damage to a single target.
If the target is Drenched, the damage is doubled.
Applies Water Prison for 5 seconds, immobilizing the target and dealing 15% of their max HP as water damage over time.
Water Prison Effect:
While trapped, the target's attack and movement speed are reduced by 50%, and they cannot cast spells or use skills.
Mana Cost: 1400
Cooldown: 35 Seconds]
[User Restriction: Level 300 or higher
1200 Strength
Master Spear Expertise]
Final Skill: Abyssal Spear. This new skill caught his attention immediately. Unlike the
Legendary-grade version, which focused heavily on AoE attacks, the Mythic-grade spear had a perfect balance between AoE and single-target damage.
Abyssal Spear unleashed a concentrated, explosive strike of water, aimed directly at a single target to deal devastating damage.
Broken quickly summarized the skills in his mind, keeping his focus on the key details:
Abyssal Cascade - AoE: Summons a massive tidal wave that deals heavy damage to all enemies in its path and applies Drench.
What is Drench?
Abyssal Tideboar - AoE + Boss Killer: Summons a mythical water boar that charges through enemies, dealing massive damage and applying boss-specific debuffs to weaken stronger opponents.
Oceanic Blessing - Passive Buff: Provides defense ignore, fire resistance, and bonus water spear attacks that automatically target enemies during combat.
Abyssal Spear - Single-Target Finisher: A high-damage thrust that traps the target in a Water
Prison, immobilizing them for a few seconds and dealing continuous water damage. Broken smirked as he finished going over the skills.
"This weapon really covers everything-AoE, boss damage, single-target finishing moves, and debuffs. Perfect."
However, before he could fully process everything, another notification popped up in front of him.
[The upgrade process from Queen Gaia has been completed.]

chapters.title: Chapter 718: Goddess of the Verdant Eclipse
paragraphs: Notifications kept popping up in front of Broken's vision, overwhelming him with updates. Completing the quest had clearly triggered several extraordinary achievements.
Focalor, meanwhile, was still busy with his villainous monologue.
Without paying him much attention, Broken quickly skimmed through the notifications, reviewing the key rewards as fast as he could.
[An incredible feat has been achieved! You are the first player to successfully upgrade a Legendary-grade Weapon to +18 Mythic-grade weapon.]
[You have unlocked the achievement: "Bearer of the Abyss."]
[Title Unlocked: "Bearer of the Abyss"]
[Title Effects: Spear's Abyssal Mastery - Grants +5% Damage with all spears. Increases Critical Rate by +5% when wielding a Mythic-grade spear.]
5% spear damage and 5% critical rate up?! This is insane! Super insane!
Broken grinned as he skimmed through the next reward.
[New Passive Skill Unlocked: "Enhancer's Gift."]
[+5% Success Rate when upgrading Legendary or Mythic-grade items. Reduced durability loss for Mythic-grade weapons during battle.]
[You have gained the following rewards: +30 Stat Points, +5 Luck Points, +5 Charisma Points.]
Okay, this one's decent too. Reducing durability loss when using a Mythic-grade weapon? That'll save me tons of materials for repairs.
The stat bonuses caught his eye next. Extra stat points? Always welcome.
But then he saw the last part- +5 Luck and +5 Charisma.
"Insane," he muttered. "Who even gets that kind of boost?"
Then his gaze landed on the final reward.
[Cosmetic Item Unlocked: Abyssal Crown]

[A mystical headpiece forged from the essence of the Abyss, adorned with dark blue water tendrils and glowing ethereal runes. The crown resonates with Mythic-grade weapons, empowering the wearer in both combat and diplomacy.]
[Effects: Mythic Resonance - Boosts weapon skill damage by 5% and attack speed by 5% when a Mythic-grade weapon is equipped.]
[Effects: Abyssal Influence - Improves NPC favorability with sea-based factions.]
[Effects: Passive Regeneration - Restores 1% Health and Mana every 5 seconds when near water sources.]
And the next reward was... Abyssal Crown (Cosmetic).
It wasn't just for show. The description made that clear. When paired with a Mythic-grade weapon, the effects were incredible.
Broken stared at the item, smirking to himself.
"This thing's practically forcing me to use it every time I wield the Abyssal Wavebreaker
Spear," he muttered. "Well, no complaints here."
That's a total of 10% attack increase! Plus, improved favorability with sea-based factions and passive health regeneration?! This is absolutely insane!
Looks like this spear just became a whole lot deadlier.
[Weapon Transformation Complete: Your Wavebreaker Spear has evolved into Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear (Mythic-grade).]
[Congratulations! Your name will be engraved forever in the legends of Immortal Legacy as the first player to wield a Mythic-grade weapon.]

Broken pulled out the Abyssal Crown from his inventory. It was a headpiece, more like a crown. Flowing dark blue tendrils shimmered along its edges, moving like living waves. Glowing runes were etched across the crown.
Without hesitation, he placed the headgear on his head, feeling a surge of power flow through him.
Next, he summoned his newly upgraded weapon-the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear. Its form hadn't changed drastically. It still had three prongs, resembling a trident more than a spear.
He spun the weapon expertly in his hands, feeling the boost of energy coursing through him. Who cares if it looks like a trident? The system named it a spear, so that's what it is.
His condition had fully recovered. His skills had reset, and his cooldowns were gone.
Broken gripped the spear tighter, his gaze sharp. He knew what he had to do.
It was time to summon the Golden Paragon once more.
However, before he could fully process everything, another notification popped up in front of him.
[The upgrade process from Queen Gaia has been completed.]
"Seriously?!"
Broken was still trying to process the flood of notifications. And now-another upgrade?
No complaints though.
[Queen Gaia's Fate Ring has been upgraded to Legendary Grade.]
Legendary Grade!

[Queen Gaia can now manifest in the physical world at will, appearing beside the summoner without needing to activate her full power. However, her full abilities remain locked to the ring's cooldown and duration.]

[Queen Gaia has evolved into Queen Gaia, Goddess of the Verdant Eclipse. The infusion of Gremory's Named Demon Soul Stone has permanently altered her nature, intertwining her essence with shadow and blood magic.]

[Gaia's appearance has changed: her cloak of vines and flowers is now entwined with shadowy tendrils and crimson blooms, and her eyes reflect both the light of dawn and dusk. Her aura carries the duality of life and death, embodying both creation and destruction.]
[Queen Gaia's personality has shifted. While still wise and protective, she now exudes a darker and more commanding presence.]

[All Queen Gaia summoned creatures have evolved into Legendary Grade forms, gaining shadow and blood magic influences. These beasts now act autonomously and adapt to battle situations, becoming more dangerous over time.]
Broken felt a faint vibration from the ring on his hand. He glanced down and noticed shadowy energy softly glowing along the intricate patterns on the ring.
Not only had Gaia been upgraded to Legendary-grade, but so had the ring that housed her essence.
Broken hadn't expected the influence of the Gremory Soul Stone to be this significant. It had completely reshaped Gaia - her abilities, her form, even her grade.

When he thought about it, this was undeniably an extraordinary upgrade. But that was to be expected. After all, a Soul Stone from a Named Demon wasn't something one could obtain easily. These stones were extremely rare, and each carried the essence of a powerful, unique demon.
Still, the thought lingered in his mind.
If he could obtain more Named Demon Soul Stones, he could potentially upgrade his other Spirit Beasts to entirely new levels. The possibilities were endless.

But there was a nagging worry beneath his excitement. Gaia's upgrade had taken her far from her natural elements. Her nature-based, life-giving energy now intertwined with something darker shadow and blood.
Wouldn't mixing too many random elements create something unstable? Something chaotic?
He frowned at the thought, but quickly reminded himself that Gaia hadn't been forced into this. She had agreed to consume the Gremory Soul Stone herself.
This was her choice. She knew what she was doing.
Even so, he couldn't shake the feeling that the line between growth and corruption was getting thinner with every step forward.
So... Now what? She can manifest anytime she wants? Like Polly?
Then, suddenly-
A figure appeared at his right side. Broken instinctively turned, and his gaze landed on a woman standing beside him.

Her ivy-like hair flowed gently, the tips fading into a shadowy mist. She wore a cloak of vines, and a thorny halo encircled her head. Dark veins pulsed through her left arm, while twisted trees and glowing plants hovered around her.
The woman tilted her head, her eyes locking onto his.
"Hi, Master..."
"So now you can just show up whenever you want? Congrats."
The woman smiled softly. "Yes, that's right. I can control my own appearance now. But unfortunately, most of my abilities are still locked... unless you use the skill tied to your ring.'
Broken nodded. "I got it."
Without wasting time, Broken quickly checked the new upgrade on his ring.
[Queen Gaia's Fate Ring]
[Grade: Legendary]

sentences.text: Notifications kept popping up in front of Broken's vision, overwhelming him with updates.
Completing the quest had clearly triggered several extraordinary achievements.
Focalor, meanwhile, was still busy with his villainous monologue.
Without paying him much attention, Broken quickly skimmed through the notifications, reviewing the key rewards as fast as he could.
[An incredible feat has been achieved!
You are the first player to successfully upgrade a Legendary-grade Weapon to +18 Mythic-grade weapon.]
[You have unlocked the achievement: "Bearer of the Abyss."]
[Title Unlocked: "Bearer of the Abyss"]
[Title Effects: Spear's Abyssal Mastery - Grants +5% Damage with all spears.
Increases Critical Rate by +5% when wielding a Mythic-grade spear.]
5% spear damage and 5% critical rate up?!
This is insane!
Super insane!
Broken grinned as he skimmed through the next reward.
[New Passive Skill Unlocked: "Enhancer's Gift."]
[+5% Success Rate when upgrading Legendary or Mythic-grade items.
Reduced durability loss for Mythic-grade weapons during battle.]
[You have gained the following rewards: +30 Stat Points, +5 Luck Points, +5 Charisma Points.]
Okay, this one's decent too.
Reducing durability loss when using a Mythic-grade weapon?
That'll save me tons of materials for repairs.
The stat bonuses caught his eye next.
Extra stat points?
Always welcome.
But then he saw the last part- +5 Luck and +5 Charisma.
"Insane," he muttered.
"Who even gets that kind of boost?"
Then his gaze landed on the final reward.
[Cosmetic Item Unlocked: Abyssal Crown]
[A mystical headpiece forged from the essence of the Abyss, adorned with dark blue water tendrils and glowing ethereal runes.
The crown resonates with Mythic-grade weapons, empowering the wearer in both combat and diplomacy.]
[Effects: Mythic Resonance - Boosts weapon skill damage by 5% and attack speed by 5% when a Mythic-grade weapon is equipped.]
[Effects: Abyssal Influence - Improves NPC favorability with sea-based factions.]
[Effects: Passive Regeneration - Restores 1% Health and Mana every 5 seconds when near water sources.]
And the next reward was...
Abyssal Crown (Cosmetic).
It wasn't just for show.
The description made that clear.
When paired with a Mythic-grade weapon, the effects were incredible.
Broken stared at the item, smirking to himself.
"This thing's practically forcing me to use it every time I wield the Abyssal Wavebreaker
Spear," he muttered.
"Well, no complaints here."
That's a total of 10% attack increase!
Plus, improved favorability with sea-based factions and passive health regeneration?!
This is absolutely insane!
Looks like this spear just became a whole lot deadlier.
[Weapon Transformation Complete: Your Wavebreaker Spear has evolved into Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear (Mythic-grade).]
[Congratulations!
Your name will be engraved forever in the legends of Immortal Legacy as the first player to wield a Mythic-grade weapon.]
Broken pulled out the Abyssal Crown from his inventory.
It was a headpiece, more like a crown.
Flowing dark blue tendrils shimmered along its edges, moving like living waves.
Glowing runes were etched across the crown.
Without hesitation, he placed the headgear on his head, feeling a surge of power flow through him.
Next, he summoned his newly upgraded weapon-the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear.
Its form hadn't changed drastically.
It still had three prongs, resembling a trident more than a spear.
He spun the weapon expertly in his hands, feeling the boost of energy coursing through him.
Who cares if it looks like a trident?
The system named it a spear, so that's what it is.
His condition had fully recovered.
His skills had reset, and his cooldowns were gone.
Broken gripped the spear tighter, his gaze sharp.
He knew what he had to do.
It was time to summon the Golden Paragon once more.
However, before he could fully process everything, another notification popped up in front of him.
[The upgrade process from Queen Gaia has been completed.]
"Seriously?!"
Broken was still trying to process the flood of notifications.
And now-another upgrade?
No complaints though.
[Queen Gaia's Fate Ring has been upgraded to Legendary Grade.]
Legendary Grade!
[Queen Gaia can now manifest in the physical world at will, appearing beside the summoner without needing to activate her full power.
However, her full abilities remain locked to the ring's cooldown and duration.]
[Queen Gaia has evolved into Queen Gaia, Goddess of the Verdant Eclipse.
The infusion of Gremory's Named Demon Soul Stone has permanently altered her nature, intertwining her essence with shadow and blood magic.]
[Gaia's appearance has changed: her cloak of vines and flowers is now entwined with shadowy tendrils and crimson blooms, and her eyes reflect both the light of dawn and dusk.
Her aura carries the duality of life and death, embodying both creation and destruction.]
[Queen Gaia's personality has shifted.
While still wise and protective, she now exudes a darker and more commanding presence.]
[All Queen Gaia summoned creatures have evolved into Legendary Grade forms, gaining shadow and blood magic influences.
These beasts now act autonomously and adapt to battle situations, becoming more dangerous over time.]
Broken felt a faint vibration from the ring on his hand.
He glanced down and noticed shadowy energy softly glowing along the intricate patterns on the ring.
Not only had Gaia been upgraded to Legendary-grade, but so had the ring that housed her essence.
Broken hadn't expected the influence of the Gremory Soul Stone to be this significant.
It had completely reshaped Gaia - her abilities, her form, even her grade.
When he thought about it, this was undeniably an extraordinary upgrade.
But that was to be expected.
After all, a Soul Stone from a Named Demon wasn't something one could obtain easily.
These stones were extremely rare, and each carried the essence of a powerful, unique demon.
Still, the thought lingered in his mind.
If he could obtain more Named Demon Soul Stones, he could potentially upgrade his other Spirit Beasts to entirely new levels.
The possibilities were endless.
But there was a nagging worry beneath his excitement.
Gaia's upgrade had taken her far from her natural elements.
Her nature-based, life-giving energy now intertwined with something darker shadow and blood.
Wouldn't mixing too many random elements create something unstable?
Something chaotic?
He frowned at the thought, but quickly reminded himself that Gaia hadn't been forced into this.
She had agreed to consume the Gremory Soul Stone herself.
This was her choice.
She knew what she was doing.
Even so, he couldn't shake the feeling that the line between growth and corruption was getting thinner with every step forward.
So...
Now what?
She can manifest anytime she wants?
Like Polly?
Then, suddenly-
A figure appeared at his right side.
Broken instinctively turned, and his gaze landed on a woman standing beside him.
Her ivy-like hair flowed gently, the tips fading into a shadowy mist.
She wore a cloak of vines, and a thorny halo encircled her head.
Dark veins pulsed through her left arm, while twisted trees and glowing plants hovered around her.
The woman tilted her head, her eyes locking onto his.
"Hi, Master..."
"So now you can just show up whenever you want?
Congrats."
The woman smiled softly.
"Yes, that's right.
I can control my own appearance now.
But unfortunately, most of my abilities are still locked... unless you use the skill tied to your ring.'
Broken nodded.
"I got it."
Without wasting time, Broken quickly checked the new upgrade on his ring.
[Queen Gaia's Fate Ring]
[Grade: Legendary]

chapters.title: Chapter 719: Verdant Eclipse Manifestation (Info Dump Alert!)
paragraphs: [Queen Gaia's Fate Ring] [Grade: Legendary]
[Durability: 100/100]
[Weight: 420]

[The Fate Ring holds the spirit of Queen Gaia, Goddess of the Verdant Eclipse, an eternal guardian of nature and rebirth. The wearer of this ring is bound to Gaia through a Bloodshadow Covenant, allowing her to manifest in the physical world at will. While her full power requires activation, Gaia can act independently when present, offering her wisdom, guidance, and unique abilities.]
[Skills:]
[Verdant Eclipse Manifestation:

Allows the wearer to activate Queen Gaia's full power, unleashing her devastating skills and abilities for a limited time. Gaia will fight alongside the wearer autonomously when summoned, making her a powerful ally both in battle and in strategic situations.
Cooldown: 60 minutes
Duration: 10 minutes]
[Herald of the Eclipse:

Allows the summoner to call forth two Legendary-grade creatures simultaneously from Gaia's Eternal Court. Summoning a third creature will replace the oldest summon. The beasts will now remain active for up to 15 minutes and can act independently, following both Gaia's and the summoner's commands.
Mana Cost: 350
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Duration: 15 minutes]
[User Restriction: Have an established contract with Queen Gaia.]

Verdant Eclipse Manifestation. At first glance, the concept didn't seem all that different. Gaia could still unleash her full range of abilities, limited by a sixty-minute cooldown and ten- minute active duration.
But something stood out-this time, she could manifest her physical form. Even so, Broken could tell that she wasn't at full combat capacity in this state. There were limitations.
Yet, that wasn't what made him stop and think.
What really caught his attention was the duration.
Ten full minutes.
Previously, she'd barely managed to stay summoned for five-a fleeting presence that rarely gave them enough time to turn the tide. But now?
Now, she could make an impact.
And it didn't stop there.
The second skill, Herald of the Eclipse, had evolved from the previous version.
Now, he could summon two beasts at once.
Two manifestations of Gaia's will, unleashed together, fighting by his side.
But it wasn't just the numbers that caught his attention - the beasts had also been transformed to Legendary-grade.
He knew he'd have to analyze their changes carefully. There was no telling how different their abilities had become.
Yet, considering Gaia herself had undergone a transformation, it was clear those beasts had likely chosen new forms as well.
Whatever they were now, they were no longer the creatures he once knew.
And the best part?
They no longer needed his constant direction. Gaia could control them directly, freeing Broken to focus on the bigger picture.
It was a massive upgrade. One that would shift the flow of any battle in his favor.
For the first time, Broken didn't feel like he was carrying the weight of her power alone. Gaia wasn't just lending her abilities anymore-she was commanding them.
He exhaled slowly, a grin tugging at the corner of his mouth.

There was too much information laid out in front of him. Even with just a quick scan, it felt overwhelming. Yet, thanks to his accelerated thought process, he managed to piece everything together in an instant.
He didn't need to dig into every detail-just grasping the broader strokes was enough to get a sense of what had changed.
Next, his attention shifted to the upgraded skills of Queen Gaia.
Whatever this new version of her was, one thing was certain-it was no longer the same Gaia he once knew.
[Name: Queen Gaia ]
[Grade: Legendary]
[Race: Goddess of the Verdant Eclipse]
[Skills - 3]
[Bloodbloom Rebirth (Support Skill)
Effect:
Heals the summoner for a large amount over time.
Enemies within a large radius are afflicted with Blood Leech, draining their health and converting it into healing for the summoner.
If any allied beast or summon dies during this time, Gaia can resurrect them as shadow- bloom spirits for the remainder of the battle.]

The first skill, Bloodbloom Rebirth, wasn't too different from before. However, this time it came with a new effect: Blood Leech, allowing Gaia to drain health from nearby enemies. A subtle but deadly upgrade.
But there was more.
And this part? Absolutely insane.
If any of his allied beasts died while the skill was active, they wouldn't stay down. Instead, they would resurrect as Shadow-Bloom Spirits.
Broken's mind immediately went to the possibilities.
"Wait... does this apply to all summons? Like Jovina's beast if they're fighting alongside me?"
If so, that meant every summon on the battlefield could be revived under Gaia's influence.
Really? He frowned, running through the implications.
That kind of ability was completely overpowered.
Turning fallen beasts into independent, spectral creatures capable of continuing the fight? It wasn't just a powerful skill - it was battlefield domination.
[Eclipse Vines of Despair (Attack Skill):
Summons 15 shadow-infused vines that entangle enemies, absorb elemental damage, and retaliate with shadow energy.
The vines emit shadow spores, which slow enemies and drain mana over time.
Enemies trapped for more than 10 seconds are afflicted with Blood Curse, reducing their defense by 15%.]
The next skill, Eclipse Vines of Despair.
It was still similar to the previous version, but there was one major difference-these weren't just ordinary massive vines anymore. They were shadow-infused vines.
Interesting.
The vines could lash out, restrain enemies, and even reduce their defense. But the real kicker?
They could also drain mana.
"Wait... they drain mana?"
This was no ordinary crowd control. It was brutal, relentless, and utterly OP.
Hell. They just keep making her scarier.
[Eternal Court of the Eclipse:
"From the shadows of nature's heart, the beasts of the Verdant Eclipse emerge to protect and destroy."

Summon creatures from Queen Gaia's Eternal Court, each representing an aspect of nature infused with shadow and blood magic. The beasts act autonomously in battle, adapting to the environment and enemy tactics. They can perform offensive, defensive, and utility roles, depending on the situation.]
And finally, the last skill - Eternal Court of the Eclipse.
This was the big one.
A summoning skill that called forth all twelve of Gaia's beasts at once.
There wasn't anything particularly flashy about the skill itself. The real question wasn't about the summon—it was about what those newly upgraded beasts could do.
He couldn't help but smirk.
The real spectacle isn't the skill. It's how those beasts will perform now.
And with their numbers?
Well, quantity and quality were clearly on his side.
"So, are you done studying the upgrades you've received?" Focalor's voice echoed from the far end of the area.
"Yeah," Broken responded. "You're surely kind enough to let me take my time with it."
"Well, I get where you're coming from. I've also received several upgrades to my own skills recently. And trust me, I needed time to figure them out too."
"Good, then. I hope you can make the most of them." Broken kept his tone casual.
But Focalor's eyes narrowed slightly. "Well, I'm not so sure I need to use all my skills properly. See... you lot? You're still no different from before."
"That's your opinion." Broken shrugged it off.
He was ready. Ready to summon everything.
But then... something shifted.
From his right, Gaia suddenly stepped back. Slowly. Quietly.
"Gaia?!" His head snapped toward her.
And then-he felt it.
Someone else stepped forward.
From the shadows beside him, Princess Alora emerged.
But it wasn't just her.
Behind her, floating ominously in the air, was something far more imposing.
It was-
It was the fucking Golden Paragon!

A majestic figure adorned in white and gold armor. The fabric draping from her shoulders moved like silk caught in an eternal breeze. Her crimson hair flowed behind her, a striking contrast to her pristine armor and the ornate golden crown on her head, shining like a radiant halo.
Her face was concealed behind a smooth, porcelain mask, save for her red lips-the only feature visible, frozen in a serene expression that somehow felt more intimidating than any glare.
And in her hand?
A golden sword, gleaming with divine light.
"Surely, you wouldn't dare start the fight without me, right?" Alora said, her lips curling into a faint smile.
Broken's eyes narrowed. "You... successfully activated the Golden Paragon?"
"I did."
Broken exhaled slowly, shifting his stance. His grip on the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear tightened.
[Summon Golden Paragon (Conditional Active Skill) activated.]
Behind him, his own Golden Paragon materialized - a towering figure clad in radiant armor.
"Let's start the final battle," he said. "And yes... this will truly be the final one."

chapters.title: Chapter 720 - Eternal Court of the Eclipse
paragraphs: The final moment.
This was it — the final battle.
It wasn't just another skirmish or challenge to overcome.
This was everything.
And it had to end, right here, right now!
Ivana, Broken, and Alora stood side by side, each of them prepared in their own way.

Ivana hovered slightly above the ground, her wings beating lightly behind her. What stood out the most was the absence of her shield. The once unshakable guardian now chose to fight without it, her posture lighter, more agile.
Craft any skill she wants, huh?
His gaze shifted to his own stance — the weight of the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear resting firmly in his grip.
Behind him, his Golden Paragon floated silently. The ethereal figure radiated divine energy, yet something was different.
No wings.
Broken frowned slightly. He knew why. The blessing from SexyGrill — the one that had once granted him flight — wasn't active. Without it, he couldn't take to the skies like before.
He tightened his grip on the spear.
Then there was Alora.
She stood to his right. Her Golden Paragon mirrored hers — radiant and majestic, hovering like a silent guardian at her back.
They didn't speak.
There was no need.
This was it. The final battle was about to begin.
Broken shot forward at incredible speed.
The rush of energy coursing through him was undeniable. His speed, his reflexes, his strength — everything felt boosted.
From a distance, Focalor watched with a faint smirk. The demon wasn't fazed.

In an instant, Broken closed the gap. He lunged straight at Focalor, his spear striking with precise, relentless attacks — a thrust, a sweep, another strike. Suddenly, two water spears materialized and attacked from both sides, converging on the demon.
But Focalor countered.
With a single motion, he unleashed a blast of force, knocking Broken backward.
Then, dozens of magic circles formed behind him. Without hesitation, they erupted in a barrage of magical explosions.
Before the blasts could hit, Alora dashed forward, her sword gleaming gold.
Slice. Slice. Slice.
She cut through each blast, the explosions bursting harmlessly in the air.
Meanwhile, Ivana swooped in from behind. Her wings folded briefly before she surged toward Focalor's back, claws poised to strike.
But the demon was faster.
Focalor spun around, summoning a magic shield that blocked all of Ivana's attacks. Sparks flew as her claws scraped against the barrier, but it held firm.
With a swift motion, he grabbed both of her wrists, locking her in place.
"Nice try. Weak," Focalor sneered, tightening his grip.
But before he could finish his taunt—
Ivana opened her mouth.
A second later, a deafening scream tore through the air.
It wasn't just a sound. It was a wave of raw energy, blasting straight into Focalor's chest. The impact sent him flying backward, his grip breaking instantly.
"That's one hell of a scream!" Broken muttered.
[Verdant Eclipse Manifestation (Active Skill) Activated.]
"Gaia, your turn!" he shouted.

From her distant position, Gaia floated forward, her form shrouded in mist and shadow. As she approached, she raised both hands, and massive shadow-infused vines erupted from the ground. The thorn-covered tendrils twisted and lashed toward Focalor, aiming to bind him in place.
"You think pathetic tricks like this can hold me?!" Focalor roared, smashing through the vines with sheer force.
The tendrils kept coming, relentless, but he tore them apart with ease.
Broken shot forward again, spear in hand, closing the distance.
At the same time, Alora darted in from the opposite side.

The two moved in perfect sync — taking turns attacking, their weapons striking at Focalor's defenses from different angles. When one pulled back, the other would press in. Close-range fighters through and through, their strikes flowed like a deadly dance, forcing Focalor to stay on the defensive.
Occasionally, their attacks aligned perfectly, and several blows landed true, tearing into their enemy.
Broken gritted his teeth, focusing on his next strike, when his gaze caught movement in the distance.
SexyGrill and SexyBloom were sprinting toward them, closing the gap fast.
Broken's chest heaved as he readied another attack, but then—
SexyGrill raised her hand.
Her blessing activated in an instant, the familiar surge of divine power rushing through his body.
His senses sharpened. His strength surged. And most importantly?
His wings returned.
"Alright... now we're talking!" Broken launched into the air as he prepared for another round. "Let's finish this!"
[Eternal Court of the Eclipse (Conditional Active Skill) Activated.]
This is it.
The time to unleash all twelve of Gaia's beasts.
The beasts appeared one by one around them.
Broken immediately noticed something — their names had changed. Not entirely different, but more like upgraded versions of what they were before.
Their appearances, too, were refined and far more menacing.
They weren't the same beasts he once knew. They were stronger. Deadlier.
[Abyss Thorn Ox]

The ox now had a much larger form, almost twice its original size. Its body was covered in thick bark armor, layered with sharp thorns jutting out at deadly angles. Dark crimson veins pulsed beneath the bark, and a shadowy mist seeped from its massive hooves with each step.
[Ironhide Truffle Boar]
A bulky boar with thick, cracked bark plates shielding its entire body. The armor was reinforced with patches of dark moss and glowing crimson fungi.
[Eclipse Tiger Lily]

The tiger still carried lily flowers on its body, but they had changed color to deep purple and crimson. In the darkness, its flowers gave off a haunting glow, and when it moved, it left behind faint, glowing trails — like a phantom drifting through the night.
[Mossguard Goat]
A nimble goat with moss-covered fur and curved horns wrapped in thorny vines. Despite its smaller size, it gave off a feral, unpredictable vibe, as if it could ram through anything in its path.
[Barkshade Hound]
Not too different from its previous form, except now its eyes burned with an eerie glow and its body bristled with more thorns.
[Infernal Chili Rooster]
An intimidating rooster wreathed in dark flames, with its feathers glowing like embers.
[Creeper Demon Monkey]
This wild monkey moved with chaotic energy, its glowing eyes darting around madly. It leapt and twisted with erratic movements. There was an unsettling madness to it, as if it thrived in chaos.
[Elder Abyss Dragon Tree]
Still the Chinese dragon kind, but now much longer, its serpentine body winding endlessly. Dark flames danced along its bark-like scales.
[Fernshade Rabbit]
A small rabbit with soft green fur resembling fern leaves. Its appearance hadn't changed much, but its colors had become more vivid, making it stand out more.
[Petal Dusk Charger]
Still a majestic horse, but its appearance had grown darker, with deep, shadowy petals blooming from its body. It looked like a creature born from twilight and dusk, elegant yet haunting.
[Toxic Ivy Rat]
A smaller rat, but more dangerous-looking. Its tail glowed green.
[Vine Eclipse Serpent]
A massive serpent, far larger than before. Its body pulsed with shadow energy, and vines twisted around its body like living armor.
It was clear — no one dared get too close to this battle.
Each attack, each explosion, shook the battlefield with massive force, far more brutal than anything from their previous fights.

Still, a few high-level allies continued to support from a distance. Zeno struck from afar, while Frostedge unleashed massive ice spikes that pierced through the air. Above them, a skeletal dragon spewed black and green flames, raining destruction down from the skies.

Their strikes collided in bursts of magic and energy, Ivana maneuvering with ease, throwing magic spheres from multiple angles as if she could do anything she wanted with her magic.
Meanwhile, Broken focused on controlling the flow of the battle. His Golden Paragon unleashed a crowd control attack, sending Focalor flying back.
Broken's gaze locked onto the demon, and his expression hardened.
It was time.
He took out the Bedrock Breaker and the Golden Bow of Artemis. With precise focus, he drew the bowstring, aiming for the Named Demon.
Seconds passed.
Then— the Bedrock Breaker shot forward.

The projectile flew at blinding speed, hurtling toward Focalor. The demon tried to catch it, his hands snapping up just in time — but the Bedrock Breaker slipped through his grip, grazing his shoulder with a brutal impact.
Boom. Boom. Boom.
Explosions followed as the ground erupted. Smoke and debris filled the air, but Broken didn't slow down.
He gripped the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear, spinning it once in his hand.
With a steady breath, he prepared his next shot.

sentences.text: The final moment.
This was it — the final battle.
It wasn't just another skirmish or challenge to overcome.
This was everything.
And it had to end, right here, right now!
Ivana, Broken, and Alora stood side by side, each of them prepared in their own way.
Ivana hovered slightly above the ground, her wings beating lightly behind her.
What stood out the most was the absence of her shield.
The once unshakable guardian now chose to fight without it, her posture lighter, more agile.
Craft any skill she wants, huh?
His gaze shifted to his own stance — the weight of the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear resting firmly in his grip.
Behind him, his Golden Paragon floated silently.
The ethereal figure radiated divine energy, yet something was different.
No wings.
Broken frowned slightly.
He knew why.
The blessing from SexyGrill — the one that had once granted him flight — wasn't active.
Without it, he couldn't take to the skies like before.
He tightened his grip on the spear.
Then there was Alora.
She stood to his right.
Her Golden Paragon mirrored hers — radiant and majestic, hovering like a silent guardian at her back.
They didn't speak.
There was no need.
This was it.
The final battle was about to begin.
Broken shot forward at incredible speed.
The rush of energy coursing through him was undeniable.
His speed, his reflexes, his strength — everything felt boosted.
From a distance, Focalor watched with a faint smirk.
The demon wasn't fazed.
In an instant, Broken closed the gap.
He lunged straight at Focalor, his spear striking with precise, relentless attacks — a thrust, a sweep, another strike.
Suddenly, two water spears materialized and attacked from both sides, converging on the demon.
But Focalor countered.
With a single motion, he unleashed a blast of force, knocking Broken backward.
Then, dozens of magic circles formed behind him.
Without hesitation, they erupted in a barrage of magical explosions.
Before the blasts could hit, Alora dashed forward, her sword gleaming gold.
Slice.
Slice.
Slice.
She cut through each blast, the explosions bursting harmlessly in the air.
Meanwhile, Ivana swooped in from behind.
Her wings folded briefly before she surged toward Focalor's back, claws poised to strike.
But the demon was faster.
Focalor spun around, summoning a magic shield that blocked all of Ivana's attacks.
Sparks flew as her claws scraped against the barrier, but it held firm.
With a swift motion, he grabbed both of her wrists, locking her in place.
"Nice try.
Weak," Focalor sneered, tightening his grip.
But before he could finish his taunt—
Ivana opened her mouth.
A second later, a deafening scream tore through the air.
It wasn't just a sound.
It was a wave of raw energy, blasting straight into Focalor's chest.
The impact sent him flying backward, his grip breaking instantly.
"That's one hell of a scream!" Broken muttered.
[Verdant Eclipse Manifestation (Active Skill) Activated.]
"Gaia, your turn!" he shouted.
From her distant position, Gaia floated forward, her form shrouded in mist and shadow.
As she approached, she raised both hands, and massive shadow-infused vines erupted from the ground.
The thorn-covered tendrils twisted and lashed toward Focalor, aiming to bind him in place.
"You think pathetic tricks like this can hold me?!" Focalor roared, smashing through the vines with sheer force.
The tendrils kept coming, relentless, but he tore them apart with ease.
Broken shot forward again, spear in hand, closing the distance.
At the same time, Alora darted in from the opposite side.
The two moved in perfect sync — taking turns attacking, their weapons striking at Focalor's defenses from different angles.
When one pulled back, the other would press in.
Close-range fighters through and through, their strikes flowed like a deadly dance, forcing Focalor to stay on the defensive.
Occasionally, their attacks aligned perfectly, and several blows landed true, tearing into their enemy.

SexyGrill and SexyBloom were sprinting toward them, closing the gap fast.
Broken's chest heaved as he readied another attack, but then—
SexyGrill raised her hand.
Her blessing activated in an instant, the familiar surge of divine power rushing through his body.
His senses sharpened.
His strength surged.
And most importantly?
His wings returned.
"Alright... now we're talking!" Broken launched into the air as he prepared for another round.
"Let's finish this!"

Deadlier.

The armor was reinforced with patches of dark moss and glowing crimson fungi.

chapters.title: Chapter 721: One Wing Left
paragraphs: "Tora..." Max sighed softly, grabbing the arm of the man beside her. "I still can't wrap my head around what's happening. This is all too fast. And... Ivana, Princess Alora, and Broken... what happened to them?"
"Well, Max, even I can't give you a detailed explanation," Tora replied. "Because honestly? I don't know why things escalated this quickly."
"No way. You're a member of the Vensalor Guild, right? Can't you at least explain why Ivana now has wings, horns, and... a tail? What even is that? Is she in some kind of demon form?"
Tora shook his head slowly. "No, Max. I'm certain it's something else... but even if it is, I think we'll have to wait until Broken decides to make that information public."

Max clicked her tongue. "I doubt Broken will ever reveal this to the public. But I've seen people speculating already. Some are calling her the Dragon Princess. Others say she's the Greed Champion. I didn't realize there were so many people out there with deep knowledge of Yunatea Lore."
"Well, Max..." Tora glanced away for a moment before sighing. "Once again, I'm going to have to keep my mouth shut."
"I understand your position, Tora."
Suddenly, the sky shifted, turning into a swirling ocean-like expanse overhead.
From the water above, a massive trident-shaped spear with three prongs emerged, descending with terrifying speed, aiming straight for the battlefield below.
"Tora... I'm worried," Max muttered. "Didn't Focalor manage to catch that spear before?"

"Yes, Max, I thought so too," Tora replied, his tone serious. "But Maylock already analyzed this, and even Broken tested it before using the pickaxe. Focalor failed to catch the pickaxe." "So, according to Maylock, this spear attack should succeed too?"
Tora nodded. "That's the theory. Let's hope it holds."
Both of them fell silent, their eyes locked on the distant battlefield as the massive spear hurtled down.
The moment it hit, a colossal wave of water crashed down with it, as if the entire ocean had spilled from the sky.
Max's mouth hung open in shock, and around them, everyone watched in awe. The sheer spectacle of it left the entire crowd breathless.
The battlefield was hidden beneath a vast flood. But they had seen it - the spear had hit its mark.
Just as Maylock predicted, Focalor had failed to stop it. The spear had pierced straight through his chest.
Max shook her head slowly. "I wonder... is Broken the only one capable of pulling off miracles like this? The avatar behind him, the power... even Princess Alora has one too."
"Yes, Max. It's incredible."

Max's eyes narrowed. "And that spear... it looked different, didn't it? Even the animation of the attack was different. That wasn't the same spear from earlier. Wasn't it supposed to be a Legendary-grade spear?"
Tora nodded in agreement. "I thought the same. It was definitely the same spear, but its skills and shape were... different."
"Do you think its grade increased? Could it have become Mythic-grade?"
Tora chuckled softly. "Maybe. Or maybe we're just getting carried away by this battle."
Max exhaled, shaking her head. "Whatever it is... this fight feels like something out of a legend."
The battle raged on, and from a distance, it was clear - the three fighters took turns attacking Focalor with brutal precision.
They continued to monitor and broadcast the fight, though even the camera had to pull back from the sheer intensity of the battle. It was impossible to get too close without risking destruction.
At one point, Ivana struck. Her claws raked repeatedly across Focalor's body, and with a final, devastating blow, she severed his right arm.
"Damn! We made it!" Max yelled. "That's the first major damage we've dealt! Damn you, demon! You're going down tonight!"
"Max, calm down.
"I can't, Tora! This is way too intense."

Tora glanced back at the battlefield. "Look at Princess Alora. She's attacking with perfect precision, alternating with Broken. It's like they're communicating without words. Their coordination is flawless."

Max nodded quickly. "Yes, and Ivana... She's fighting without her shield now. Who would've thought the chef girl from Deadbay could be this powerful? Seriously, those three... they're the center of attention right now."
"With the three of them taking the lead, Zeno, Frostedge, Galactron, and the remaining high- level fighters can attack more freely. They're creating opportunities."
Max grinned. "Yes, I see that. They've become the pillars holding this entire fight together."
The battle raged on, and everyone watching or supporting from a distance could do nothing but throw everything they had and pray there wouldn't be another twist to shatter their hopes.
Every second felt heavier.
Then came a pivotal moment - Broken swung his spear with all his might, the impact slamming Focalor backward. The Named Demon flew across the battlefield, crashing hard.
A deep gash ran across Focalor's chest, dark energy seeping from the wound. Before he could recover, Ivana was already closing in.

She dashed forward, relentless, unleashing skill after skill. Explosions erupted one after another, creating a chaotic storm of light and shadow. The sheer intensity of the attacks made it impossible to see where Focalor was amidst the barrage.
Every passing second felt like eternity. Those watching from afar held their breath, tense and powerless.
They could only hope the battle would end soon- the weight of helplessness crushing them as they witnessed such a monumental clash.
Suddenly, a massive slash cut through the air.
Alora's sword struck true, slicing through Focalor's wings. Several of them tore off, falling to the ground.
Now, he was left with only two wings on his right side and one on his left.
The demon was starting to falter.
Broken shot forward, soaring through the air with his spear in hand. Behind him, his Golden Paragon spread its wings, following closely like a shadow of divine power.
At the same time, Ivana flew in from the left, her eyes locked on the Named Demon.
Without wasting a second, she lunged, her claws slashing rapidly. Each strike unleashed waves of energy that ripped through Focalor's defenses, tearing into his body.
Broken closed in, spinning his spear before delivering a thrust, a sweep, and another strike.
Focalor struggled to block.
"You will never defeat me!" Focalor roared as he dashed away, trying to put distance between himself and the relentless attacks.
But Alora was already there.
She stood in his path, her sword slicing through the air faster than the eye could see.
"You're not going anywhere, Demian!"
Focalor growled, surging toward her with a desperate attack.
Before he could reach her, Ivana dropped from above, crashing into him with enough force to slam him into the ground.
The Named Demon took off again, trying to retreat once more.
But Broken was waiting.
He surged forward. With a swift motion, he unleashed a wave of water energy, the crashing force knocking Focalor back into the ground.
Before the demon could recover, Alora appeared again.
With a blur of movement, her sword struck fast and precise, slicing through Focalor's remaining wings.
By the time she finished, he had only one wing left - a single tattered wing on his right side.
[Heaven's Judgment (Ultimate Active Skill) activated.]

Broken unleashed the Golden Paragon's ultimate skill. The Golden Paragon avatar raised its greatsword high into the air, and a brilliant golden light erupted from the blade. It grew rapidly, transforming into a massive weapon.

With one colossal swing, the greatsword came crashing down, creating a devastating explosion that shattered everything in its path. Focalor was thrown to the ground, reeling under the relentless onslaught.
The brutal attacks had left Focalor grounded- he could no longer fly.
Before he could recover, Ivana struck again, crashing into him with relentless force. The demon tried to block, but the impact sent him flying backward.
Alora dashed in next, her sword flashing in a blur of movement.
"You die tonight, Demian!" she shouted. "Your rebellion, your betrayal! This is the punishment you deserve!"
Despite the continuous onslaught, Focalor laughed.
Even as he was struck and thrown back again and again, he refused to yield. "I'm not done! I haven't lost!"
His voice echoed through the battlefield as he was blasted far into the distance.
Suddenly his wings began to regenerate.
As he tumbled through the air, new wings sprouted from his back!
A faint smile crept across his face.
"I will return..." he began, his voice defiant.
But he never finished the sentence.
Because...
He froze.
His head... slid clean off his shoulders.
And standing behind the Named Demon was Broken.
His spear, still gleaming with power. His strike had been perfect. Precise.
The headless body of Focalor collapsed.
The battle was over.
For sure!

chapters.title: Chapter 722 - The Golden Paragon's Price
paragraphs: Broken stood frozen, gripping his spear tightly.
The entire battle, the endless struggle — it still felt unreal.
And yet, the system notification that appeared before him left no doubt.
They had done it. They had killed Focalor.
Even as the notification lingered in his vision, he dismissed it, shaking his head to clear his thoughts. He scanned his surroundings carefully, making sure there were no more surprises.
Alora was still on her knees, bracing herself with her sword. Her breathing was labored, and the glow of her Golden Paragon began to fade into nothingness.
Moments later, Broken's own Golden Paragon vanished as well.
Nearby, Ivana approached Alora, her dragon wings shrinking and folding back into her body. Without a word, she bent down and helped the princess to her feet.
And then, Ivana pulled Alora into a gentle embrace.

Broken remained standing in place, his chest rising and falling rapidly as the adrenaline continued to course through his body. Slowly, he closed his eyes, letting the rush fade and a quiet calm settle in its place.
In the distance, cheers erupted from all directions.
Victory!
The sound of celebration spread across the battlefield, a chorus of relief and triumph.
Broken opened his eyes, and before he could react, two figures ran toward him.
Both women threw their arms around him, pulling him into a tight embrace.
It was Princess Alora and Ivana.
"Broken... we won," Ivana whispered, her voice trembling with emotion. "We won. We killed the Named Demon. We did it."
Broken nodded, resting his hand gently on the back of Ivana's head. Alora's arms remained wrapped around him, holding him close.
As he glanced around the battlefield, he noticed a few scattered demons still lingering in the distance. The weaker creatures hadn't been wiped out yet, but the tides had turned.
The remaining forces were being hunted down and crushed.
The battle wasn't entirely over, but the real threat was gone.
Broken took a deep breath.
The main enemy was destroyed. Victory was finally theirs.
He noticed several figures approaching in the distance — Fokil, Zeno, and the remaining members of the Vensalor Guild.
Broken released his embrace from the two women.
As they drew closer, Alora walked toward Zeno, while Ivana stepped forward to greet Fokil.
Around them, the air was filled with cheers, shouts of triumph, and the unmistakable energy of victory.
Soon after, Maylock appeared by Broken's side, patting his shoulder gently.
Broken turned to him. "Thanks for coming."
Maylock shook his head slowly. "I only did what I had to do."
Broken nodded in quiet acknowledgment before his gaze shifted again — toward Ivana.
"There's still much to be done after this," Maylock said, breaking the brief silence.
He continued. "Rebuilding the kingdom, the Princess's ascension to the throne, and..."
Broken glanced at him. "And?"
Maylock stepped closer, his lips curling into a faint smile. "Celebrating your wedding."
Broken blinked, his brows furrowed. "You know about that?"
Maylock chuckled softly. "Where else do you think you got the Golden Paragon from, if not through the Harem Ring?"
Broken let out a low sigh, shaking his head with a faint grin. "That's a unique way to name the ring King Elandorr gave me."
Maylock smirked. "Fitting, though."
As their conversation drew to a close, the battle was finally over. Truly over.
The remaining knights and troops wasted no time, immediately moving to clear the battlefield, organize the forces, and ensure no demons remained.
Meanwhile, Princess Alora had already joined the other knights, issuing orders to the higher-ranking officials to divide tasks and stabilize the situation.
The war might have ended, but the work of rebuilding had only just begun.

Broken and Maylock, followed by the remaining members of the Vensalor Guild, walked together into the city. Ivana and Fokil were right behind them, the group moving through the streets that were slowly settling after the battle.
"How much longer is your login time, Broken?" Maylock asked, glancing at him.
Broken checked his interface. "Ten hours Yunatea Time."
Maylock nodded. "I can stay. I'll wait for the others to log back in, then we can divide tasks."
"You sure you don't need to log out soon?"
"Maybe." Maylock shrugged, then sighed with a soft smile. "But honestly? This game makes me feel nostalgic."
"You know everyone misses you too, right?"
Maylock turned to him with a raised eyebrow. "Because you're all struggling without me in the guild?"
Broken smirked. "I won't deny that your absence left a huge void. Your brilliance is hard to replace." He paused before adding softly, "But more than that... we've been worried about you."
Maylock slowed his pace, then suddenly threw an arm around Broken's shoulders.
"That's so sweet, you know," he teased.
Then they laughed quietly.
Broken and the others made their way into one of the remaining intact rooms in the castle. There were urgent matters to discuss, and this was the best place to do it.
Inside the room sat Maylock, Freya, RememberMe, Pussycat, and Forev.
The moment they sat around the round table, RememberMe was the first to react.
"Oh damn, Broken!" he blurted out, grinning as he said. "You actually made your marriage to Princess Alora official?!"
He laughed and gave Broken a hard slap on the back.
"That's totally unexpected, right?" Pussycat chimed in with a smirk. "Getting a chance like that, at a time like this?
"But it was a smart move," Forev added with a nod. "Especially since that marriage secured him the Golden Paragon."
The atmosphere grew more relaxed as the banter continued, but Maylock suddenly shifted the tone with a question.
"Are you okay with it, Freya?" he asked, tilting his head slightly.
The entire room fell silent.
Everyone turned to Freya.
Her eyes narrowed, confused. "Why me?!"
Maylock chuckled. "Oh, what a polite response."
"You shouldn't even be online, Maylock!"
RememberMe couldn't resist jumping in. "Yeah, Freya, relax. You can still marry Broken outside the game, hahaha!"
"Shut up!" Freya snapped.
The room erupted into laughter, breaking the tension.
Freya crossed her arms. "Idiots..."
Freya turned her gaze toward Broken, narrowing her eyes. "What?"
"No..." Broken shook his head and smiled faintly. "I didn't say anything."
"I hate your smile."
The room burst into laughter, the tension breaking for a brief moment.
For a while, they continued chatting and laughing, letting the lingering euphoria of victory fill the space. After all, it had been a long, grueling war.
Even if the entire battle had only lasted a few hours in real time, the emotional weight of it felt immense.
They had faced four Named Demons, each bringing chaos and destruction, forcing everyone to push their limits just to survive.
Then, there was the appearance of the higher-ranking Named Demon. The death of King Elandorr. And finally, Demian's transformation into the new Named Demon.
No one could tell how long it would take for the Dissidia Kingdom to recover from the devastation.
But one thing was certain — the kingdom needed a new ruler. And the ascension of the next monarch would have to happen soon.
The laughter faded. Silence returned to the room.
It was Maylock who broke it.
"I have a few things I want to discuss," he said.
Everyone's attention shifted toward him.
"First, we need to address the most critical issue." He paused for a moment, his gaze steady. "The Sword of Dissidia."
Broken nodded slowly.
They'd finally reached this point.
The moment he'd been haunted by ever since he received that quest from King Elandorr.
The moment he'd be face-to-face with the truth behind the sword.

chapters.title: Chapter 723: Make Dissidia Great Again
paragraphs: "I'm sure this will be quite a long and important discussion..." Broken began with a serious tone. "So, I'm inviting all members of the Vensalor Guild to join us for this."
In the same room, floating screens materialized above several empty chairs, displaying the avatars of each member joining the meeting.
"Broken, congratulations! You did it!" Elincia was the first to shout.
"Hahaha! Too bad I wasn't there for the final moments," Booba chimed in.
"Damn it! I lost my ring again!" Melliandra groaned, drawing laughter from the group.
"But seriously, we need to throw a huge party for Broken and Queen Alora's official wedding ceremony!" Jovina added with a grin.
More laughter followed.
"You truly are a man, Broken. Khi khi khi."
Once everyone had gathered, including Tora, who joined a little later, the atmosphere in the room shifted to a more serious tone. The discussion was ready to begin.
Broken took a moment before speaking. "I'd like to give anyone here the chance to speak first."
Maylock gave a slight nod. "You're certainly humble to let others go first in something this important."
"The decision is obvious, though," RememberMe chimed in casually.
"Shut up, RememberMe," Forev shot back.
Maylock pressed on. "Alright, the first topic we need to address is the future ruler of the Dissidia Kingdom,"
The room fell into silence. Everyone seemed lost in their own thoughts, weighing the gravity of the matter at hand.
"I want to hear from each of you first," Broken said, breaking the stillness.
But no one spoke immediately. The silence stretched on until Goldrich finally stepped in to break it.
"Broken," he began, "I'm sure everyone here has a lot to say, but it looks like no one wants to go first. So, I'll take the lead."
Broken gave a small nod, signaling him to continue.

"So, Broken... I'm going to speak from my personal perspective, as a member of the Vensalor Guild," Goldrich began, his voice steady. "We've made a massive contribution to this war. Yes, I know we weren't the only ones to make all of this happen, but let's be honest - we played the biggest role."
Several heads nodded in agreement, acknowledging the truth of his words.
"Even without considering your personal position, we deserve an extraordinary reward from the Kingdom," he continued.
There was a brief pause before Goldrich's expression grew more serious.
"However..." He held his words for a moment. "Since you're now officially married to Princess Alora, I'll say this boldly - you can claim the throne and become the new ruler."
His statement hung in the air, and a ripple of excitement spread through the room. Everyone seemed energized by the thought.

"You could become the new King - the first player to ever take the throne of Dissidia Kingdom. Together, we could rebuild the Kingdom and make it stronger than ever. And when it comes to funding, you already know you've got people here who will back you up." Broken nodded.
Goldrich continued. "I believe that's the most logical and reasonable solution to this issue," he said confidently.
"However..." He paused for a moment before continuing. "I'm also certain that every decision comes with its own burden."
A brief silence fell over the room as Goldrich stopped speaking.
"That's clearly the only choice. Broken must take the throne," RememberMe chimed in.
All eyes turned toward RememberMe for a moment, before they slowly shifted back to Broken.
"Will you take the throne, Broken?" Goldrich asked.
Broken offered a faint smile, though his mind was already spinning with countless scenarios. He had been weighing the possible outcomes and risks long before this conversation began.

"Thanks for your input, Goldrich," Broken finally responded. "But before I give my answer, I'd like to hear from Maylock first. I want to know all the risks we might face if I decide to take this path."
Maylock gave a faint smile. "You really know who's best suited to take the fall for this, don't you?"
Broken returned the smile.

Freya chimed in with a teasing tone. "Didn't you once say that you've gotten used to delivering unpopular opinions, Maylock? This is exactly your role. At least if you're the one proposing this idea, people can blame you for a decision that might end up sounding foolish." Maylock sighed heavily. "Alright, I'll take that risk. After all, I won't be online much, so I can dodge most of the backlash. I'm doing this to protect the honor of my proud Guild Master."
After a brief pause, Maylock continued.
"First, I'll start with the Sword of Dissidia," he began. "No one knows why it didn't appear during the war, why the King never used it, or where it's currently hidden."
He cast a glance at Broken.
"I'll ask Alora for more details about the sword," Broken replied with a nod.

Maylock gave a slow nod before continuing. "In Yunatea, the system of succession has always been tied to those with royal bloodlines. In this case, that's why Princess Alora was named the crowned princess and the legitimate heir to the throne."
He paused briefly, letting his words sink in before continuing.

"Even so, her status has been controversial. Many opposed her claim to the throne, which led to the formation of factions against her. The reason? She's half-human and half-elf- something the more traditionalist factions couldn't accept. And her main rival for the throne was Demian... whom we've already taken down."
Maylock scanned the room, his gaze lingering on each person before he spoke again.

"This kingdom spans vast territories, with many high-ranking nobles holding influence in the cities across the land. We could take the most brutal and bold path - seizing the throne by declaring Broken the new ruler. But make no mistake, that will spark rebellions in multiple regions."
A tense silence followed as Maylock's words hung in the air. Some of the members shifted uncomfortably, clearly uneasy with the harsh reality he'd laid out.
"Then just wipe out anyone who opposes us," RememberMe suggested casually.
"That's certainly the easiest solution," Maylock replied with a smirk.
"I believe it would be a foolish decision if we let the chance slip for Broken to become the ruler," RememberMe continued.
"Well, that's exactly why I'm presenting this," Maylock said, leaning back slightly. "I'm laying out the worst-case scenario so everyone here can respond as harshly as they want."
"Keep going, Maylock," Elincia encouraged.

Maylock gave a quick nod and continued. "The real problem is that taking the throne from Princess Alora will likely trigger a prolonged civil war. And considering our status as players - outsiders in this world - it will only increase resistance against us." "But Broken has done more for this kingdom than any of those nobles ever did!" RememberMe interjected. "Why should their opinions matter when they've contributed nothing?"
Forev chuckled dryly. "You're surprisingly naïve for someone who's used to dealing with politics."
"Well, someone's gotta play the opposition, right?" RememberMe grinned. "Even if I'm making dumb arguments, it's good to have someone push back against Maylock's points."
The tension eased slightly as a few of them chuckled at RememberMe's playful defiance. But soon, all eyes turned to Broken once again.
"What about your opinion, Broken?" Maylock asked.
Broken nodded slowly. "I've considered three key factors... but first, thanks for opening up this topic, Maylock."
Everyone nodded in agreement, leaning in with anticipation. They were ready to hear his reasoning.
