chapters.title: Chapter 732: Infernal Mirage
paragraphs: There was one final item left on the table. Broken reached for it, his fingers closing around a small, black-and-purple coin. The surface shimmered faintly, almost like liquid shadows swirling beneath glass.
[Infernal Mirage (Weapon Cosmetic)]
[Effect: Changes the appearance of any weapon to have a shadowy aura with flickering fire embers.
[Skill Modifier: Converts the weapon's active skills to shadow and fire effects.]
A Weapon Cosmetic?
He inspected it carefully. There were no damage-boosting effects or battle-enhancing abilities attached to the item. It was purely cosmetic. But... it came with an interesting twist.

The item would coat any weapon he wielded in an aura of shadow and fire. Not only that, but any skills cast through the weapon would also gain a shadow-fire visual effect. It was subtle, but powerful in its own way - a disguise to conceal his true identity while adding a layer of intimidation.
"Take it," Alora said softly, breaking his train of thought.
Broken turned to her, but he remained silent for a moment.

"This item can mask any weapon you use, right?" she continued. "It'll be perfect for you if you ever want to fight in your Demon Form but still use your regular weapon - like the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear."
Broken gave a slow nod. "Then... I'm taking two items?"

"Yes," Alora replied with a gentle smile. "Why not? The war won't be won without your contribution. Don't forget, if it weren't for you crafting that device to block the meteor strike, everyone would've been obliterated."
Broken's eyes softened as he recalled that moment.

The meteor fall had been catastrophic, one that should have annihilated everything in its path. Yet, thanks to the device he'd crafted with help from RememberMe, PussyCat, and Frostedge, who had contributed massive amounts of Soul Stones to its creation - they had managed to survive the unthinkable.
"That's why you deserve this," Alora said. "You're the one holding everything together." "Alright," he said with a small grin. "I'll take it."
Broken equipped the item. He stood up straight and summoned the Mythic-grade Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear into his hand.

The moment the spear materialized, its usual oceanic glow shifted. The weapon's aura transformed into a mesmerizing blend of swirling shadows and blazing fire, crackling along the spear's length. The same dark, fiery aura spread across his body.

He spun the spear effortlessly, watching the fiery trail it left in the air, flames dancing and flickering with each movement. Shadows intertwined with the blaze, creating a mesmerizing contrast between darkness and light.

For a brief second, Broken entertained the idea of casting a skill to see the full effect. His mind raced with possibilities - what would his attacks look like with this enhancement? But he stopped himself. There was no need to unleash anything serious now.
Instead, he turned to Alora with a small, satisfied smile. Without a word, he dismissed the spear, sending it back into his inventory.
"I really like it," Broken said.
Alora smiled softly. "Yes, I can see that from your eyes," she replied. "That look... the gaze of someone hungry for war."
Broken chuckled, shaking his head. "Why do you sound just like Lily?"
"Lily?" Alora tilted her head.
"Lily is Bloom," Broken explained.
"Do all players have different identities out there, Broken? Different names beyond this world?
Broken gave a small nod. "Yes. My name outside is Leon."
"Leon..." Alora repeated, as if tasting the name on her tongue. "That's a cute name. It makes me wonder why you chose the name Broken for yourself in this world."
Broken fell silent for a moment, rubbing the back of his neck. "Uhm... I don't really remember why," he admitted with a sheepish laugh. "I guess I just thought it sounded cool at the time."
Alora chuckled softly. "And now, you've even earned the title 'The Broken Player' from your guild members, haven't you?"
"Yeah... guess the name stuck, huh?"
[Name: Broken]
[Level: 153]
[Class: Unique - Super Novice | Unique - Royal Blacksmith | Unique - Rift Digger | Unique - Elemental Forger]
[Health: 4230 | Mana: 8028]
[Strength: 1015 | Agility: 384 | Intelligence: 669 | Constitution: 623 | Stamina: 465]
[Charisma: 105 | Luck: 62 | Dexterity: 50 | Survival: 30 | Perception: 20]
[Available Stat Points: 30]
Broken opened his status menu, carefully reviewing his updated stats while only wearing the accessories. No armor, no weapons - just the passive boosts provided by the items he had equipped.
It was a good way to see his raw stats without any extra enhancements. And immediately, a few things stood out.
And yes... it was obvious. His Agility was the most lacking stat by far.
I really need to start spending more points on Agility.
Without further hesitation, he allocated 30 stat points into Agility.

While it wasn't his weakest area in combat, he knew that a higher Agility stat would allow him to move faster, dodge attacks more effectively, and strike with greater speed. It wasn't something he could keep ignoring.
And more importantly-it would boost his damage when using a bow.

Next, Stamina. It was lagging behind as well, but that didn't worry him too much. His armor provided a solid Stamina boost when equipped, so he wasn't too concerned about running out of endurance during battles.
Charisma: 105.
Isn't 105 in Charisma really high?
He couldn't help but wonder how that would affect his interactions with NPCs. Would they be more willing to share information? Offer better deals? Maybe even unlock hidden quests?
Broken then took a moment to review some of his skills that had leveled up after the recent battle.
[Blessing of Health (Active Skill) Lv. 7]
[Healing Touch (Active Skill) Lv. 7]
[Charged Attack (Active Skill) Lv. 7]
[Quick Strike (Active Skill) Lv. 7]
[Mining Technique (Passive Skill) Lv. 5]
[Explosive Arrow (Active Skill) Lv. 6]
[Spiral Pierce (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv. 6] [Spear Guard (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv. 6]
[Groundbreaker (Active Skill) Lv. 6]
[Sniper's Focus (Active Skill) Lv. 6]
[Blade Dance (Active Skill) Lv. 6]
[Quake Strike (Active Skill) Lv. 6]
[Miner's Fortitude (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv. 5]
[Summon Elemental Golem (Conditional Active Skill) Lv. 2]
[Elemental Command Slots (Utility Skill) Lv. 2]

Most of the upgraded skills came from his Super Novice class. In particular, two of his signature bow-related abilities stood out: Sniper's Focus and Explosive Arrow. These were the core of his long-range arsenal, and seeing them power up was a welcome boost.
But what surprised him the most was that two of his golem-related skills had also leveled up -Summon Golem and Elemental Command Slots.
This meant only one thing: Broken could now command more golems at once. He was no longer limited to controlling just two at a time!
With these upgrades, he would be able to summon and manage more golems moving forward.

He took a deep breath, feeling a sense of satisfaction as his stats adjusted. Then, lifting his gaze toward Alora, he realized there was one more important thing he needed to confirm. "Do you think an hour will be enough for us to check out the thing I've been searching for all this time?"
"Yes, I believe that's more than enough."
Slowly, Broken exhaled. This was it—the moment he had been waiting for. Soon, he would finally lay eyes on the Sword of Dissidia.

Shadows intertwined with the blaze, creating a mesmerizing contrast between darkness and light.
For a brief second, Broken entertained the idea of casting a skill to see the full effect.
His mind raced with possibilities - what would his attacks look like with this enhancement?
But he stopped himself.
There was no need to unleash anything serious now.
Instead, he turned to Alora with a small, satisfied smile.
Without a word, he dismissed the spear, sending it back into his inventory.
"I really like it," Broken said.
Alora smiled softly.
"Yes, I can see that from your eyes," she replied.
"That look... the gaze of someone hungry for war."
Broken chuckled, shaking his head.
"Why do you sound just like Lily?"
"Lily?" Alora tilted her head.
"Lily is Bloom," Broken explained.
"Do all players have different identities out there, Broken?
Different names beyond this world?
Broken gave a small nod.
"Yes.
My name outside is Leon."
"Leon..." Alora repeated, as if tasting the name on her tongue.
"That's a cute name.
It makes me wonder why you chose the name Broken for yourself in this world."
Broken fell silent for a moment, rubbing the back of his neck.
"Uhm...
I don't really remember why," he admitted with a sheepish laugh.
"I guess I just thought it sounded cool at the time."
Alora chuckled softly.
"And now, you've even earned the title 'The Broken Player' from your guild members, haven't you?"
"Yeah... guess the name stuck, huh?"
[Name: Broken]
[Level: 153]
[Class: Unique - Super Novice | Unique - Royal Blacksmith | Unique - Rift Digger | Unique - Elemental Forger]
[Health: 4230 | Mana: 8028]
[Strength: 1015 | Agility: 384 | Intelligence: 669 | Constitution: 623 | Stamina: 465]
[Charisma: 105 | Luck: 62 | Dexterity: 50 | Survival: 30 | Perception: 20]
[Available Stat Points: 30]
Broken opened his status menu, carefully reviewing his updated stats while only wearing the accessories.
No armor, no weapons - just the passive boosts provided by the items he had equipped.
It was a good way to see his raw stats without any extra enhancements.
And immediately, a few things stood out.
And yes... it was obvious.
His Agility was the most lacking stat by far.
I really need to start spending more points on Agility.
Without further hesitation, he allocated 30 stat points into Agility.
While it wasn't his weakest area in combat, he knew that a higher Agility stat would allow him to move faster, dodge attacks more effectively, and strike with greater speed.
It wasn't something he could keep ignoring.
And more importantly-it would boost his damage when using a bow.
Next, Stamina.
It was lagging behind as well, but that didn't worry him too much.
His armor provided a solid Stamina boost when equipped, so he wasn't too concerned about running out of endurance during battles.
Charisma: 105.
Isn't 105 in Charisma really high?
He couldn't help but wonder how that would affect his interactions with NPCs.
Would they be more willing to share information?
Offer better deals?
Maybe even unlock hidden quests?
Broken then took a moment to review some of his skills that had leveled up after the recent battle.
[Blessing of Health (Active Skill) Lv.
[Healing Touch (Active Skill) Lv.
[Charged Attack (Active Skill) Lv.
[Quick Strike (Active Skill) Lv.
[Mining Technique (Passive Skill) Lv.
[Explosive Arrow (Active Skill) Lv.
[Spiral Pierce (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv.
6] [Spear Guard (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv.
[Groundbreaker (Active Skill) Lv.
[Sniper's Focus (Active Skill) Lv.
[Blade Dance (Active Skill) Lv.
[Quake Strike (Active Skill) Lv.
[Miner's Fortitude (Conditional Passive Skill) Lv.
[Summon Elemental Golem (Conditional Active Skill) Lv.
[Elemental Command Slots (Utility Skill) Lv.
Most of the upgraded skills came from his Super Novice class.
In particular, two of his signature bow-related abilities stood out: Sniper's Focus and Explosive Arrow.
These were the core of his long-range arsenal, and seeing them power up was a welcome boost.
But what surprised him the most was that two of his golem-related skills had also leveled up -Summon Golem and Elemental Command Slots.
This meant only one thing: Broken could now command more golems at once.
He was no longer limited to controlling just two at a time!
With these upgrades, he would be able to summon and manage more golems moving forward.
He took a deep breath, feeling a sense of satisfaction as his stats adjusted.
Then, lifting his gaze toward Alora, he realized there was one more important thing he needed to confirm.
"Do you think an hour will be enough for us to check out the thing I've been searching for all this time?"
"Yes, I believe that's more than enough."
Slowly, Broken exhaled.
This was it—the moment he had been waiting for.
Soon, he would finally lay eyes on the Sword of Dissidia.

chapters.title: Chapter 733: The Sword of Dissidia
paragraphs: Alora led Broken, with Lionell accompanying them as a guard, through an unfamiliar section of the castle. It was a network of underground corridors-dark, winding, and branching off in unpredictable directions.
One thing was clear: anyone entering without proper guidance would be hopelessly lost, and whatever fate awaited them in those depths was best left unimagined.

The walls were solid, made of rough stone embedded with faintly glimmering crystals, while the dry floors echoed softly with each step. Every now and then, they encountered a dead end. But Alora would press her hand against the stone, and the wall would shift like pieces of a puzzle, revealing a hidden passage.
At one such opening, Alora turned to Lionell.
"We'll continue from here on our own," she said firmly.
"Understood, Your Highness." Knight Lionell gave a respectful nod before stepping back to stand guard.
As Alora and Broken ventured deeper, silence enveloped them, broken only by the soft sound of their footsteps and the steady rhythm of their breaths.
"What is this place?"
"This is the underground vault where the Sword of Dissidia is kept."
"Are you the only one who can enter?"

Alora glanced at him. "Only the rightful heir of the kingdom can unlock these doors," she explained. Then, with a teasing glint in her eyes, she added, "And don't even think about using any of your skills to break through them, okay?"
"Noted."
Broken continued walking alongside Alora, but a question lingered in his mind. Eventually, he voiced it.
"Why didn't you hide in this place during the attack?"
Alora glanced at him. "I couldn't hide when the kingdom was under a major assault, could I?"
Broken nodded slowly, respecting her answer.

They walked in silence for a while, the air growing colder as they ventured further underground. Finally, they reached a larger chamber-an expansive space illuminated by softly glowing crystal lamps embedded into the walls.
And there, standing firmly in the center, was a sword.
It wasn't an ordinary weapon. The blade was nearly twice the size of a normal sword. The weapon stood embedded in a stone pedestal.
Broken stepped forward, his gaze locked on the sword.
"Is this the sword?" he asked quietly.
Alora came to stand beside him and nodded. "Yes. The Sword of Dissidia.
Broken's brow furrowed slightly as he glanced back at her. "If this sword is as powerful as it's said to be, why didn't the King use it during the war?"
"There's a reason for that. But I think you should find out for yourself. The sword will tell you."
Without a word, Broken turned back to the sword. Slowly, he reached out and laid his hand on the hilt.
[The Sword of Dissidia]
[Grade: ???]
[Durability: 100/100]
[Weight: 6932]

[When the sword is wielded by one who is not the rightful king, it remains dull and lifeless. But in the hands of a ruler who has passed the Three Royal Trials, it awakens with cosmic power, its edge capable of splitting the fabric of reality and negating divine protections.] [Judgment of Sovereigns - Final Form:
"Only a true ruler can wield the full might of Dissidia's legacy."]
[User Restriction: To wield the Sword of Dissidia and unlock its full potential, the wielder must fulfill two out of the three royal requirements:
1. Royal Bloodline and Recognition by the Kingdom's Legacy
2. Champion of the Sloth Deity
3. Found a Respected Kingdom]

The sword's grade remained unknown. However, one thing was clear-it was incredibly heavy. Even with his Strength stat over 1000, Broken could feel the immense weight of the blade just by gripping the hilt.
But beyond the sheer weight, there was another problem. The sword was still locked. Several requirements needed to be met before it could be wielded.
One requirement immediately caught his attention: Royal Bloodline.
He turned to Alora. "Does that mean I'll never be able to fulfill the first requirement? I don't have royal blood."

Alora shook her head. "I can't wield it either, Broken. Even though I have royal blood, I'm not qualified. That's because one of the conditions is to be the Champion of the Sloth Deity-a title you already hold."
Broken absorbed her words, nodding slowly.
"So, I've already met the second condition. Which leaves... the third one. Found a respected kingdom?"
Silence stretched between them for a moment as he processed what that meant.
"The sword is asking me to found a kingdom?" he murmured, half to himself.

"And not just any kingdom," Alora added gently. "It must be one that is respected. That means someone can't simply declare a piece of land as a kingdom and fulfill the condition. It has to be earned."
Broken took a moment to study the sword's description more carefully. His eyes narrowed as he spotted something curious in the text.
"Tri Royal Quest?" he muttered, reading it aloud. "What's that supposed to mean?"
"Maybe it's a quest that will reveal itself once you've met all the sword's requirements," she offered.
Broken nodded slowly, agreeing with her assessment. "That makes sense."

Without further hesitation, he placed both hands on the hilt of the sword and lifted it. As he pulled it free from the stone, the sheer size of the weapon became apparent. The blade stretched nearly as tall as his own body. Despite its elegant craftsmanship, the sword felt more like a weapon made for a colossal creature-something a giant might wield in battle. Though it was undoubtedly a sword by design, its massive proportions made it feel as though it belonged to a realm beyond human hands.
Broken adjusted his grip, feeling the strain in his arms.
"Can I take this sword and store it in the Moonlight Dimension?"
Alora nodded without hesitation. "Of course. You're free to do that."
Without another word, the sword vanished, disappearing from sight as if it had never been there.

"The sword has tasked me with founding a kingdom," he said slowly. "It seems our decision for you to take the crown was the right choice for everyone. With you on the throne, it strengthens my path toward fulfilling the sword's requirement."
Alora tilted her head slightly. "To build your own kingdom?"
"It looks like that's where everything is heading," Broken replied. "And I'm certain that's what I'll do."
"I'll do my best to support you in whatever way I can."
"But... are you sure you want to let me take the sword from this place?"
Alora closed her eyes briefly before meeting his gaze again.
"I'm sure. That sword will serve a far greater purpose in your hands than it ever would down here."
With her assurance, Broken nodded.

As they began making their way out of the underground vault, he couldn't help but reflect on the weapon now in his possession. The Sword of Dissidia-a blade of immense power, its true potential still beyond his grasp. Even now, he couldn't measure its strength, nor could he fully comprehend its mysteries.
But there was one thing he was certain of.
It was said that this sword could challenge gods. And if that was true... this was no ordinary weapon.

As he imagined what it might be capable of when he finally fulfilled all of its requirements and unlocked its hidden quests, a thrill of anticipation coursed through him. Whatever lay ahead, Broken knew one thing for sure: this sword would change everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 734: The Crown of Dissidia
paragraphs: Broken and all the members of the Vensalor Guild had gathered in a single room. They had just defended the capital city of Dissidia Kingdom from a massive attack, and now it was time to focus on what came next. After years of preparation and hard work, the moment they had been striving for was finally within reach.

Broken shared the details about the Sword of Dissidia. As he explained everything-its requirements, its mysterious power, and the potential quests tied to it-the room fell into a contemplative silence.
The first to speak was Maylock. "It's pretty clear that the sword isn't meant for regular battles. Its real purpose is to fight the deities."
Goldrich chuckled. "Doesn't that just prove that there's an even bigger plot waiting for us in the future? I mean, think about it-what kind of situation would force us to go up against deities?"
Jovina let out a dry laugh, shaking her head. "Come on. We barely survived fighting Named Demons last time. We were a mess! If we're serious about fighting gods, we need to get way stronger."
The group chuckled at her blunt honesty, but everyone knew she wasn't wrong.
Goldrich turned his attention back to Broken. "And you, Broken-I think it's time we start thinking seriously about how you're going to found your own kingdom."
Everyone grew quiet again as Goldrich's words sank in. The Sword of Dissidia had made it clear that building a kingdom was part of Broken's path. But how would they accomplish that?
Maylock took the lead in answering.

"Let's keep it simple. If we want to found a kingdom, there are a few key requirements we need to meet. First, we need land to claim as our own. Second, we need people willing to become citizens of that kingdom. And third, we need recognition from at least some of the other kingdoms on this continent and ideally from kingdoms on the other continents as well."
Booba chimed in with a grin. "We can get that recognition if we just buy their loyalty."

Maylock sighed at Booba's words. "It's not that easy, Booba. This isn't just about throwing money around. And finding enough land to claim as our own? That's going to be the hardest part. We'll either need to take land from someone else or discover new, unoccupied land somewhere."
Broken nodded slowly before speaking.

"I'm sure this will take a much longer time than we initially thought. Right now, our main focus should be stabilizing the Dissidia Kingdom first. We need to make sure the kingdom stands on solid ground before taking any bigger steps."
He paused, letting his gaze sweep over everyone in the room.

"Once we've established that stability, the next step is to strengthen our defenses-both the kingdom's internal security and its borders. With the resources and areas we can now access more effectively within Dissidia's territory, we can use that to build our strength further. Only then will we be able to expand beyond what we currently have."
There was a brief silence. Then Maylock smiled, leaning back in his seat.
"That's a very nice plan. Careful, strategic, and focused on long-term growth. Exactly what we need right now."
With their discussion about founding a kingdom concluded, the group shifted their attention to something—or rather, someone-more pressing: Ivana.
Maylock was the first to speak.

"I've already mobilized our resources to search for Ivana. For now, our focus is still on the East Continent, but I've also hired people to investigate her whereabouts on other continents. Unfortunately, we can't cover every area. Because with her having unlocked her blessing, she's capable of doing things we can't predict."
Broken nodded, absorbing the information.

Goldrich picked up where Maylock left off. "There's no significant movement from the Central Continent yet. However, word has spread that the Champion of Ancestral Greed has returned. That news has already reached the ears of the High Elf Queen."
Broken frowned at that. "That could be a problem if the Queen decides to get involved."
Maylock said with a nod. "If she takes action, it could complicate things further."
Broken took a deep breath, letting his thoughts settle before speaking.

"For now, I'll stay in the capital. I need time to work on my golems and push my skill levels higher. I'll also aim to craft another Legendary-grade item to advance my blacksmith class to Legendary grade."

He glanced around the room, making sure everyone was paying attention before continuing. "Once I've done that, I'll build a ship golem-something powerful enough to withstand the long journey-and head to the West Continent to search for Ivana."

It would take time-possibly more time than they had before the Eternal Challenge began. Yet no one voiced any concern about that event. Perhaps they all sensed that, for Broken, the Eternal Challenge was no longer his top priority.
Ivana was.
And nothing-not even a world-shaping event-seemed more important to him now.

A few days later, hundreds, if not thousands of people gathered around the royal palace. The streets of the capital were still undergoing repairs from the recent battle, but that did nothing to dull the grandeur and excitement of this day.
It was a day of historic importance-the coronation of the new ruler of Dissidia Kingdom.
Rows of seats had been arranged in front of the castle gates, filled with a mix of important NPCs, emissaries from neighboring kingdoms, and prominent players from across the continents.

From the far side of the castle grounds, Alora, the Crowned Princess, emerged. Her elegant steps were steady and poised as she walked down the aisle toward the ceremonial platform, flanked by two royal knights in full ceremonial armor.

Her gown shimmered in the sunlight-a rich blend of midnight blue and silver embroidery, symbolizing the nobility of the night sky and the enduring light of the kingdom. Her red hair was styled into a braid crown, with strands of fine silver thread woven through, making her look every bit the queen she was destined to become.

She walked with the composure of someone prepared to take on the mantle of leadership. Behind her, the knights moved in perfect unison, their polished armor glinting under the sun. When Alora reached the platform, she stopped in front of High Priest Elandir. His long emerald robes, marked with the insignia of the Seven Deities, swayed lightly in the breeze. The crowd murmured, a mix of whispers and speculation spreading. Some questioned what this coronation would mean for the kingdom's future. Others speculated on whether Alora would fulfill the prophecy tied to the Sword of Dissidia. And there were even murmurs about Broken, wondering what role he would play in the new era of the kingdom.
As Alora stood still, waiting for the ceremony to begin, all eyes remained locked on her.
The future of the Dissidia Kingdom was about to be reshaped.
Elandir stepped forward, his solemn voice carrying across the crowd.

"Today, we stand at the crossroads of history," he began. "The Dissidia Kingdom has endured countless challenges-wars, betrayals, and hardships. Yet it stands, unbroken. And now, a new chapter begins."
He turned to Alora. "Alora Rogwyn of the House of Dissidia, do you stand here today of your own will, prepared to take the crown and bear the burdens of this kingdom?"
Alora nodded, her voice clear. "I do."
"Do you vow to uphold the legacy of your ancestors, to protect this land and its people, and to guide them through both peace and storm?"
"I vow," Alora answered, placing a hand over her heart.

"With the blessings of the Seven Deities who watch over this world," he began, "I call upon the ancestors of Dissidia to bear witness to this moment. And with their guidance, I bestow upon you the mantle of rulership, a burden both sacred and eternal."
Two knights stepped forward, carrying the Crown of Dissidia.
Elandir took the crown in both hands. He turned once more to Alora.
"Alora Rogwyn, with this crown, you are no longer a princess, but Queen of Dissidia. May you rule with wisdom, compassion, and courage."
He gently placed the crown upon her head, and as it settled, a faint glow emanated from the gemstones, signifying the acceptance of her as the rightful ruler.
The crowd remained silent for a moment, as if holding their collective breath.
Then, Elandir stepped back, and with a voice that echoed across the capital, he declared.
"All hail Queen Alora of Dissidia!"

"Once I've done that, I'll build a ship golem-something powerful enough to withstand the long journey-and head to the West Continent to search for Ivana."
It would take time-possibly more time than they had before the Eternal Challenge began.
Yet no one voiced any concern about that event.
Perhaps they all sensed that, for Broken, the Eternal Challenge was no longer his top priority.
Ivana was.
And nothing-not even a world-shaping event-seemed more important to him now.
A few days later, hundreds, if not thousands of people gathered around the royal palace.
The streets of the capital were still undergoing repairs from the recent battle, but that did nothing to dull the grandeur and excitement of this day.
It was a day of historic importance-the coronation of the new ruler of Dissidia Kingdom.
Rows of seats had been arranged in front of the castle gates, filled with a mix of important NPCs, emissaries from neighboring kingdoms, and prominent players from across the continents.
From the far side of the castle grounds, Alora, the Crowned Princess, emerged.
Her elegant steps were steady and poised as she walked down the aisle toward the ceremonial platform, flanked by two royal knights in full ceremonial armor.
Her gown shimmered in the sunlight-a rich blend of midnight blue and silver embroidery, symbolizing the nobility of the night sky and the enduring light of the kingdom.
Her red hair was styled into a braid crown, with strands of fine silver thread woven through, making her look every bit the queen she was destined to become.
She walked with the composure of someone prepared to take on the mantle of leadership.
Behind her, the knights moved in perfect unison, their polished armor glinting under the sun.
When Alora reached the platform, she stopped in front of High Priest Elandir.
His long emerald robes, marked with the insignia of the Seven Deities, swayed lightly in the breeze.
The crowd murmured, a mix of whispers and speculation spreading.
Some questioned what this coronation would mean for the kingdom's future.
Others speculated on whether Alora would fulfill the prophecy tied to the Sword of Dissidia.
And there were even murmurs about Broken, wondering what role he would play in the new era of the kingdom.
As Alora stood still, waiting for the ceremony to begin, all eyes remained locked on her.
The future of the Dissidia Kingdom was about to be reshaped.
Elandir stepped forward, his solemn voice carrying across the crowd.
"Today, we stand at the crossroads of history," he began.
"The Dissidia Kingdom has endured countless challenges-wars, betrayals, and hardships.
Yet it stands, unbroken.
And now, a new chapter begins."
He turned to Alora.
"Alora Rogwyn of the House of Dissidia, do you stand here today of your own will, prepared to take the crown and bear the burdens of this kingdom?"
Alora nodded, her voice clear.
"I do."
"Do you vow to uphold the legacy of your ancestors, to protect this land and its people, and to guide them through both peace and storm?"
"I vow," Alora answered, placing a hand over her heart.
"With the blessings of the Seven Deities who watch over this world," he began, "I call upon the ancestors of Dissidia to bear witness to this moment.
And with their guidance, I bestow upon you the mantle of rulership, a burden both sacred and eternal."
Two knights stepped forward, carrying the Crown of Dissidia.
Elandir took the crown in both hands.
He turned once more to Alora.
"Alora Rogwyn, with this crown, you are no longer a princess, but Queen of Dissidia.
May you rule with wisdom, compassion, and courage."
He gently placed the crown upon her head, and as it settled, a faint glow emanated from the gemstones, signifying the acceptance of her as the rightful ruler.
The crowd remained silent for a moment, as if holding their collective breath.
Then, Elandir stepped back, and with a voice that echoed across the capital, he declared.
"All hail Queen Alora of Dissidia!"

chapters.title: Chapter 735: Where Is Freya?
paragraphs: Reviewing all the leveled-up skills? Clear.
Checking the loot from the Demons? Clear.
Securing the Sword of Dissidia? Done-though for now, it remained locked and unusable.
And with that, the major milestones had been ticked off.
But perhaps the most significant achievement was that Alora had now officially ascended as the Queen of Dissidia Kingdom.
The next big event? Something that would undoubtedly shake the entire continent.
The announcement of Queen Alora's marriage to a player.
While many had speculated about Alora's growing closeness to a certain player, few truly believed the rumors would become reality. But soon, the official announcement would leave no room for doubt.

The wedding ceremony had been intentionally delayed until after Alora's coronation. It was a calculated move-to ensure that her position as ruler was secure, and to gather more support while managing potential opposition from certain factions within the kingdom.
The pieces were falling into place.

The capsule device hissed as it opened, releasing a soft puff of air. Leon stepped out slowly, his expression flat and unreadable, as though he hadn't quite returned from the world he'd just left behind.
The morning light filtered through the apartment window, casting a pale glow over the quiet room.
As he made his way to the kitchen, the familiar sound of movement greeted him. Lily was already there, dressed for the day and eating breakfast.
She looked up when she saw him. "Leon... you're going to campus today, right?"
"Yes," he answered simply as he slid into the chair across from her and took a sandwich from the plate on the table.
Lily tilted her head slightly. "Tomorrow's the weekend. How about we go out somewhere? Maybe a little trip or just... have some fun outside?"
Leon glanced at her, "That sounds good," he said softly.
"We could invite Freya too. It's been... three days since I last saw her."
Leon froze for a moment, the sandwich halfway to his mouth.
Three days.

It was true. Freya hadn't logged into the game for the past three days. And more concerning than that he hadn't been able to reach her, either. She hadn't answered any of his messages, both in-game and outside.
"Yeah..." Leon murmured. "I haven't been able to contact her."
"Don't worry. I'll try to reach her today."
Leon nodded slowly.
After finishing her breakfast, Lily stood, slinging her bag over her shoulder. "I'll see you later. And don't forget-we're going out tomorrow. Don't you dare cancel!"
"Got it," Leon replied with a faint smile, watching her leave.
As the door clicked shut behind her, the apartment grew silent again. Where is Freya?

A few minutes later, Leon drove his Northstar EV out of the hotel parking lot, heading toward campus. The smooth hum of the electric engine was the only sound accompanying him as the city streets blurred by.
When he arrived at the campus and parked the car, the moment he stepped out, he felt something... off.
Closing the car door behind him, Leon paused, his gaze subtly shifting around.
Why does it feel like more people are staring at me?

It wasn't just his imagination. As he walked toward the main building, more eyes than usual seemed to track his every move. Some students glanced at him, whispering to their friends, while others gave him brief, curious looks before quickly turning away.
Leon sighed softly, keeping his expression neutral.

This had been happening more often ever since the battle in Dissidia Kingdom. His name had started to gain more recognition, even outside the game. He hadn't bothered to check online to see how far it had spread, but the reality was starting to catch up with him.
And now, with Alora officially crowned as the Queen of Dissidia, it seemed the attention on him had only increased.
As he walked across campus, several people passing by gave him small waves or said a quick "hi."
Leon nodded politely, responding with a simple, "Hi."

He wasn't the type to enjoy being in the spotlight, but it was becoming harder to avoid. Before he could reach his destination, someone caught up to him from the right. He glanced over and saw a familiar face-a young woman with wavy blonde hair.
"Hi, Leon. Good morning." It was Laura.
"Hi, Laura..." Leon greeted her with a smile.
She walked alongside him, matching his pace. "You've been absent from campus for a few days," she pointed out. "I was thinking of dropping by to check on you."
Leon chuckled softly. "We just saw each other in-game, didn't we?"
Laura gave him a playful look. "True. But you do realize you've been hard to reach lately, right? Even in-game."
"Really?" Leon raised a brow.

Over the past few days, he had been completely absorbed in various tasks within the game. Between working on the Tower in the Moonlight Dimension, handling guild commissions, and gathering materials for a new golem, he'd barely had time for anything else.

The campus day passed without much notice. For Leon, it felt like a routine-something he went through merely to fulfill a responsibility. The lectures, the conversations, the familiar faces... none of it sparked any real interest.
What's happening to me?

That thought lingered in his mind as he trudged through the day. Even during his usual high- intensity run, something felt off. His body moved, his muscles burned, and sweat poured down his face, but there was no rush of adrenaline, no sense of accomplishment.
Just exhaustion.
He wasn't thinking of quitting-that wasn't his style. But something inside him felt... missing. A strange emptiness he couldn't quite define.
Later that afternoon, he drove to Lily's school to pick her up.

When he spotted Lily walking toward the car, something felt off. She wasn't with Hazel, her usual companion. But more than that-it was her expression. Lily was walking faster than usual, her face tense.
Leon stepped out of the car, meeting her halfway.
"Why do you look so panicked, Lily?"
"Freya..."
"Freya? What about her?"
"Yes... she's been sick for the past few days.
"What? What happened to her? Which hospital?"
Lily shook her head, tugging at his sleeve. "Get in the car. I'll explain everything on the way."
The Northstar EV sped out of the school area.
"So, what's the deal with Freya? Is she being treated at the hospital?"
Lily shook her head. "No..."
Leon frowned, glancing at her. "What do you mean no?"
"She's being treated at home."
"At home? Why not at the hospital? What's wrong with her?"
"It sounds like her body just gave out. She's completely drained and needs bed rest."
Leon fell silent for a moment, processing the information. "I don't know where she lives. She never told me."
He shot a quick glance at Lily. "Where did you get this information?"
"From Alfred," Lily replied, her voice soft. Then she hesitated. "And..."
"And what?"
"How about we visit Freya?"
Leon sighed. "I'd like that, but... we don't even know where she lives."
Lily gave a small smile. "I do. I know where she lives."
"Really?"
"Yes."
Without waiting for his response, Lily tapped the dashboard screen in front of her, entering their destination. The map loaded quickly, showing a route leading out of the city.
Leon's brows furrowed as he saw where the destination pointed.
"She lives there?"
Lily nodded.
"Yes."
The location was in a remote area, near a hilltop outside the city. It wasn't the kind of place most people would choose to live.
It reminded him of the kind of place someone like Goldrich would pick to stay away from the world.
"Why would she live there?" Leon muttered to himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 736: Welcome to Freya’s World
paragraphs: The drive to Freya's place wasn't particularly long-just about two hours. But even so, Leon couldn't help but wonder.
Does Freya make this trip every day to meet me?
It seemed unlikely. After all, Freya often stayed in the hotel, on the same floor as him, and she'd mentioned a few times that she also had a place in the city.
How many places does she have?

That question lingered in his mind as they continued the drive, heading into a hilly area. It wasn't as elevated as the secluded spot where Goldrich lived, but the road leading up to it was surprisingly well-maintained. Smooth pavement, neatly trimmed trees, and well-placed signs made it clear that someone took care of this road regularly-despite how empty it was. They hadn't seen a single other car on the way.
Eventually, they reached a large iron gate. As they approached, the gate opened automatically, without Leon having to confirm his identity.
He glanced at Lily, a bit surprised. "She knows we're coming?"
Lily shook her head. "Alfred knows."
Leon's brow furrowed. "Do you think Alfred is someone sent by the Golden Age Company, or is he actually someone Freya hired herself?"
Lily gave a shrug. "I don't know."
As they drove through the gate, a large white house came into view. It was modern in design, made up of stacked rectangular blocks, giving it a sleek yet elegant appearance.
Leon let out a soft chuckle. "She really is... that rich."
The Northstar EV rolled to a stop in the parking area, where a few people in black suits were already waiting. They were clearly staff a mix of men and women, all dressed neatly.

As Leon opened the car door and stepped out, one of the men, who appeared to be in his fifties, approached. His demeanor was calm and respectful, with a hint of warmth in his eyes, as if he recognized Leon.
"Welcome, Mr. Leon, Miss Lily," the man greeted with a slight bow. "We've been expecting you."
Leon gave a polite bow in return. "Hi, I'm a friend of Freya. Is it true she lives here?"
The older man smiled warmly. "Yes. Miss Freya is currently staying here. Please, follow me inside."
Lily stepped up beside Leon, giving him a reassuring nod as they both followed the man toward the house.
"We'll take you both inside," the man added as he opened the front door, revealing the house's interior.

The house's design was warm and modern, with an emphasis on natural light. Large windows filled the space with soft sunlight, making the white walls and light wooden floors feel fresh and airy. The furniture was a blend of modern minimalism and cozy touches-a plush gray sofa, earthy tones in the decor, and fresh green plants placed in just the right spots to make the space feel alive.
Everything about the house gave a sense of comfort and tranquility. It wasn't flashy, but there was a subtle elegance in how everything seemed perfectly arranged.
Leon and Lily were led to the main living area, where they were invited to sit on the sofa set in the center of the room.
The older man gave a respectful bow before stepping back. "Please wait here. Someone will be with you shortly.
As they sat down, Leon glanced around, taking in the space.
After some time waiting, someone finally appeared from behind the wall leading to another room.
Leon's face softened into a relieved smile the moment he saw her.

The girl they both knew-Freya-stepped into the living area, her brown hair tied back in a loose ponytail, wearing a simple blue shirt and shorts. But despite her casual appearance, there was something different about her-she looked tired.
Lily stood and waved. "Hi, Freya..."
Leon stood as well.
Freya smiled as she approached, waving back. "You found my house."
Then her gaze shifted to Leon. "What are you doing here?"
"We were worried about you."
Freya let out a light laugh as she sat across from them.
"Worried?" she teased. "That's not like you."
Leon and Lily both sat back down, and Lily quickly took over the conversation. "I heard from Alfred that you were sick."
Freya sighed and leaned back in her chair. "I'm sorry I didn't let you know... That was really irresponsible of me."
Leon shook his head. "Not really. You've been working so hard these past few months. It's no surprise you're exhausted."
Freya gave a faint smile. "Yeah, I guess I needed a break... a long one."
Lily giggled, leaning forward with a teasing look. "You should've seen Leon's panicked face when he heard you were sick, Freya."
Freya's eyes sparkled with amusement as she turned to Leon. "Really? You were that worried?" Her lips curved into a mischievous grin. "And yet, you show up empty-handed? No flowers, no gifts?"

Leon smiled, shaking his head. "Looks like you're already feeling better if you're back to teasing me. Besides, I wasn't here to bring you gifts. I came to put you back to work. Don't misunderstand my panic."
Freya playfully kicked the table leg.
"Ugh, Lily, your brother is terrible. He's going to make me stay sick even longer with comments like that!"
"That's just how Leon is. Don't worry-I'm here to confirm that he really was worried about you."
"Yeah, sure... I believe you. I'm sure the real reason he panicked is because he missed me."
Both girls burst out laughing.
"Glad to see you two are enjoying yourselves, at my expense."
Freya grinned but then tilted her head slightly. "But seriously, Leon... are you really worried about me?"
Leon met her gaze. "Yeah. I just want to make sure you're okay."
Freya leaned back in her chair, exhaling softly. "I'm fine. I've got a private doctor staying here to keep an eye on me, so there's really nothing to worry about."
"A private doctor, huh? I guess I shouldn't be surprised. Looking at this place, you really do live like royalty."
"I told you—I'm super rich. You just didn't believe me before."
Leon nodded. "I believed you. I never doubted that."
The conversation between them flowed easily, lighthearted and filled with laughter. But after a while, Leon's attention drifted, his eyes drawn to something across the room.
On the far wall, there were several framed photos displayed. His gaze locked on them, narrowing slightly as a strange feeling stirred inside him.
Without saying a word, Leon stood up. His sudden movement caught both Freya and Lily by surprise, and they turned to watch him.
"Leon?" Freya raised an eyebrow, confused.

But Leon didn't respond immediately. He walked slowly toward the photo wall. His gaze focused on one particular picture-a photo of a young girl standing between two adults, who were clearly her parents. The girl looked no older than five years old, her brown hair tied in loose pigtails.
Leon's mind raced as he stared at the photo. It wasn't the adults that caught his attention-it was the girl in the middle.
There was something strangely familiar about her. That face... those eyes...
It reminded him of someone.
"Leon?" Lily's voice broke through his thoughts.
Leon turned to face them. "Freya... is this girl in the photo... you?"

"Glad to see you two are enjoying yourselves, at my expense."
Freya grinned but then tilted her head slightly.
"But seriously, Leon... are you really worried about me?"
Leon met her gaze.
"Yeah.
I just want to make sure you're okay."
Freya leaned back in her chair, exhaling softly.
"I'm fine.
I've got a private doctor staying here to keep an eye on me, so there's really nothing to worry about."
"A private doctor, huh?
I guess I shouldn't be surprised.
Looking at this place, you really do live like royalty."
"I told you—I'm super rich.
You just didn't believe me before."
Leon nodded.
"I believed you.
I never doubted that."
The conversation between them flowed easily, lighthearted and filled with laughter.
But after a while, Leon's attention drifted, his eyes drawn to something across the room.
On the far wall, there were several framed photos displayed.
His gaze locked on them, narrowing slightly as a strange feeling stirred inside him.
Without saying a word, Leon stood up.
His sudden movement caught both Freya and Lily by surprise, and they turned to watch him.
"Leon?" Freya raised an eyebrow, confused.
But Leon didn't respond immediately.
He walked slowly toward the photo wall.
His gaze focused on one particular picture-a photo of a young girl standing between two adults, who were clearly her parents.
The girl looked no older than five years old, her brown hair tied in loose pigtails.
Leon's mind raced as he stared at the photo.
It wasn't the adults that caught his attention-it was the girl in the middle.
There was something strangely familiar about her.
That face... those eyes...
It reminded him of someone.
"Leon?" Lily's voice broke through his thoughts.
Leon turned to face them.
"Freya... is this girl in the photo... you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 737: Dissidia’s New Era (Full-Length)
paragraphs: "Freya... is this girl in the photo... you?"
Leon tilted his head slightly as he asked.
Freya blinked, then let out a small laugh. "Yes... that's me. Why? Were you captivated by my cuteness as a kid, huh?"
Lily, standing between them, gave both of them a flat look.
Leon didn't laugh. His expression remained thoughtful, and he murmured softly, "Are you..."
His words trailed off.
Freya took a step closer, crossing her arms. "What? What are you trying to say?"
Leon's gaze finally lifted to meet hers. "Are you... the rich little girl..."
Freya raised a brow. "Yes, I've been rich since I was a kid. What's your point?"
Leon shook his head. "You're the rich little girl who was... annoying."
Freya blinked in shock. "What?!"
Leon took a step back. "Yes... you're the annoying little rich girl who always tried to play with the other kids at the park."
"Say that again!"
"You told everyone your name was Freda back then!" Leon continued. "But now I realize... you weren't Freda. You're Freya. So, what's your real name?"
"Say that again."
"You were bossy, annoying, and you always tried to order the other kids around."

"Annoying? Seriously? That's your impression of me?!" She stomped her foot and took another step closer, glaring up at him. "You should be grateful that you finally get to reunite with your wonderful, rich childhood friend! Doesn't this bring back precious memories for you?"
"No. What I remember is you being annoying. That's the impression I had. You were bossy and stubborn."
"Leon... this is my house. You're not going to get away from my wrath this time!"
Leon's grin widened as he took a step back. "Oh? Still want to try?"
Without another word, Freya lunged at him, and Leon immediately spun on his heel and took off running, laughing as she chased after him through the house.
"Leon! Come back here! You're going to regret this!" Freya shouted.
Lily stood silently, watching the two of them chase each other around the sofa.

Freya had grabbed several cushions from the couch, throwing them at Leon with full force, not holding back at all. The pillows sailed through the air, barely missing him as he darted around the furniture.

When Leon ran past a decorative vase precariously perched on a side table, Freya hesitated, lowering her arm to avoid knocking it over. But once he was clear of the fragile item, she resumed her attack, continuing to throw pillows at him despite not landing a single hit.
"Leon!" Freya yelled, still chasing him. "You won't escape my wrath this time! I can order everyone in this house to catch you if I want!"
Leon glanced back over his shoulder, grinning.
"See? This is exactly how you were when we were kids, Freya! Bossy and ordering people around!"

"That's not true! I was cute! Kind! And friendly to everyone! You're just refusing to admit it!" She huffed, grabbing another pillow. "Leon, you have to acknowledge that I was a delight to be around. If not, you're not leaving this house in one piece!"

Meanwhile, Lily sat back down on the sofa, watching them with an amused expression. The whole scene was ridiculous, but at the same time, it was hard not to enjoy seeing Leon and Freya bicker like this.
As they ran past again, Leon shouted,
"Lily! Did you know all along that Freya was the annoying rich girl from our childhood?"
Lily shrugged, raising her voice so they could hear her.
"No, Leon. I just found out too."
Freya slowed down slightly and turned toward Lily.
"Lily! Tell me the truth. What does Leon say about me when I'm not around? Don't lie!"
Lily sighed, then stood up and raised her voice to answer.

"Leon always asks about you, Freya. He worries about you more than he shows. And-" she smiled, "he used to tell me stories about how happy he was when he played with you as a kid. He always smiled when he talked about those memories."
"Lily! Stop making things up!"
"See, Leon! You have to admit it now! You missed me. You liked playing with me. You've always cared about me!"
"That's... not exactly how I remember it."
"Stop running, Leon! Accept my anger like a man!"
"Are you sure you can catch me? Let's see if you still have the stamina!"
"Leon! Get back here!"

It had been about one month in Yunatea Time since Alora's coronation as Queen of Dissidia Kingdom. The time that had passed felt both short and long, as the entire kingdom had been in constant motion, busy with recovery efforts and adjusting to life under new leadership. For Alora, the past month had been critical. As the new ruler, she had been fully immersed in managing the kingdom's affairs, overseeing repairs to the city, and rebuilding trust among her people. The kingdom had taken heavy damage during the last battle, but slowly, life in the capital was returning to normal.
Trade routes had reopened.
Government activities resumed.
And diplomatic visits from neighboring kingdoms had become a frequent occurrence, with many rulers stopping by to congratulate Queen Alora on her ascension-and to discuss future alliances.
However, today marked another pivotal moment in Dissidia's recovery: a ceremony honoring the heroes who had fought to defend the kingdom during the demon invasion.

The event was grand and formal, held in the royal hall, with knights, commanders, and key players from various guilds in attendance. This was a time to recognize bravery and reward those who had risked their lives to protect the capital.

The Vensalor Guild was among those receiving special recognition for their efforts. Broken, Goldrich, Maylock, Jovina, and others stood proudly, representing their guild as one of the key forces that had turned the tide of the battle.
But not everyone chose to accept the kingdom's offer of recognition.
The Shadow Wolves and Horde of Hell refused to attend the ceremony.
Despite joining the fight at the last moment to help defend the capital, they rejected any form of official acknowledgment or alliance with the kingdom.
To accept the kingdom's honor meant building ties with the crown, and it was clear that both guilds preferred to keep their independence.

The Horde of Hell eventually returned to their original continent, disappearing from Dissidia entirely. As for the Shadow Wolves, they remained wandering within Dissidia's borders. While the crown granted them an official pardon for their previous hostile actions, the Shadow Wolves were still watched closely by the kingdom's forces whenever they roamed near the capital. There was no trust, only a fragile truce.

During the past month, Broken had immersed himself in crafting commissions for his guild members, focusing on weapons for each of them. He worked tirelessly to ensure that those who played a critical role in the war-Goldrich, Elincia, Optimus, Jovina, and others- received personalized gear to boost their combat effectiveness.
Yet, despite all his efforts, he still hadn't achieved a Legendary-grade item to complete his blacksmith quest.
Time was running out.
He knew he couldn't delay his journey to the West Continent much longer. But before leaving, he had resolved to spend the next week finalizing his golem designs.
Later that evening, Broken walked through the halls of the royal castle, heading toward
Alora's room. Now that she had officially moved into the main castle, her quarters were far more lavish, fit for a queen.
As Broken entered, he saw Alora sitting in the middle of the room, her gaze lighting up the moment she spotted him.
The girl stood up gracefully and smiled. "Hi, My King."
Broken couldn't help but smile as he walked toward her. When they met halfway, she wrapped her arms around him, pulling him into
They stayed like that for a long moment.
warm embrace.

For Broken, moments like these were precious-a chance to release the weight of his exhaustion, even if just for a little while. He had spent countless hours in the workshop, pushing himself to the limit. But here, in Alora's arms, he allowed himself to breathe.
When they finally pulled back, Alora looked up at him.

"We're holding the official ceremony for our marriage in one week," she said softly. "Everything is prepared, and the announcement will be made soon. People will call you King Broken-the first player in Immortal Legacy to become a king."
She smiled, tapping his shoulder and chest, which still had traces of soot and dust from his blacksmithing work.
"Your reputation has already spread across Dissidia. Everything will go smoothly. There's nothing to worry about."
Broken reached out, gently taking both of her hands in his. His gaze softened as he said.
"You don't have to worry about me. I'm not afraid of anything. I'll face any challenge with open arms."
"I knew you'd say that. You always do."
She stepped closer, wrapping her arms around him once more. Broken leaned down, gently stroking her hair, his fingers weaving through the strands.

Alora grew up surrounded by rejection, constantly facing prejudice for being half-human, half-elf. It had shaped her into someone who carried the weight of being an outsider, always navigating the fine line between two worlds.
This experience was why she couldn't shake the concern that haunted her thoughts about Broken-a player who now held such a prominent place in her life.

No matter how much they achieved, players would always be seen as outsiders by the people of Yunatea. And for a player to hold an important position of power? That was something many would find difficult-if not impossible to accept.
"My priority is you." His voice was soft, steady, and sincere.
Alora closed her eyes, resting her head against his chest, holding him tightly.
"And I'll always be by your side," she whispered.
In that quiet moment, all the noise of the outside world seemed to fade away, leaving just the two of them in their own little sanctuary.

chapters.title: Chapter 738: The Royal Wedding Gossip Hour
paragraphs: "Tora! Ha ha ha! I'm thrilled to have you here on the show tonight. This is such a monumental moment!" The talk show setting was nothing short of fantastical luxury. The room exuded an opulent yet whimsical atmosphere, with golden chandeliers suspended in mid-air. On one side of the stage sat Brando, the charismatic host, dressed sharply in a black suit. Seated across from him, Tora, a member of the Vensalor Guild, gave a small smile as he adjusted his posture.

"I know you're now part of the famed Vensalor Guild," Brando continued. "And let's be honest—your guild, especially your guild leader, is at the center of every conversation right now! Nobody can believe what's happening! Her Majesty Queen Alora is marrying Broken?! Come on, Tora, you've got to share some insider details with us tonight."
Tora smiled politely.

"Brando, thank you for having me on the show." He nodded slightly before continuing. "Yes, this is undeniably a huge moment. Broken's contributions during the last war, combined with his relationship with Queen Alora—well, that's something that's been growing for a long time. What people don't realize is that their bond was cultivated through countless experiences, many of which aren't known to the public. This wasn't something that just happened overnight. It's the result of persistence, dedication, and..."
Tora trailed off briefly, shaking his head with a small smile before finishing.
"...only someone like Broken could achieve something like this."
Brando let out a hearty laugh, clapping his hands.
"Ha ha ha! Of course, you'd sing praises about your guild master, wouldn't you?" He grinned. "But now, let's hear another perspective."

Brando turned toward the next guest. "Joining us tonight is someone who's had several run-ins with Broken in the past—both during unexpected encounters and even in competitive settings. Please welcome... Titonor, an Advanced Rank Blacksmith!"
The camera panned to Titonor.

"Well, I'm not a stranger to Broken," he said, his tone calm. "I've known him since he first started gaining attention back in Clario Town... no, not too far back. Maybe just one or two years Yunatea time. Yes, I'd say I've got a decent understanding of how he acts, especially when we end up competing against each other."
Brando's eyes lit up as he jumped in.
"Oh, you mean the competition where he won by crafting that Legendary-grade spear, right?"
"Yes!" Titonor replied. "That was... sheer luck."
Before Brando could respond, Tora smirked, leaning forward slightly. "It's not luck if he's able to do it more than once."
Titonor let out a chuckle, shaking his head. "It's still luck. He hasn't managed to pull off something like that again, has he?"
"Oh, are you fishing for me to tell you just how many Legendary-grade items Broken has crafted since then? Is that it?"
Brando waved a hand, cutting in with a laugh.

"Alright, alright, let's not start a blacksmith war on the show! I can feel the energy between you two already." He gestured back toward Titonor. "Let's stay focused. So, Titonor, what do you think is extraordinary about Broken that's gotten him to where he is now?"
Titonor wasted no time, his tone turning sharp.

"He's got luck. And he's surrounded by wealthy backers. Everyone knows the reputation of the Ass Guild. Whatever's going on in their heads, I'm sure Broken figured out how to leverage that to his advantage. That's how they ended up joining his guild. And now? Marrying Queen Alora? That's just the icing on the cake for a victory that wasn't solely his effort.
"Titonor, were you even watching the whole war?" Tora said. "Because I was there. I saw it all unfold in real time. Do you need me to walk you through everything from the beginning?"

"Alright!" Brando interjected, clapping his hands with a wide grin to break the escalating tension. "I know that was one hell of a war—an absolutely incredible event! I wasn't in the capital when it happened, but my eyes never left the broadcast, courtesy of Tora and Max. And yes, I saw it—the moment Broken held back the meteor. With... What kind of item or skill was that?!"
Titonor chimed in quickly.
"That wouldn't have been possible without everyone's contribution in the battle. Frostedge and Galactron were there, too, and let's not forget the thousands of players fighting on the ground."
"Oh, now tell me that it would've ended just as well without Broken?" Tora quipped.
Brando nodded thoughtfully, leaning forward.
"That's also a big question. Just what kind of item was that? How did Broken manage to get the right thing at the right time?"
Titonor smirked, shaking his head as he added, "Oh, maybe Broken knew it was going to happen all along."
Tora's expression didn't falter as he shot back. "That's why I keep saying, Titonor, you'll never fully grasp what's happening. Broken is far beyond what you can understand, even in blacksmithing."

Titonor straightened slightly, his tone now more serious. "I've been a blacksmith since the very first day Immortal Legacy launched. I can take on any challenge from any blacksmith across Yunatea and answer all their questions with ease."
Tora raised a brow but didn't respond.
Brando seized the moment, turning toward Titonor with an eager grin.
"Now, Titonor, enlighten us casuals about blacksmithing. What do you think Broken did to craft an item capable of stopping that meteor while involving so many people in the process?"
Titonor exhaled, rubbing his chin as if considering the question carefully.
"Well, to pull off something like that..." he began, his tone slowing. "It had to be a high-level crafted item, likely Legendary or close to it. But that alone wouldn't cut it."
Titonor paused, his hand resting on his chin as he continued,
"The materials must've been incredibly expensive and versatile. Like, I don't know, maybe a ton of soul stones."
Brando's eyebrows shot up.
"A ton of soul stones? Just one is already a fortune!"

"Exactly," Titonor nodded. "Soul stones are used to amplify effects. If the item was crafted with a single, specific purpose, there are really only two possible explanations. Either the blueprint already existed, or there was access to something like a creative blueprint—an item that allows someone to design a unique blueprint tailored to their needs, setting the materials and even finer details manually."
Brando tapped the armrest of his chair, nodding thoughtfully. "I have to say, that explanation makes a lot of sense."
Tora smirked, leaning slightly toward Titonor. "I'll give you credit, Titonor. Your knowledge of blacksmithing is impressive."

"But I'm not convinced Broken had access to something like that. How could he get such an item? And the materials—how would he manage to gather them, especially in a time-sensitive, high-pressure situation?"
Tora raised a brow at him. "And I'm sure you don't know every single person backing Broken in detail, do you?"

Before Tora could reply, Brando chimed in with a grin. "I know for a fact that someone important from Northstar is part of the Vensalor Guild. Doesn't that make this kind of feat entirely achievable?"

It's the result of persistence, dedication, and..."
Tora trailed off briefly, shaking his head with a small smile before finishing.
"...only someone like Broken could achieve something like this."
Brando let out a hearty laugh, clapping his hands.
"Ha ha ha!
Of course, you'd sing praises about your guild master, wouldn't you?" He grinned.
"But now, let's hear another perspective."
Brando turned toward the next guest.
"Joining us tonight is someone who's had several run-ins with Broken in the past—both during unexpected encounters and even in competitive settings.
Please welcome...
Titonor, an Advanced Rank Blacksmith!"
The camera panned to Titonor.
"Well, I'm not a stranger to Broken," he said, his tone calm.
"I've known him since he first started gaining attention back in Clario Town... no, not too far back.
Maybe just one or two years Yunatea time.
Yes, I'd say I've got a decent understanding of how he acts, especially when we end up competing against each other."
Brando's eyes lit up as he jumped in.
"Oh, you mean the competition where he won by crafting that Legendary-grade spear, right?"
"Yes!" Titonor replied.
"That was... sheer luck."
Before Brando could respond, Tora smirked, leaning forward slightly.
"It's not luck if he's able to do it more than once."
Titonor let out a chuckle, shaking his head.
"It's still luck.
He hasn't managed to pull off something like that again, has he?"
"Oh, are you fishing for me to tell you just how many Legendary-grade items Broken has crafted since then?
Is that it?"
Brando waved a hand, cutting in with a laugh.
"Alright, alright, let's not start a blacksmith war on the show!
I can feel the energy between you two already." He gestured back toward Titonor.
"Let's stay focused.
So, Titonor, what do you think is extraordinary about Broken that's gotten him to where he is now?"
Titonor wasted no time, his tone turning sharp.
"He's got luck.
And he's surrounded by wealthy backers.
Everyone knows the reputation of the Ass Guild.
Whatever's going on in their heads, I'm sure Broken figured out how to leverage that to his advantage.
That's how they ended up joining his guild.
And now?
Marrying Queen Alora?
That's just the icing on the cake for a victory that wasn't solely his effort.
"Titonor, were you even watching the whole war?" Tora said.
"Because I was there.
I saw it all unfold in real time.
Do you need me to walk you through everything from the beginning?"
"Alright!" Brando interjected, clapping his hands with a wide grin to break the escalating tension.
"I know that was one hell of a war—an absolutely incredible event!
I wasn't in the capital when it happened, but my eyes never left the broadcast, courtesy of Tora and Max.
And yes, I saw it—the moment Broken held back the meteor.
With...
What kind of item or skill was that?!"
Titonor chimed in quickly.
"That wouldn't have been possible without everyone's contribution in the battle.
Frostedge and Galactron were there, too, and let's not forget the thousands of players fighting on the ground."
"Oh, now tell me that it would've ended just as well without Broken?" Tora quipped.
Brando nodded thoughtfully, leaning forward.
"That's also a big question.
Just what kind of item was that?
How did Broken manage to get the right thing at the right time?"
Titonor smirked, shaking his head as he added, "Oh, maybe Broken knew it was going to happen all along."
Tora's expression didn't falter as he shot back.
"That's why I keep saying, Titonor, you'll never fully grasp what's happening.
Broken is far beyond what you can understand, even in blacksmithing."
Titonor straightened slightly, his tone now more serious.
"I've been a blacksmith since the very first day Immortal Legacy launched.
I can take on any challenge from any blacksmith across Yunatea and answer all their questions with ease."
Tora raised a brow but didn't respond.
Brando seized the moment, turning toward Titonor with an eager grin.
"Now, Titonor, enlighten us casuals about blacksmithing.
What do you think Broken did to craft an item capable of stopping that meteor while involving so many people in the process?"
Titonor exhaled, rubbing his chin as if considering the question carefully.
"Well, to pull off something like that..." he began, his tone slowing.
"It had to be a high-level crafted item, likely Legendary or close to it.
But that alone wouldn't cut it."
Titonor paused, his hand resting on his chin as he continued,
"The materials must've been incredibly expensive and versatile.
Like, I don't know, maybe a ton of soul stones."
Brando's eyebrows shot up.
"A ton of soul stones?
Just one is already a fortune!"
"Exactly," Titonor nodded.
"Soul stones are used to amplify effects.
If the item was crafted with a single, specific purpose, there are really only two possible explanations.

Either the blueprint already existed, or there was access to something like a creative blueprint—an item that allows someone to design a unique blueprint tailored to their needs, setting the materials and even finer details manually."
Brando tapped the armrest of his chair, nodding thoughtfully.
"I have to say, that explanation makes a lot of sense."
Tora smirked, leaning slightly toward Titonor.
"I'll give you credit, Titonor.
Your knowledge of blacksmithing is impressive."
"But I'm not convinced Broken had access to something like that.
How could he get such an item?
And the materials—how would he manage to gather them, especially in a time-sensitive, high-pressure situation?"
Tora raised a brow at him.
"And I'm sure you don't know every single person backing Broken in detail, do you?"
Before Tora could reply, Brando chimed in with a grin.
"I know for a fact that someone important from Northstar is part of the Vensalor Guild.
Doesn't that make this kind of feat entirely achievable?"

chapters.title: Chapter 739: The Crown and the Sword United
paragraphs: "Today marks a historic moment for both Immortal Legacy and the world of Yunatea!"
Brando, back in the familiar luxurious talk show setting, was as energetic as ever. This time, however, his guests were different, bringing fresh perspectives to the lively discussion.
"I know all of you are filled with excitement as we witness the wedding of Her Majesty Queen Alora and Broken, leader of the Vensalor Guild."
He gestured to his two guests, seated on either side of him.

"To delve deeper into this extraordinary moment, I've invited two familiar faces-figures who, I'm sure, need no introduction given their connections to the very people we're discussing today. Please welcome... Lucy and TheKnight!"
The two guests waved at the camera, smiling warmly.
Brando turned to the audience, pointing briefly at Lucy.

"Lucy is the leader of the Valantar Guild Alliance, known for their ambitious-and sometimes controversial-efforts in battles like their push against Slumdon Town. While the outcome of those battles might not have gone their way, there's no denying their significance in the larger narrative. And most importantly... during the last war, Lucy and her alliance came to the capital to lend their strength to the fight!"
Lucy smiled, her expression polite but tinged with awkwardness, and gave another small nod. Brando's attention shifted to the other guest.

"And as for TheKnight, well, if we're talking about Queen Alora, there's no one more vocal in their support of her than him. TheKnight is widely recognized as the leader of her official fan club, a truly remarkable achievement!"
TheKnight straightened proudly. "It's an honor to be here."
Brando chuckled, leaning forward.
"Alright, let's dive in. Starting with TheKnight-what do you think will be the reaction from both NPCs and fellow players regarding this marriage?"
"I'm sure this will spark anger among many of the Queen's fans," TheKnight said.
Brando raised an eyebrow. "Oh, you're being quite vocal here, aren't you?"
"Yeah, I mean... no one really knows who Broken is. His contributions are vague at best. Even in the last war, he only showed up toward the end."

TheKnight paused, his expression hardening. "I'm not convinced this marriage is happening for pure reasons. Let's be real-there's something about Broken that feels... off. He seems to have some kind of special power or influential backing behind him. Even the Valantar Guild Alliance, who were initially his enemies, are now supporting him. It raises a lot of questions." Lucy's eyes narrowed as she glared at him. "That's quite the accusation without any proof, TheKnight," she snapped.
But TheKnight wasn't done. "Tell me I'm wrong. Isn't the reason your alliance aligned with Broken because you're chasing popularity? You saw the influence you'd gain by siding with him, didn't you?"
Brando quickly interjected, raising his hands in a calming gesture.
"Oh, wow, this is heating up fast! Let's take a step back and refocus, shall we?"

He turned to Lucy. "Lucy, from your perspective, what truly brought Broken and Queen Alora together? And while you're at it, could you share your journey-how you went from opposing Broken to becoming one of his supporters?"
Lucy took a deep breath, her voice steady as she began to speak.
"That's love! Pure love!"

The room fell silent for a moment as her words lingered in the air. Then, all eyes turned toward the screen, where Queen Alora and Broken stood facing each other in their wedding attire, their expressions soft and filled with emotion.
Lucy pointed toward the screen.

"Only those who understand true love can see the sincerity and affection in their eyes. Someone idolizing the Queen blindly, like TheKnight, will only spout baseless accusations. If you're truly a devoted fan of Queen Alora, then open your eyes and see how they look at each other-with pure love!"
She turned back to TheKnight.

"As for why I now support Broken? It's because I realized we were wrong. What we did in the past was unjustified-they were only defending themselves. There's no reason to keep antagonizing someone who never intended harm to anyone. Without Broken, the war would never have ended. He stopped the meteor, and he's the one who struck down Vocalor! There's no doubt about that!"
The screen shifted, showing the ceremony preparations, with Queen Alora and Broken exchanging glances as the final steps of the wedding were about to begin.
Brando leaned back in his chair, a warm smile spreading across his face as he added, "I have to agree, Lucy. You can see the love in their eyes-how deeply they care for each other."
Broken stood in a midnight-black suit with silver accents, while Queen Alora wore a gown of shimmering starlight silver.

The wedding venue was the same hall where Alora's coronation had taken place, now transformed into a scene of romance and grandeur. Rows of polished chairs, draped in royal blue and silver, lined the aisle.
At the altar stood High Priest Elandir, the same figure who had crowned Alora, his emerald robes glinting faintly in the light as he prepared to begin the ceremony.
Broken stood, his gaze fixed on Alora.

They had faced countless challenges together: the battle against the Named Demon, the defense of the capital city, and all the struggles in between. What many didn't know was that they were already legally husband and wife before this day. Now, they stood before the world, ready to seal their union in an official ceremony.
"I'm so proud to stand here before you today," Alora whispered softly.
Broken's lips curved into a faint smile. "That's supposed to be my line."
With a quiet chuckle, they turned together to face High Priest Elandir, ready to begin the next chapter of their shared journey.
High Priest Elandir raised his hands.

"Today, we gather not only to celebrate the union of two hearts but the unity of strength and leadership that will shape the future of Dissidia Kingdom. Before us stand two figures who have proven their dedication through trials, battles, and trust."
He turned first to Broken.
"Broken, leader of the Vensalor Guild, do you vow to stand beside Her Majesty Queen Alora, to be her shield, her sword, and her support in all things?"
Broken, meeting Alora's gaze, spoke with firm resolve.
"I vow to protect her, to guide her, and to give my all to ensure her reign is unshakable."
Elandir then turned to Alora.

"Alora Rogwyn, Queen Regnant of Dissidia Kingdom, do you vow to uphold the legacy of your ancestors, to lead with wisdom, and to cherish the one who stands beside you as both your partner and your strength?"
Alora's voice was steady. "I vow to honor him, to lead with grace, and to ensure that together, we bring prosperity to our kingdom."
Elandir extended his arms wide.

"With the blessings of the Seven Deities who watch over this world, I call upon the ancestors of Dissidia to bear witness to this moment, I declare Broken as King Consort of Dissidia, protector and advisor to the throne. Together, he and Queen Alora shall stand as the Crown and the Sword, a beacon of hope and strength for our kingdom."
He turned to the crowd, his voice booming.
"All hail Queen Alora, Sovereign Ruler of Dissidia Kingdom!"
The crowd erupted into a chorus of voices.
"All hail the Queen!"
"All hail Queen Alora!" Elandir raised his hands again.
"All hail King Broken, Protector of Dissidia!"
The room shook with the enthusiastic response.
"All hail King Broken!"
"All hail the Sword of the Kingdom!"
