chapters.title: Chapter 749: Aego! Move out!
paragraphs: "We need a name," Broken said, turning toward Ronan and Mizuki.
"A name?" Ronan raised an eyebrow. "For what, King?"
"A name for the ship. This is going to be our main vessel at sea, so I'm giving you both the chance to name it," Broken replied.
Ronan glanced at Mizuki. "Got any ideas, Mizuki?"

Mizuki shook her head and looked back at Broken. "King, I think you should name the golem yourself. We want to call it something that comes from you-something meaningful for the creation you've worked so hard for."
Ronan nodded in agreement with Mizuki's words.

Broken smiled at their response, though inwardly, he had hoped they would pick the name because, frankly, he was stumped. He tended to go for simple names-something easy to pronounce, often a play on the original name of the golem, like calling Zephyris Sentinel "Zepy."
Now here he was, stuck with Aegis Voyager as a starting point. What kind of name would be fitting yet simple enough?
Damn it, he thought. Why do I even have to name it? Can't the system just auto-generate one? "Aego?" he muttered under his breath.
"That's adorable, King," Mizuki said, her face lighting up.
"Really?" he asked, a little surprised.
Mizuki nodded enthusiastically. "Yes, it's perfect. It's short, catchy, and cute!"
"Alright then," Broken said, a small grin tugging at his lips. "Aego it is!"
[Name: Aego - Aegis Voyager]
[Grade: Legendary]
[Tier: 4]
[Level: 250]
[Skills - 4]
Broken smiled softly as he saw the golem's tier displayed: Tier 4.

He couldn't help but chuckle. Tier 4 was the high expectation he had been aiming for, his most ambitious hope. This meant the golem possessed self-repairing abilities-able to use its own core to reinforce and even regenerate its structure.
Of course, major damage would still require manual repairs, but the golem's system ensured those repairs could be completed with near perfection.

With Tier 4, the ship also inherited the defensive systems granted at Tier 3. Essentially, this meant the golem had a natural defense mechanism, like hardening certain areas when under attack or during a collision.
As for the golem's offensive capabilities, Broken couldn't quite picture how they would function. It seemed like something he would need to test out firsthand.
[Ocean Veil (Active Skill):
The ship cloaks itself in shimmering water magic, making it difficult to target and blending it with its surroundings.]
The first skill the golem possessed was Ocean Veil-a skill Broken hadn't expected at all.

With this ability, the golem could camouflage itself within the vast expanse of the ocean. The question was, did this skill only work against ships and vessels on the surface, or would it also affect sea creatures lurking below?

Regardless, the potential was undeniable. This skill could prove invaluable, especially in situations where evasion was critical. If they encountered a threat they needed to avoid, Ocean Veil could ensure their escape.
It was an extraordinary skill for a ship to have, one that could turn the tide of danger in their favor.
[Oceanstride Boost (Active Skill):
Activates the ship's turbine for a massive speed boost, leaving a glowing trail of energy behind.
Effect: Increases speed by 100% for 20 seconds. The glowing trail slows pursuing enemies by 30%.]

The next skill was Oceanstride Boost. Broken was always fascinated by mobility-focused abilities, especially in his type of golems that thrived on speed and maneuverability. It reminded him of Beebot and Zepy, both of whom had skills in a similar vein.

Although this skill wasn't something they'd need to activate repeatedly-since long sea voyages required careful resource management-it could be a game-changer in critical moments. If they encountered an adversary they needed to evade, Oceanstride Boost would allow them to break away quickly.
Once again, here was another skill tailored perfectly for escape mechanisms. Truly ideal for their mission.
[Ripple Phase (Active Skill):
Temporarily phases the ship into an ethereal state, allowing it to pass through obstacles.
Grants invincibility for 5 seconds and lets the ship move through enemies or terrain without collision.]
What the hell?
Broken blinked, rereading the skill description.
Ripple Phase?!

The skill allowed the ship to enter an ethereal state, phasing through obstacles as if they weren't even there. But wait-did this also apply to the passengers on board? It would be bizarre (and dangerous) if activating this mode somehow caused everyone inside to plummet into the ocean.
He'd have to test this one right away, especially since they were still near the shore.

Still, if the skill worked seamlessly for both the ship and its passengers, it would be incredible when paired with the first two skills. Combining Ocean Veil, Oceanstride Boost, and Ripple Phase would create a nearly foolproof escape system. Camouflage to disappear, speed to flee, and phasing to bypass any physical barriers-all tools for evasion in the harsh and unpredictable sea.

But there it was. Three skills entirely focused on escape mechanisms. While this might seem limited, it made perfect sense for their situation. In the open ocean, where danger could come from any direction, survival often meant running rather than fighting. After all, the sea wasn't their battleground; a single misstep could lead to disaster if the ship were to sink.

Escape-focused skills were not just practical-they were lifesaving. Even for a legendary- grade ship, Broken found the specialization impressive. The extraordinary nature of the abilities likely compensated for the sheer size of the vessel, which was no doubt a significant factor in its energy demands.

Moving a ship this massive required immense power, and the golem core would surely deplete faster than usual during extended journeys. They'd need to prepare for this by hunting sea monsters along the way to replenish their supply of cores.
The stakes were high, but with these abilities, the ship had the potential to be their greatest tool-or their most demanding challenge.
[Leviathan's Fury (Active Skill):
The ship channels the wrath of the seas, summoning colossal waves imbued with destructive energy to crush its foes.
Generates a massive tidal wave, dealing heavy water-element damage and knocking back enemies. Sea creatures are stunned for 5 seconds.]
And then there it was-the final skill. Leviathan's Fury!

Finally, an offensive ability, and judging by the description, it was nothing short of extraordinary. This was a massive area-of-effect skill that could summon colossal waves to attack enemies within a designated zone. Not only that, but it also stunned sea creatures for five seconds a remarkable power.

Even so, Broken knew the ship didn't necessarily need offensive capabilities. After all, everyone aboard could contribute to its defense if the situation demanded it. As long as the ship could hold its ground and avoid sinking, that was already a victory in itself. More importantly, the ship's ability to maneuver effectively, utilizing the mechanics built into it, was the real priority. For that reason, Broken was eager to see how the turbines would perform. Would they operate as smoothly as the design promised?
He glanced at the others. "Let's take it out for a spin and see how it handles."
"Let's go!" came the unified response.
One by one, they climbed aboard. Broken, Ronan, and Mizuki quickly moved toward the control room, where Broken would install the golem core and bring the ship to life for its very first movement.
The system came to life smoothly-everything seemed to be working perfectly.
"All right!" he said, the excitement building in his voice.
He took a deep breath, standing tall as he faced the controls.
"Aego! Move out!" he commanded with determination.

sentences.text: "We need a name," Broken said, turning toward Ronan and Mizuki.
"A name?" Ronan raised an eyebrow.
"For what, King?"
"A name for the ship.
This is going to be our main vessel at sea, so I'm giving you both the chance to name it," Broken replied.
Ronan glanced at Mizuki.
"Got any ideas, Mizuki?"
Mizuki shook her head and looked back at Broken.
"King, I think you should name the golem yourself.
We want to call it something that comes from you-something meaningful for the creation you've worked so hard for."
Ronan nodded in agreement with Mizuki's words.
Broken smiled at their response, though inwardly, he had hoped they would pick the name because, frankly, he was stumped.
He tended to go for simple names-something easy to pronounce, often a play on the original name of the golem, like calling Zephyris Sentinel "Zepy."
Now here he was, stuck with Aegis Voyager as a starting point.
What kind of name would be fitting yet simple enough?
Damn it, he thought.
Why do I even have to name it?
Can't the system just auto-generate one?
"Aego?" he muttered under his breath.
"That's adorable, King," Mizuki said, her face lighting up.
"Really?" he asked, a little surprised.
Mizuki nodded enthusiastically.
"Yes, it's perfect.
It's short, catchy, and cute!"
"Alright then," Broken said, a small grin tugging at his lips.
"Aego it is!"
[Name: Aego - Aegis Voyager]
[Grade: Legendary]
[Tier: 4]
[Level: 250]
[Skills - 4]
Broken smiled softly as he saw the golem's tier displayed: Tier 4.
He couldn't help but chuckle.
Tier 4 was the high expectation he had been aiming for, his most ambitious hope.
This meant the golem possessed self-repairing abilities-able to use its own core to reinforce and even regenerate its structure.
Of course, major damage would still require manual repairs, but the golem's system ensured those repairs could be completed with near perfection.
With Tier 4, the ship also inherited the defensive systems granted at Tier 3.
Essentially, this meant the golem had a natural defense mechanism, like hardening certain areas when under attack or during a collision.
As for the golem's offensive capabilities, Broken couldn't quite picture how they would function.
It seemed like something he would need to test out firsthand.
[Ocean Veil (Active Skill):
The ship cloaks itself in shimmering water magic, making it difficult to target and blending it with its surroundings.]
The first skill the golem possessed was Ocean Veil-a skill Broken hadn't expected at all.
With this ability, the golem could camouflage itself within the vast expanse of the ocean.
The question was, did this skill only work against ships and vessels on the surface, or would it also affect sea creatures lurking below?
Regardless, the potential was undeniable.
This skill could prove invaluable, especially in situations where evasion was critical.
If they encountered a threat they needed to avoid, Ocean Veil could ensure their escape.
It was an extraordinary skill for a ship to have, one that could turn the tide of danger in their favor.
[Oceanstride Boost (Active Skill):
Activates the ship's turbine for a massive speed boost, leaving a glowing trail of energy behind.
Effect: Increases speed by 100% for 20 seconds.
The glowing trail slows pursuing enemies by 30%.]
The next skill was Oceanstride Boost.
Broken was always fascinated by mobility-focused abilities, especially in his type of golems that thrived on speed and maneuverability.
It reminded him of Beebot and Zepy, both of whom had skills in a similar vein.
Although this skill wasn't something they'd need to activate repeatedly-since long sea voyages required careful resource management-it could be a game-changer in critical moments.
If they encountered an adversary they needed to evade, Oceanstride Boost would allow them to break away quickly.
Once again, here was another skill tailored perfectly for escape mechanisms.
Truly ideal for their mission.
[Ripple Phase (Active Skill):
Temporarily phases the ship into an ethereal state, allowing it to pass through obstacles.
Grants invincibility for 5 seconds and lets the ship move through enemies or terrain without collision.]
What the hell?
Broken blinked, rereading the skill description.
Ripple Phase?!
The skill allowed the ship to enter an ethereal state, phasing through obstacles as if they weren't even there.
But wait-did this also apply to the passengers on board?
It would be bizarre (and dangerous) if activating this mode somehow caused everyone inside to plummet into the ocean.
He'd have to test this one right away, especially since they were still near the shore.
Still, if the skill worked seamlessly for both the ship and its passengers, it would be incredible when paired with the first two skills.
Combining Ocean Veil, Oceanstride Boost, and Ripple Phase would create a nearly foolproof escape system.
Camouflage to disappear, speed to flee, and phasing to bypass any physical barriers-all tools for evasion in the harsh and unpredictable sea.
But there it was.
Three skills entirely focused on escape mechanisms.
While this might seem limited, it made perfect sense for their situation.
In the open ocean, where danger could come from any direction, survival often meant running rather than fighting.
After all, the sea wasn't their battleground; a single misstep could lead to disaster if the ship were to sink.
Escape-focused skills were not just practical-they were lifesaving.
Even for a legendary- grade ship, Broken found the specialization impressive.
The extraordinary nature of the abilities likely compensated for the sheer size of the vessel, which was no doubt a significant factor in its energy demands.
Moving a ship this massive required immense power, and the golem core would surely deplete faster than usual during extended journeys.
They'd need to prepare for this by hunting sea monsters along the way to replenish their supply of cores.
The stakes were high, but with these abilities, the ship had the potential to be their greatest tool-or their most demanding challenge.
[Leviathan's Fury (Active Skill):
The ship channels the wrath of the seas, summoning colossal waves imbued with destructive energy to crush its foes.
Generates a massive tidal wave, dealing heavy water-element damage and knocking back enemies.
Sea creatures are stunned for 5 seconds.]
And then there it was-the final skill.
Leviathan's Fury!
Finally, an offensive ability, and judging by the description, it was nothing short of extraordinary.
This was a massive area-of-effect skill that could summon colossal waves to attack enemies within a designated zone.
Not only that, but it also stunned sea creatures for five seconds a remarkable power.
Even so, Broken knew the ship didn't necessarily need offensive capabilities.
After all, everyone aboard could contribute to its defense if the situation demanded it.
As long as the ship could hold its ground and avoid sinking, that was already a victory in itself.
More importantly, the ship's ability to maneuver effectively, utilizing the mechanics built into it, was the real priority.
For that reason, Broken was eager to see how the turbines would perform.
Would they operate as smoothly as the design promised?
He glanced at the others.
"Let's take it out for a spin and see how it handles."
"Let's go!" came the unified response.
One by one, they climbed aboard.
Broken, Ronan, and Mizuki quickly moved toward the control room, where Broken would install the golem core and bring the ship to life for its very first movement.
The system came to life smoothly-everything seemed to be working perfectly.
"All right!" he said, the excitement building in his voice.
He took a deep breath, standing tall as he faced the controls.
"Aego!
Move out!" he commanded with determination.

chapters.title: Chapter 750: The Golem Ship Awakens
paragraphs: Broken monitored the golem console intently as the ship began to move. His eyes were fixed on the interface, carefully watching every aspect of the golem's mechanics. He hoped the ship would fully utilize the systems they had painstakingly designed.
And then...
The moment of truth arrived.

His jaw dropped in awe as the turbines spun to life, propelling the ship forward. Even more astonishingly, the ship began to turn, smoothly adjusting its course as the mechanism for steering kicked in. The massive vessel shifted gracefully toward the open sea.
He wasn't the only one amazed. The entire room erupted in cheers and shouts of excitement as the golem ship moved.
It was really moving!

Broken burst into laughter, overwhelmed with relief. After such a monumental investment of time and resources, the thought of the golem ship being a failure had haunted him. But now, seeing it in action, all that anxiety evaporated.

Taking a step back, he dropped into a nearby chair and leaned into it, watching through the window as the golem ship slowly pulled away from the dock. On the deck outside, the crew celebrated, their cheers echoing across the harbor as they marveled at the sight of the ship moving under its own power.
"We did it, King! We actually did it! Hahaha!" Ronan, still buzzing with energy, practically shouted, his excitement filling the room.
"We did it!" Mizuki exclaimed, leaping with joy before punching Ronan playfully on the shoulder. "Ronan, we're going to explore the seas with this golem ship! This is amazing!"

Broken couldn't help but share in the infectious energy of the moment. A grin spread across his face as he soaked in the celebratory atmosphere. The golem ship was truly pulling away from the harbor now, its massive form gliding further out into the water.

But he reminded himself that this was still just a trial run. They weren't embarking on a full- fledged journey yet. For now, the goal was to put some distance between the ship and the shore to test out the various skills built into the golem.
Still, even with the trials ahead, the success of this moment filled Broken with a deep, undeniable satisfaction.

Broken stood up and began tweaking some of the ship's settings, ensuring everything was optimized for their next steps. One critical adjustment was assigning secondary command control of the golem to Ronan.
The moment the change took effect, Ronan's face froze in shock, his mouth hanging open as he realized he could now operate the ship's console.
"Oh... no way! No way! This is... this is... incredible!" Ronan shouted, his voice bursting with excitement.
"Now you're the captain of this ship. You have full control over Aego," Broken said with a smirk.
"Congratulations, Ronan! You're so lucky!" Mizuki chimed in with a grin.
"Damn, King! Why would you do this?" Ronan laughed, though it was clear he was thrilled. "King, you've seriously made my day-no, my life! This is amazing!"

The team then moved on to fine-tuning Aego's security systems, setting up protocols for responding to potential alarms or danger. After finishing those adjustments, they steered the ship far enough from the shore to test out the golem's skills.

First, they activated the camouflage skill. From inside the ship, it looked as though the vessel had been wrapped in a thin layer of shimmering water. But when Broken sent out his flying golem to observe from a distance, the effect was truly astonishing-the ship appeared completely veiled by water, blending so seamlessly with the ocean that it was nearly invisible. "This is incredible," Broken muttered, his admiration growing with every detail.

Next, they tested the speed boost skill. When activated, Aego suddenly surged forward, racing across the water with startling speed. The sudden acceleration drew gasps and shouts of surprise from everyone onboard.

Finally, they turned their attention to the phasing skill. At first, they activated it without attempting to pass through anything. There wasn't any noticeable sensation-no jolts or shifts—but the ship's protective shield subtly changed color, signaling the skill's activation. Broken's earlier worry was put to rest when he realized the passengers weren't affected at all. To test further, they steered Aego toward a jagged rock jutting out of the water. Everyone held their breath, hearts pounding as the ship approached. And then-seamlessly, as if the obstacle wasn't even there-the ship phased through the rock without so much as a scratch.
"It worked! It really worked!" Mizuki shouted.
"Absolutely unbelievable!" Ronan added, his face lit up with pure joy.
There was still one more task Broken needed to handle. He called for Zepy, and the bird-like golem swiftly soared through the window into the control room, landing gracefully on his shoulder.
"Woah... what a cute bird..." Mizuki said, her face lighting up with excitement.
Without a word, Broken began making adjustments, setting Zepy's secondary command control to Mizuki.
The moment the transfer was complete, Mizuki froze, her expression mirroring Ronan's earlier shock.
"King..." she said, her voice trembling. "Are you really letting me control this bird?

"Yes," Broken replied casually. "Zepy is efficient for reconnaissance and has low energy consumption. With this, you and Ronan can divide tasks more effectively. I trust you'll do well as the ship's navigator."
"King..." Mizuki's voice wavered, and then, much to everyone's surprise, she burst into tears. "King, you're so kind! I'm so happy!"
"Stop it, Mizuki!" Ronan said, giving her a hearty pat on the back. "Now try it out! Let's see what the golem bird can actually do."
"H-Hiks!" Mizuki sniffled, wiping her tears before stepping closer to Broken. "Excuse me, King."
"Go ahead. Take it."
Carefully, Mizuki held Zepy in her hands, her eyes sparkling as she studied the golem's intricate design.
"The bird is so cute... Zepy... I love you so much!"
With a soft whir, Zepy lifted off and flew out of the control room. Mizuki quickly accessed its interface, sharing live visual footage from the golem's eyes.

"Damn! This is absolutely incredible. An autonomous golem!" Ronan said, visibly amazed. "Yes, and we can program so many different functions for it. This is beyond amazing!" Mizuki added, her enthusiasm spilling over as she navigated Zepy's controls with increasing ease. Afterward, Broken quietly observed as Ronan and Mizuki enthusiastically discussed various ways to optimize the use of the two golems. Their excitement was infectious, and it was clear they were eager and ready to begin their adventure across the ocean.
But that journey wouldn't start today. Not yet.
A few hours later, everyone gathered in the ship's central room. Broken stood at the front, his presence commanding attention as the crew assembled.

"In three days, Yunatea time, we'll embark on our first voyage to the West Continent," he announced, his voice steady and confident. "I trust that each of you knows what needs to be prepared. This will be our maiden voyage-a chance to test the ship's resilience on a relatively short journey."
The anticipation and determination in everyone's eyes told Broken everything he needed to know.
"Thank you for your enthusiasm!" he continued, a small smile breaking across his face. "Let's sail the world, Vensalor Outriders!"
The room erupted with a unified cheer:
"To the seas!"
